# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication. This API uses OAuth 2 with the implicit grant flow.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [/oauth2/v1/authorize](/oauth2/v1/authorize)
    - Token URL = [/oauth2/v1/token](/oauth2/v1/token)

* API Key (apiKeyAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **DD-API-KEY**, in: header. Your Datadog API Key.

* API Key (appKeyAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **DD-APPLICATION-KEY**, in: header. Your Datadog APP Key.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-api-management">API Management</h1>

Configure your API endpoints through the Datadog API.

## List APIs

<a id="opIdListAPIs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/apicatalog/api \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/apicatalog/api`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

List APIs and their IDs.

<h3 id="list-apis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Filter APIs by name|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of items per page.|
|page[offset]|query|integer(int64)|false|Offset for pagination.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "name": "Payments API"
      },
      "id": "abc-123"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 20,
      "offset": 0,
      "total_count": 1
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Missing required attribute in body",
      "meta": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "source": {
        "header": "Authorization",
        "parameter": "limit",
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/title"
      },
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Missing required attribute in body",
      "meta": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "source": {
        "header": "Authorization",
        "parameter": "limit",
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/title"
      },
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-apis-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ListAPIsResponse](#schemalistapisresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[JSONAPIErrorResponse](#schemajsonapierrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[JSONAPIErrorResponse](#schemajsonapierrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKeyAuth & appKeyAuth, AuthZ ( Scopes: apm_api_catalog_read )
</aside>

## Update an API

<a id="opIdUpdateOpenAPI"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/apicatalog/api/90646597-5fdb-4a17-a240-647003f8c028/openapi \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'openapi_spec_file=@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /api/v2/apicatalog/api/{id}/openapi`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Update information about a specific API. The given content will replace all API content of the given ID.
The ID is returned by the create API, or can be found in the URL in the API catalog UI.

> Body parameter

```yaml
openapi_spec_file: openapi-spec.yaml
```

<h3 id="update-an-api-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|[ApiID](#schemaapiid)|true|ID of the API to modify|
|body|body|[OpenAPIFile](#schemaopenapifile)|true|none|
|» openapi_spec_file|body|string(binary)|false|Binary `OpenAPI` spec file|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "failed_endpoints": []
    },

}
```

## Create a new API

<a id="opIdCreateOpenAPI"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/apicatalog/openapi \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'openapi_spec_file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /api/v2/apicatalog/openapi`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated

See the [API Catalog documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api_catalog/add_metadata/) for additional

## Get service list

<a id="opIdGetServiceList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/apm/services?filter%5Benv%5D=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/apm/services`

<h3 id="get-service-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[env]|query|string|true|Filter services by environment. Can be set to `*` to return all services across all environments.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "metadata": [
        {
          "isTraced": true,
          "isUsm": false

        "test-service"
      ]

    "id": "abc-123",
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-apm-retention-filters">APM Retention Filters</h1>

Manage configuration of [APM retention filters](https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces/retention-filters) for your organization. You need an API and application key with Admin rights to interact with this endpoint. See [retention filters](https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/trace_pipeline/trace_retention/#retention-filters) on the Trace Retention page for more information.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/trace_pipeline/trace_retention/">Find out more at</a>

## List all APM retention filters

<a id="opIdListApmRetentionFilters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/apm/config/retention-filters \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

## Create a retention filter

<a id="opIdCreateApmRetentionFilter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/apm/config/retention-filters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "enabled": true,
        "filter": {
          "query": "@http.status_code:200 service:my-service"
        },
        "filter_type": "spans-sampling-processor",
        "name": "my retention filter",
        "rate": 1,
        "trace_rate": 1
      },
      "type": "apm_retention_filter"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/apm/config/retention-filters`

Create a retention filter to index spans in your organization.
Returns the retention filter definition when the request is successful.

Default filters with types spans-errors-sampling-processor and spans-appsec-sampling-processor cannot be created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "enabled": true,
      "filter": {
        "query": "@http.status_code:200 service:my-service"
      },
      "filter_type": "spans-sampling-processor",
      "name": "my retention filter",
      "rate": 1,
      "trace_rate": 1
    },
    "type": "apm_retention_filter"
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» data|body|[RetentionFilterCreateData](#schemaretentionfiltercreatedata)|true|The body of the retention filter to be created.|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-apm-trace">APM Trace</h1>

Retrieve full or pruned APM traces by trace ID.

## Get a pruned trace by ID

<a id="opIdGetPrunedTraceByID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/pruned_trace/0000000000000000abc1230000000000 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/pruned_trace/{trace_id}`

Retrieve a pruned, hierarchical view of an APM trace by its trace ID.
The trace is summarized as a tree of spans rooted at the trace root and reduced in size
to keep rendering large traces in the UI practical.
A `400 Bad Request` response means the trace ID is malformed. A `404 Not Found` response means
no trace with this ID is available, such as when the trace is outside the retention period.
This endpoint is rate limited to `60` requests per minute per organization.

<h3 id="get-a-pruned-trace-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trace_id|path|string|true|The trace ID. Accepts either a hexadecimal string of up to 32 characters (128-bit trace ID)<br>or a decimal string of up to 39 digits. Hexadecimal IDs are case-insensitive, and shorter<br>values are left-padded with zeros.<br>Use the `trace_id` attribute of a span returned by the Search spans or Get a list of spans endpoints.<br>Values in any other format, such as UUIDs, return `400 Bad Request`. A well-formed ID with<br>no matching trace returns `404 Not Found`.|
|expand_span_id|query|integer(int64)|false|Span ID to expand and preserve in the pruned tree even when its branch would<br>normally be summarized.|
|time_hint|query|integer(int32)|false|Optional Unix time hint, in seconds, used to optimize the lookup of the trace<br>in long-term storage.|
|force_source|query|string|false|Force the trace to be loaded from a specific source. When unset, the API picks<br>the source automatically.|
|include_path|query|[string]|false|Restrict the pruned tree to spans matching the given `key:value` pairs.<br>Values may be passed as repeated query parameters.|
|tag_include|query|[string]|false|Regex patterns of tag keys whose values must be included in the pruned spans.<br>Values may be passed as repeated query parameters.|
|tag_exclude|query|[string]|false|Regex patterns of tag keys whose values must be excluded from the pruned spans.<br>Values may be passed as repeated query parameters.|
|only_service_entry_spans|query|boolean|false|When set to `true`, only service entry spans are included in the pruned tree.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "is_truncated": false,
      "size_bytes": 12345,
      "summarized_trace": {
        "root": {
          "children": [],
          "durationSeconds": 0.5,
          "endTime": "2026-05-27T12:00:00.5Z",
          "error": 0,
          "hidden_child_spans_count": 0,
          "meta": {
            "env": "production"
          },
          "metrics": {
            "http.status_code": 200
          },
          "name": "web.request",
          "parentID": 0,
          "resource": "GET /products",
          "service": "web-store",
          "spanID": 9876543210987655000,
          "span_kind": "SERVER",
          "startTime": "2026-05-27T12:00:00Z"
        },
        "traceId": "0000000000000000abc1230000000000"
      }
    },
    "id": "0000000000000000abc1230000000000",
    "type": "pruned_trace"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Missing required attribute in body",
      "meta": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "source": {
        "header": "Authorization",
        "parameter": "limit",
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/title"
      },
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
```

> 403 Response

## Get a trace by ID

<a id="opIdGetTraceByID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/trace/0000000000000000abc1230000000000 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/trace/{trace_id}`

Retrieve a full APM trace by its trace ID, including every span in the trace.
Traces are returned from live storage when available and fall back to longer-term storage.
A `400 Bad Request` response means the trace ID is malformed. A `404 Not Found` response means
no trace with this ID is available, such as when the trace is outside the retention period.
This endpoint is rate limited to `60` requests per minute per organization.

<h3 id="get-a-trace-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trace_id|path|string|true|The trace ID. Accepts either a hexadecimal string of up to 32 characters (128-bit trace ID)<br>or a decimal string of up to 39 digits. Hexadecimal IDs are case-insensitive, and shorter<br>values are left-padded with zeros.<br>Use the `trace_id` attribute of a span returned by the Search spans or Get a list of spans endpoints.<br>Values in any other format, such as UUIDs, return `400 Bad Request`. A well-formed ID with<br>no matching trace returns `404 Not Found`.|
|include_fields|query|[string]|false|List of span fields to include in the response. When omitted, every available field is returned.<br>Values may be passed as repeated query parameters or as a single comma-separated value.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "is_truncated": false,
      "spans": [
        {
          "duration": 500000000,
          "endTime": 1716800000500000000,
          "error": 0,
          "meta": {
            "env": "production",
            "http.method": "GET"
          },
          "metrics": {
            "http.status_code": 200
          },
          "name": "web.request",
          "parentID": 0,
          "resource": "GET /products",
          "service": "web-store",
          "spanID": 9876543210987655000,
          "startTime": 1716800000000000000,
          "traceID": 12345678901234567000,
          "traceIDFull": "0000000000000000abc1230000000000",
          "type": "web"
        }
      ]
    },
    "id": "0000000000000000abc1230000000000",
    "type": "trace"
  }
}
```

## Create an AWS integration

<a id="opIdCreateAWSAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/integration/aws/accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "account_tags": [
          "env:prod"
        ],
        "auth_config": {
          "access_key_id": "ACCESS_KEY_ID",
          "secret_access_key": "SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
        },
        "aws_account_id": "123456789012",
        "aws_partition": "aws",
        "aws_regions": {
          "include_all": true
        },
        "logs_config": {
          "lambda_forwarder": {
            "lambdas": [
              "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:DatadogLambdaLogForwarder"
            ],
            "sources": [
              "s3"
            ]
          }
        },
        "metrics_config": {
          "automute_enabled": true,
          "collect_cloudwatch_alarms": false,
          "collect_custom_metrics": false,
          "collect_service_quotas": false,
          "enabled": true,
          "metric_name_filters": [
            {
              "include_only": [
                "aws.ec2.network_in"
              ],
              "namespace": "AWS/EC2"
            }
          ],
          "tag_filters": [
            {
              "namespace": "AWS/EC2"
            }
          ]
        },
        "resources_config": {
          "cloud_security_posture_management_collection": false,
          "extended_collection": true
        }
      },
      "type": "account"
    }
  }'
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-action-connection">Action Connection</h1>

Action connections extend your installed integrations and allow you to take action in your third-party systems
(e.g. AWS, GitLab, and Statuspage) with Datadog’s Workflow Automation and App Builder products.

Datadog’s Integrations automatically provide authentication for Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Opsgenie,
JIRA, GitHub, and Statuspage. You do not need additional connections in order to access these tools within
Workflow Automation and App Builder.

We offer granular access control for editing and resolving connections.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/service_management/workflows/connections/">Find out more at</a>

## List datastore items

<a id="opIdListDatastoreItems"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/actions-datastores/string/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/actions-datastores/{datastore_id}/items`

Lists items from a datastore. You can filter the results by specifying either an item key or a filter query parameter, but not both at the same time. Supports server-side pagination for large datasets.

<h3 id="list-datastore-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datastore_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the datastore to retrieve.|
|filter|query|string|false|Optional query filter to search items using the [logs search syntax](https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/explorer/search_syntax/).|
|item_key|query|string|false|Optional primary key value to retrieve a specific item. Cannot be used together with the filter parameter.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Optional field to limit the number of items to return per page for pagination. Up to 100 items can be returned per page.|
|page[offset]|query|integer(int64)|false|Optional field to offset the number of items to skip from the beginning of the result set for pagination.|
|sort|query|string|false|Optional field to sort results by. Prefix with '-' for descending order (e.g., '-created_at').|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {

        "org_id": 123,
```

`GET /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotated-interactions`

## Create an Agent Observability annotation queue

<a id="opIdCreateLLMObsAnnotationQueue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "description": "Queue for annotating customer support traces",
        "name": "My annotation queue",
        "project_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
      },
      "type": "queues"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues`

Create an annotation queue. The `name` and `project_id` fields are required.
An optional `annotation_schema` can be provided to define the labels for the queue.
Optional access-control fields can restrict annotation access to reviewers or assignees.
Fields such as `created_by`, `owned_by`, `created_at`, `modified_by`,
and `modified_at` are inferred by the backend.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "description": "Queue for annotating customer support traces",
      "name": "My annotation queue",
      "project_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
    },
    "type": "queues"
  }
}
```

## Create or update annotations

<a id="opIdUpsertLLMObsAnnotations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/annotations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "annotations": [
          {
            "interaction_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
            "label_values": [
              {
                "label_schema_id": "abc-123",
                "value": "good"
              },
              {
                "label_schema_id": "ef56gh78",
                "value": "positive"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "type": "annotations"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues/{queue_id}/annotations`

Create or update annotations on interactions in a queue. Each annotation is matched
by `interaction_id` and the requesting user's identity.
Results and errors in the response are linked to request items by `interaction_id`.
Errors for individual items are returned in the `errors` field without blocking the rest of the batch.
Requests where every item is denied by queue access rules return `403`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "annotations": [
        {
          "interaction_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
          "label_values": [
            {
              "label_schema_id": "abc-123",
              "value": "good"
            },
            {
              "label_schema_id": "ef56gh78",
              "value": "positive"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "annotations"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-annotations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability annotation queue.|
|body|body|[LLMObsAnnotationsRequest](#schemallmobsannotationsrequest)|true|Payload for creating or updating annotations.|
|» data|body|[LLMObsAnnotationsDataRequest](#schemallmobsannotationsdatarequest)|true|Data object for creating or updating annotations.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "annotations": [
        {
          "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",

          "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
          "interaction_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
          "label_values": [
            {
              "label_schema_id": "abc-123",
              "value": "good"
            }
          ],
          "modified_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
          "modified_by": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
        }
      ]
    },
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",

  }
}
```

## Add annotation queue interactions

<a id="opIdCreateLLMObsAnnotationQueueInteractions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/interactions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "interactions": [
          {
            "content_id": "trace-abc-123",
            "type": "trace"
          }
        ]
      },
      "type": "interactions"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues/{queue_id}/interactions`

Add one or more interactions to an annotation queue. At least one
interaction must be provided. Each interaction has a `type`:

- `trace`, `experiment_trace`, `session`: `content_id` references the
  upstream entity; the server fetches the actual content.
- `display_block`: omit `content_id` and provide the rendered content
  in `display_block`. The server generates `content_id` as a
  deterministic hash of the block list.

Items of different types can be mixed in a single request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "interactions": [
        {
          "content_id": "trace-abc-123",
          "type": "trace"
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "interactions"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-annotation-queue-interactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability annotation queue.|
|body|body|[LLMObsAnnotationQueueInteractionsRequest](#schemallmobsannotationqueueinteractionsrequest)|true|Add interactions payload.|
|» data|body|[LLMObsAnnotationQueueInteractionsDataRequest](#schemallmobsannotationqueueinteractionsdatarequest)|true|Data object for adding interactions to an annotation queue.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "data": {

          "already_existed": false,
          "content_id": "trace-abc-123",

          "type": "trace"
        }
      ]
    },
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "type": "interactions"
  }
}
```

## Update annotation queue label schema

<a id="opIdUpdateLLMObsAnnotationQueueLabelSchema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/label-schema \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "annotation_schema": {
          "label_schemas": [
            {
              "has_assessment": true,
              "is_assessment": true,
              "is_required": true,
              "name": "is_correct",
              "type": "boolean"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "queues"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/annotation-queues/{queue_id}/label-schema`

Create or replace the label schema for a given annotation queue.
The label schema defines the labels annotators can apply to interactions in the queue.
Label names must be unique within the queue and match the pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`.
Each label must have a valid type: score, categorical, boolean, or text.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "annotation_schema": {
        "label_schemas": [
          {
            "has_assessment": true,
            "is_assessment": true,
            "is_required": true,
            "name": "is_correct",
            "type": "boolean"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "type": "queues"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-annotation-queue-label-schema-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability annotation queue.|

## Aggregate Agent Observability experimentation

<a id="opIdAggregateLLMObsExperimentation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experimentation/analytics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "aggregate": {
          "compute": [
            {
              "metric": "score_value",
              "name": "avg_faithfulness"
            }
          ],
          "group_by": [
            {
              "field": "span_id"
            }
          ],
          "indexes": [
            "experiment-evals"
          ],
          "search": {
            "query": "@experiment_id:3fd6b5e0-8910-4b1c-a7d0-5b84de329012 @label:faithfulness"
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "experimentation"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experimentation/analytics`

Execute an analytics aggregation over Agent Observability experimentation data.
Use this endpoint to compute metrics (for example average eval scores) grouped by fields such as `span_id` or `experiment_id`.

At least one `compute` definition and one `index` must be provided.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "aggregate": {
        "compute": [
          {
            "metric": "score_value",
            "name": "avg_faithfulness"
          }
        ],
        "group_by": [
          {
            "field": "span_id"
          }
        ],
        "indexes": [
          "experiment-evals"
        ],
        "search": {
          "query": "@experiment_id:3fd6b5e0-8910-4b1c-a7d0-5b84de329012 @label:faithfulness"
        }
      }
    },
    "type": "experimentation"
  }
}
```

## Search Agent Observability experimentation

<a id="opIdSearchLLMObsExperimentation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experimentation/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "filter": {
          "query": "@project_id:a33671aa-24fd-4dcd-9b33-a8ec7dde7751",
          "scope": [
            "experiments"
          ]
        },
        "page": {
          "limit": 50
        }
      },
      "type": "experimentation"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experimentation/search`

Search across Agent Observability experimentation entities — projects, datasets, dataset records, experiments, and experiment runs — using cursor-based pagination.

The `filter.scope` field controls which entity types are returned. At least one valid scope must be provided.

Returns `200 OK` when all results fit in a single page. Returns `206 Partial Content` with a cursor in `meta.after` when additional pages are available.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "filter": {
        "query": "@project_id:a33671aa-24fd-4dcd-9b33-a8ec7dde7751",
        "scope": [
          "experiments"
        ]
      },
      "page": {
        "limit": 50
      }
    },
    "type": "experimentation"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="search-agent-observability-experimentation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LLMObsExperimentationSearchRequest](#schemallmobsexperimentationsearchrequest)|true|Experimentation search payload.|
|» data|body|[LLMObsExperimentationSearchDataRequest](#schemallmobsexperimentationsearchdatarequest)|true|Data object for an experimentation search request.|

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experimentation/simple-search`

Search across Agent Observability experimentation entities using offset-based (page-number) pagination.
Use this endpoint when you need total page count or want to navigate to a specific page number.

The `filter.scope` field controls which entity types are returned. At least one valid scope must be provided.

```json
{
  "data": {

          "experiments"
        ]
      },
      "page": {
        "limit": 50,
        "number": 1
      },
      "sort": [

}
```

## List Agent Observability experiments

<a id="opIdListLLMObsExperiments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experiments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/experiments`

List all Agent Observability experiments sorted by creation date, newest first.

<h3 id="list-agent-observability-experiments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[project_id]|query|string|false|Filter experiments by project ID. Required if `filter[dataset_id]` is not provided.|
|filter[dataset_id]|query|string|false|Filter experiments by dataset ID.|
|filter[id]|query|string|false|Filter experiments by experiment ID. Can be specified multiple times.|
|filter[name]|query|string|false|Filter experiments by their exact run name.|
|filter[experiment]|query|string|false|Filter by logical experiment name. This is the `name` field set when creating an experiment through `POST /experiments`. Returns all experiment runs that share the same name, enabling cross-commit and cross-branch comparisons.|
|filter[metadata]|query|string|false|Filter by JSONB metadata containment. Provide a JSON object string where<br>experiments whose metadata contains all specified key-value pairs are returned.<br>For example: `{"commit":"abc123","branch":"main"}`.|
|filter[parent_experiment_id]|query|string|false|Filter experiments by the ID of their parent (baseline) experiment. Returns all experiments that were run against the given baseline. Can be specified multiple times.|
|filter[is_deleted]|query|boolean|false|When `true`, return only soft-deleted experiments. Defaults to `false`.|
|include[user_data]|query|boolean|false|When `true`, enrich each experiment with its author's user data in the `author` field.|
|include[dataset_names]|query|boolean|false|When `true`, enrich each experiment with its dataset name in the `dataset_name` field.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Use the pagination cursor returned in `meta.after` to retrieve the next page of results.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of results to return per page. Values above 5000 are clamped<br>to 5000. Defaults to 5000.|

> Example responses

## Run an LLM inference

<a id="opIdCreateLLMObsIntegrationInference"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/integrations/openai/account-abc123/inference \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "messages": [
      {
        "content": "What is the capital of France?",
        "role": "user"
      }
    ],
    "model_id": "gpt-4o",
    "temperature": 0.7
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/integrations/{integration}/{account_id}/inference`

Run an LLM inference request through the specified integration and account, returning the model response and token usage.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "messages": [
    {
      "content": "What is the capital of France?",
      "role": "user"
    }
  ],
  "model_id": "gpt-4o",
  "temperature": 0.7
}
```

<h3 id="run-an-llm-inference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|integration|path|[LLMObsIntegrationName](#schemallmobsintegrationname)|true|The name of the LLM integration.|
|account_id|path|string|true|The ID of the integration account.|
|body|body|[LLMObsIntegrationInferenceRequest](#schemallmobsintegrationinferencerequest)|true|Inference request parameters.|
|» anthropic_metadata|body|[LLMObsAnthropicMetadata](#schemallmobsanthropicmetadata)|false|Anthropic-specific metadata for an inference request.|
|» azure_openai_metadata|body|[LLMObsAzureOpenAIMetadata](#schemallmobsazureopenaimetadata)|false|Azure OpenAI-specific metadata for an integration account or inference request.|
|» bedrock_metadata|body|[LLMObsBedrockMetadata](#schemallmobsbedrockmetadata)|false|Amazon Bedrock-specific metadata for an inference request.|
|» frequency_penalty|body|number(double) \| null|false|Penalty for token frequency to reduce repetition.|
|» json_schema|body|string \| null|false|JSON schema for structured output, if supported by the model.|
|» max_completion_tokens|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of completion tokens to generate (alternative to max_tokens for some providers).|
|» max_tokens|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of tokens to generate.|
|» messages|body|[LLMObsInferenceMessagesList](#schemallmobsinferencemessageslist)|true|List of messages in an inference conversation.|
|» model_id|body|string|true|The model identifier to use for inference.|
|» openai_metadata|body|[LLMObsOpenAIMetadata](#schemallmobsopenaimetadata)|false|OpenAI-specific metadata for an inference request.|
|» presence_penalty|body|number(double) \| null|false|Penalty for token presence to encourage topic diversity.|
|» temperature|body|number(double) \| null|false|Sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Higher values produce more random output.|
|» tools|body|[LLMObsInferenceToolsList](#schemallmobsinferencetoolslist)|false|List of tools available to the model.|
|» top_k|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Top-K sampling parameter.|
|» top_p|body|number(double) \| null|false|Nucleus sampling probability mass.|
|» vertex_ai_metadata|body|[LLMObsVertexAIMetadata](#schemallmobsvertexaimetadata)|false|Vertex AI-specific metadata for an integration account or inference request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|integration|openai|
|integration|amazon_bedrock|
|integration|anthropic|
|integration|azure_openai|
|integration|vertex_ai|
|integration|llmproxy|

## Create an Agent Observability prompt

<a id="opIdCreateLLMObsPrompt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/prompts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "config": {
          "model": "provider-model",
          "response_format": {
            "type": "json_object"
          },
          "temperature": 0.2
        },
        "description": "Answers customer questions using the company knowledge base.",
        "prompt_id": "customer-support-assistant",
        "template": [
          {
            "content": "You are a helpful customer support assistant for {{company_name}}.",
            "role": "system"
          },
          {
            "content": "Help {{customer_name}} with this question: {{question}}",
            "role": "user"
          }
        ],
        "title": "Customer Support Assistant"
      },
      "type": "prompt-templates"
    }
  }'
```

<h3 id="get-an-agent-observability-prompt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prompt_id|path|string|true|The customer-provided identifier of the Agent Observability prompt.|
|label|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Optional label of the prompt version to return. Do not use this parameter for new integrations. If omitted, the latest version is returned. If the prompt has no labels, the latest version is returned even when a label is requested. If the prompt has labels but none match the requested label, a 404 response is returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "chat_template": [
        {
          "content": "You are a helpful customer support assistant for {{company_name}}.",
          "role": "system"
        },
        {
          "content": "Help {{customer_name}} with this question: {{question}}",
          "role": "user"
        }
      ],
      "config": {
        "model": "provider-model",
        "temperature": 0.2
      },
      "prompt_id": "customer-support-assistant",
      "prompt_version_uuid": "d83ab666-61cc-5545-a83b-2424bb85467b",
      "version": "2"
    },
    "id": "4a1a28ff-8a25-5f0f-946f-f48264d772eb",
    "type": "prompt-templates"
  }
}
```

## Update an Agent Observability prompt

<a id="opIdUpdateLLMObsPrompt"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

## Create a new Agent Observability prompt version

<a id="opIdCreateLLMObsPromptVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/prompts/customer-support-assistant/versions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "template": {
          "messages": [
            {
              "include": {
                "prompt_id": "assistant-introduction",
                "version": 2
              }
            },
            {
              "include": {
                "items": [
                  2,
                  0,
                  0
                ],
                "prompt_id": "response-examples",
                "version": 4
              }
            },
            {
              "content": "Answer {{question}}.",
              "role": "user"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "prompt-template-versions"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/versions`

## List Agent Observability spans

<a id="opIdListLLMObsSpans"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/spans/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/spans/events`

List Agent Observability spans matching the specified filters.

<h3 id="list-agent-observability-spans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[from]|query|string|false|Start of the time range. Accepts ISO 8601 or relative format (e.g., `now-15m`). Defaults to `now-15m`.|
|filter[to]|query|string|false|End of the time range. Accepts ISO 8601 or relative format. Defaults to `now`.|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|Search query using Agent Observability query syntax. Supports attribute filters using the field:value syntax (e.g. session_id, trace_id, ml_app, meta.span.kind). When provided, structured field filters (`filter[span_id]`, `filter[trace_id]`, etc.) are ignored.|
|filter[span_id]|query|string|false|Filter by exact span ID.|
|filter[trace_id]|query|string|false|Filter by exact trace ID.|
|filter[span_kind]|query|string|false|Filter by span kind (e.g., llm, agent, tool, task, workflow).|
|filter[span_name]|query|string|false|Filter by span name.|
|filter[ml_app]|query|string|false|Filter by ML application name.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of spans to return. Defaults to `10`.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Cursor from the previous response to retrieve the next page.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort order for the results.|
|include_attachments|query|boolean|false|Whether to include attachment data in the response. Defaults to `true`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "duration": 1500000000,
        "ml_app": "my-llm-app",

        "name": "llm_call",

    }

}
```

## Batch update Agent Observability dataset records

<a id="opIdBatchUpdateLLMObsDataset"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/a33671aa-24fd-4dcd-9b33-a8ec7dde7751/datasets/9f64e5c7-dc5a-45c8-a17c-1b85f0bec97d/batch_update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "create_new_version": true,
        "delete_records": [
          "rec-old-record-1"
        ],
        "insert_records": [
          {
            "expected_output": {
              "answer": "Paris"
            },
            "input": {
              "question": "What is the capital of France?"
            },
            "tags": [
              "topic:geography"
            ]
          }
        ],
        "update_records": [
          {
            "expected_output": {
              "answer": "Paris, France"
            },
            "id": "rec-7c3f5a1b-9e2d-4f8a-b1c6-3d7e9f0a2b4c"
          }
        ]
      },
      "id": "9f64e5c7-dc5a-45c8-a17c-1b85f0bec97d",
      "type": "datasets"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/{project_id}/datasets/{dataset_id}/batch_update`

Insert, update, and delete records in a single dataset operation. By default, a new dataset version is created when the batch is applied.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "create_new_version": true,
      "delete_records": [
        "rec-old-record-1"
      ],
      "insert_records": [
        {
          "expected_output": {
            "answer": "Paris"
          },
          "input": {
            "question": "What is the capital of France?"
          },
          "tags": [
            "topic:geography"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "update_records": [
        {
          "expected_output": {
            "answer": "Paris, France"
          },
          "id": "rec-7c3f5a1b-9e2d-4f8a-b1c6-3d7e9f0a2b4c"
        }
      ]
    },
    "id": "9f64e5c7-dc5a-45c8-a17c-1b85f0bec97d",
    "type": "datasets"
  }
}
```

`GET /api/v2/llm-obs/v1/{project_id}/datasets/{dataset_id}/export`

Download the contents of a dataset as a CSV file. The download is streamed and includes one row per dataset record.

<h3 id="export-an-agent-observability-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability project.|
|dataset_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability dataset.|
|format|query|[LLMObsDatasetExportFormat](#schemallmobsdatasetexportformat)|false|Export format for the dataset contents. Only `csv` is currently supported.|
|version|query|integer(int64)|false|Version of the dataset to export. If omitted, the current version is used. Must be between 0 and the current version of the dataset, inclusive.|

## Upload records to an Agent Observability dataset

<a id="opIdUploadLLMObsDatasetRecordsFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/llm-obs/v2/a33671aa-24fd-4dcd-9b33-a8ec7dde7751/datasets/9f64e5c7-dc5a-45c8-a17c-1b85f0bec97d/records/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /api/v2/llm-obs/v2/{project_id}/datasets/{dataset_id}/records/upload`

Upload records to a dataset from a file. The request is a `multipart/form-data` upload containing a single `file` part.
Currently only CSV is supported. The CSV must include an `input` column. Optional columns are `id`, `expected_output`, `metadata`, and `tags`.

The response is a Server-Sent Events stream (`text/event-stream`) emitting progress updates while records are processed. The stream emits the following named events:
  - `progress`: incremental record counts written so far.
  - `completed`: terminal event with a JSON body containing `records_created`.
  - `error`: terminal event with a JSON body containing an error `message`.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: records.csv
```

<h3 id="upload-records-to-an-agent-observability-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability project.|
|dataset_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Agent Observability dataset.|
|deduplicate|query|boolean|false|Whether to skip records whose `input` already exists in the dataset. Defaults to `false`.|
|overwrite|query|boolean|false|Whether to overwrite existing records that share the same user-provided `id`. Defaults to `true`.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|Tags to apply to every uploaded record, in addition to any tags defined on individual rows. Can be repeated, e.g. `tags=env:prod&tags=team:ai`.|
|include[user_data]|query|boolean|false|Whether to enrich the response with user metadata.|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-agentless-scanning">Agentless Scanning</h1>

Datadog Agentless Scanning provides visibility into risks and vulnerabilities
within your hosts, running containers, and serverless functions—all without
requiring teams to install Agents on every host or where Agents cannot be installed.
Agentless offers also Sensitive Data Scanning capabilities on your storage.
Go to https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/agentless-scanning/ to learn more.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-annotations">Annotations</h1>

Add annotations to dashboards and notebooks to mark events such as deployments, incidents, or other notable moments in time.

## List annotations

<a id="opIdListAnnotations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/annotation?page_id=dashboard%3Aabc-def-xyz&start_time=1704067200000&end_time=1704153600000' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/annotation`

Returns a flat list of annotations matching the given page, time window, and optional widget filter.

<h3 id="list-annotations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_id|query|string|true|ID of the page to list annotations for, prefixed with the page type and joined by a colon<br>(for example, `dashboard:abc-def-xyz` or `notebook:1234567890`).|
|start_time|query|integer(int64)|true|Start of the time window in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.|
|end_time|query|integer(int64)|true|End of the time window in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.|
|widget_id|query|string|false|Optional widget ID to restrict results to annotations on a specific widget.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "author_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
        "color": "blue",
        "created_at": 1704067200000,
        "description": "Deployed v2.3.1 to production.",
        "end_time": null,
        "modified_at": 1704067200000,
        "page_id": "dashboard:abc-def-xyz",
        "start_time": 1704067200000,
        "type": "pointInTime",
        "widget_ids": [
          "1234567890"
        ]
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
      "type": "annotation"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Missing required attribute in body",
      "meta": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "source": {
        "header": "Authorization",
        "parameter": "limit",
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/title"
      },
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get annotations for a page

<a id="opIdGetPageAnnotations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/annotation/page/dashboard%3Aabc-def-xyz?start_time=1704067200000&end_time=1704153600000' \

  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/annotation/page/{page_id}`

Returns all annotations on a specific page for a given time window, grouped by widget.
Unlike `ListAnnotations`, this endpoint returns a single structured object with annotations
indexed by their ID and a widget-to-annotation mapping for easy UI rendering.

<h3 id="get-annotations-for-a-page-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_id|path|string|true|The ID of the page, prefixed with the page type and joined by a colon<br>(for example, `dashboard:abc-def-xyz` or `notebook:1234567890`).|
|start_time|query|integer(int64)|true|Start of the time window in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.|
|end_time|query|integer(int64)|true|End of the time window in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-app-builder">App Builder</h1>

Datadog App Builder provides a low-code solution to rapidly develop and integrate secure, customized applications into your monitoring stack that are built to accelerate remediation at scale. These API endpoints allow you to create, read, update, delete, and publish apps.

## List Apps

<a id="opIdListApps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/app-builder/apps \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/app-builder/apps`

List all apps, with optional filters and sorting. This endpoint is paginated. Only basic app information such as the app ID, name, and description is returned by this endpoint. This API requires a [registered application key](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/action-connection/#register-a-new-app-key). Alternatively, you can configure these permissions [in the UI](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/api-app-keys/#actions-api-access).

<h3 id="list-apps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of apps to return per page.|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|The page number to return.|
|filter[user_name]|query|string|false|Filter apps by the app creator. Usually the user's email.|
|filter[user_uuid]|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter apps by the app creator's UUID.|
|filter[name]|query|string|false|Filter by app name.|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|Filter apps by the app name or the app creator.|
|filter[deployed]|query|boolean|false|Filter apps by whether they are published.|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Filter apps by tags.|
|filter[favorite]|query|boolean|false|Filter apps by whether you have added them to your favorites.|
|filter[self_service]|query|boolean|false|Filter apps by whether they are enabled for self-service.|
|sort|query|[[AppsSortField](#schemaappssortfield)]|false|The fields and direction to sort apps by.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|name|
|sort|created_at|
|sort|updated_at|
|sort|user_name|
|sort|-name|
|sort|-created_at|
|sort|-updated_at|
|sort|-user_name|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "description": "A sample app",

        ]
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",

}
```

## Unpublish App

<a id="opIdUnpublishApp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/app-builder/apps/{app_id}/deployment`

Unpublish an app, removing the live version of the app. Unpublishing creates a new instance of a `deployment` object on the app, with a nil `app_version_id` (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`). The app can still be updated and published again in the future. This API requires a [registered application key](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/action-connection/#register-a-new-app-key). Alternatively, you can configure these permissions [in the UI](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/api-app-keys/#actions-api-access).

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-application-security">Application Security</h1>

[Datadog Application Security](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/application_security/) provides protection against
application-level attacks that aim to exploit code-level vulnerabilities,
such as Server-Side-Request-Forgery (SSRF), SQL injection, Log4Shell, and
Reflected Cross-Site-Scripting (XSS). You can monitor and protect apps
hosted directly on a server, Docker, Kubernetes, Amazon ECS, and (for
supported languages) AWS Fargate.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/application_security/">Find out more at</a>

## Create a WAF custom rule

<a id="opIdCreateApplicationSecurityWafCustomRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/remote_config/products/asm/waf/custom_rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "action": {
          "action": "block_request",
          "parameters": {
            "location": "/blocking",
            "status_code": 403
          }
        },
        "blocking": false,
        "conditions": [
          {
            "operator": "match_regex",
            "parameters": {
              "data": "blocked_users",
              "regex": "path.*",
              "value": "custom_tag"
            }
          }
        ],
        "enabled": false,
        "name": "Block request from a bad useragent",
        "path_glob": "/api/search/*",
        "scope": [
          {
            "env": "prod",
            "service": "billing-service"
          }
        ],
        "tags": {
          "category": "business_logic",
          "type": "users.login.success"
        }
      },
      "type": "custom_rule"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/remote_config/products/asm/waf/custom_rules`

## Search Audit Logs events

<a id="opIdSearchAuditLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/audit/events/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "from": "now-15m",
      "query": "@type:session AND @session.type:user",
      "to": "now"
    },
    "options": {
      "timezone": "GMT"
    },
    "page": {
      "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
      "limit": 25
    },
    "sort": "timestamp"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/audit/events/search`

List endpoint returns Audit Logs events that match an Audit search query.
[Results are paginated][1].

Use this endpoint to build complex Audit Logs events filtering and search.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "from": "now-15m",
    "query": "@type:session AND @session.type:user",
    "to": "now"
  },
  "options": {
    "timezone": "GMT"
  },
  "page": {
    "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
    "limit": 25
  },
  "sort": "timestamp"
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-authn-mappings">AuthN Mappings</h1>

[The AuthN Mappings API](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/authn_mapping/?tab=example)
is used to automatically map groups of users to roles in Datadog using attributes
sent from Identity Providers. Use these endpoints to manage your AuthN Mappings.

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/authn_mappings \
```

## Update GitHub CI Visibility status

<a id="opIdUpdateCIAppGitHubAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/ci/github/accounts \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \

  -d '{

        "enabled": true,
        "host": "github.com",
        "repository": {
          "enabled": true,
          "name": "shopist"
        }
      },
      "type": "ci_github_account"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/ci/github/accounts`

Enable or disable CI Visibility for a GitHub account, one of its repositories, or both in the same request.
The account (and, optionally, repository) are identified by name. Account-level and repository-level
changes are independent and may both be supplied in the same request. At least one of `enabled` or
`repository.enabled` must be provided. If the account name matches installations on more than one host,
`host` must be supplied to disambiguate, otherwise a 409 is returned. Returns a 404 if the CI Visibility
GitHub integration is not enabled for this organization, or if the given account or repository cannot be
found by name.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "account": "datadog",
      "enabled": true,
      "host": "github.com",
      "repository": {
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "shopist"
      }
    },
    "type": "ci_github_account"
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CIAppGitHubAccountUpdateRequest](#schemaciappgithubaccountupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[CIAppGitHubAccountUpdateRequestData](#schemaciappgithubaccountupdaterequestdata)|true|Data object for updating a GitHub account's CI Visibility opt-in status.|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-ci-visibility-logs">CI Visibility Logs</h1>

Send CI job logs over HTTP for CI Visibility.

## Send CI job logs

<a id="opIdSubmitCILog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cilogs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "ddtags": "runner:linux,architecture:amd64",
      "job_id": "job-456",
      "line_number": 812,
      "message": "Running go test ./...",
      "pipeline_unique_id": "3eacb6f3-ff04-4e10-8a9c-46e6d054024a",
      "provider_name": "example-provider",
      "section_name": "tests",
      "status": "warn",
      "stream": "stdout"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /api/v2/cilogs`

Send log lines for a CI job over HTTP. See the [CI Visibility Pipelines
API](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/ci-visibility-pipelines/send-pipeline-event/) for submitting the
associated pipeline and job events.

A request can contain one log object or an array of up to 1,000 log objects. The maximum uncompressed request
body size is 5.1 MiB.

You can stream log lines while a CI job runs or send them after it finishes. After you submit the completed job
event, 20 seconds without a new log line marks the job's logs as complete. Lines sent after that may not appear.

A job can have up to 128 additional attributes and 256 tags. Additional attributes are top-level fields with
string, number, Boolean, or null values. Nested objects and arrays are rejected. Additional attributes and
`ddtags` apply to all log lines in the job. If an additional attribute has different values on different lines,
the first value received is used. Tags supplied on different lines are combined. A job can contain up to
2,000,000 log records or 1 GiB of message bytes in total.

To reduce request size, send gzip-compressed JSON with the `Content-Encoding: gzip` header. Retry requests after
a 408, 429, 500, or 503 response.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "ddtags": "runner:linux,architecture:amd64",
    "job_id": "job-456",
    "line_number": 812,
    "message": "Running go test ./...",
    "pipeline_unique_id": "3eacb6f3-ff04-4e10-8a9c-46e6d054024a",
    "provider_name": "example-provider",
    "section_name": "tests",
    "status": "warn",
    "stream": "stdout"
  }
]
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|header|[CILogContentEncoding](#schemacilogcontentencoding)|false|HTTP header used to compress the JSON request body.|
|body|body|[CILogRequest](#schemacilogrequest)|true|CI job log line or batch in JSON format.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|identity|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-ci-visibility-pipelines">CI Visibility Pipelines</h1>

Search or aggregate your CI Visibility pipeline events and send them to your Datadog site over HTTP. See the [CI Pipeline Visibility in Datadog page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/continuous_integration/pipelines/) for more information.

## Send pipeline event

<a id="opIdCreateCIAppPipelineEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/ci/pipeline \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "resource": {
          "end": "2024-11-25T20:08:11.018Z",
          "git": {
            "author_email": "john.doe@email.com",
            "repository_url": "https://github.com/organization/example-repository",
            "sha": "7f263865994b76066c4612fd1965215e7dcb4cd2"
          },
          "level": "pipeline",
          "name": "Deploy to AWS",
          "partial_retry": false,
          "start": "2024-11-25T20:06:41.018Z",
          "status": "success",
          "unique_id": "3eacb6f3-ff04-4e10-8a9c-46e6d054024a",
          "url": "https://my-ci-provider.example/pipelines/my-pipeline/run/1"
        }
      },
      "type": "cipipeline_resource_request"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/ci/pipeline`

Send your pipeline event to your Datadog platform over HTTP. For details about how pipeline executions are modeled and what execution types we support, see [Pipeline Data Model And Execution Types](https://docs.datadoghq.com/continuous_integration/guides/pipeline_data_model/).

Multiple events can be sent in an array (up to 1000).

Pipeline events can be submitted with a timestamp that is up to 18 hours in the past.
The duration between the event start and end times cannot exceed 1 year.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {

      }
    },
    "type": "cipipeline_resource_request"
  }
}
```

## Aggregate pipelines events

<a id="opIdAggregateCIAppPipelineEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/ci/pipelines/analytics/aggregate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "compute": [
      {
        "aggregation": "pc90",
        "interval": "5m",
        "metric": "@duration",
        "type": "timeseries"
      }
    ],
    "filter": {
      "from": "now-15m",
      "query": "@ci.provider.name:github AND @ci.status:error",
      "to": "now"
    },
    "group_by": [
      {
        "facet": "@ci.status",
        "histogram": {
          "interval": 10,
          "max": 100,
          "min": 50
        },
        "sort": {
          "aggregation": "count",
          "order": "asc"
        }
      }
    ],
    "options": {
      "timezone": "GMT"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/ci/pipelines/analytics/aggregate`

## Search tests events

<a id="opIdSearchCIAppTestEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/ci/tests/events/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "from": "now-15m",
      "query": "@test.service:web-tests AND @test.status:fail",
      "to": "now"
    },
    "options": {
      "timezone": "GMT"
    },
    "page": {
      "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
      "limit": 25
    },
    "sort": "timestamp"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/ci/tests/events/search`

List endpoint returns CI Visibility test events that match a [search query](https://docs.datadoghq.com/continuous_integration/explorer/search_syntax/).
[Results are paginated similarly to logs](https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/collect-multiple-logs-with-pagination).

Use this endpoint to build complex events filtering and search.

```json
    "to": "now"

    "timezone": "GMT"
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-csm-ownership">CSM Ownership</h1>

Datadog Cloud Security Management (CSM) Ownership infers the most likely owner
for a cloud resource by combining ownership signals from across the platform,
and lets you review the inference, inspect its evidence, and submit feedback to
persist, override, or correct the inferred owner.
For more information, see [Cloud Security Management](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management).

## Get ownership settings for the org

<a id="opIdGetOwnershipSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/csm/ownership/settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/csm/ownership/settings`

Get ownership settings for the org. When settings are unset, the API returns the default opt-out configuration with `auto_tag` set to `true` and `confidence_level` set to `high`.

```json
    "attributes": {

  }
}
```

## Submit feedback on an ownership inference

<a id="opIdCreateOwnershipFeedback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/csm/ownership/res-1/team/feedback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "action": "confirm",
        "inference_checksum": "abc123"
      },
      "type": "ownership_feedback"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/csm/ownership/{resource_id}/{owner_type}/feedback`

Submit feedback on the current ownership inference for a resource and owner type. Valid actions are `confirm`, `reject`, `correct`, and `persist`.

The request must include the current inference `checksum` in `inference_checksum`. If the checksum does not match the current inference state, the endpoint returns `409 Conflict`.

When `action` is `correct`, `corrected_owner_handle` and `corrected_owner_type` are required.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "action": "confirm",
      "inference_checksum": "abc123"
    },
    "type": "ownership_feedback"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="submit-feedback-on-an-ownership-inference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource_id|path|string|true|The identifier of the resource that the feedback applies to.|
|owner_type|path|[OwnershipOwnerType](#schemaownershipownertype)|true|The type of owner that the feedback applies to.|
|body|body|[OwnershipFeedbackRequest](#schemaownershipfeedbackrequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[OwnershipFeedbackRequestData](#schemaownershipfeedbackrequestdata)|true|The data wrapper for an ownership feedback request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|owner_type|user|
|owner_type|team|
|owner_type|service|
|owner_type|unknown|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "action": "confirm",
      "checksum": "abc123",
      "new_status": "suggested",
      "owner_type": "team",
      "previous_status": "suggested",
      "primary_contact_ref": "ref:handle/team-a",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-15T10:00:00Z"
    },
    "id": "res-1",
    "type": "ownership_feedback_result"
  }
}
```

```json
    {

      },

    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-csm-settings">CSM Settings</h1>

Datadog Cloud Security Management (CSM) Settings APIs allow you to list and filter
your cloud hosts monitored by CSM, covering both agentless and agent-based discovery.
For more information, see [Cloud Security Management](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management).

## List agentless hosts

<a id="opIdListCSMAgentlessHosts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/csm/settings/agentless_hosts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/csm/settings/agentless_hosts`

Get the list of agentless hosts for CSM, with optional pagination and filtering.

<h3 id="list-agentless-hosts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The page index for pagination (zero-based).|
|size|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of agentless hosts to return per page.|
|query|query|string|false|A search query string to filter agentless hosts.|

> Example responses

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-csm-threats">CSM Threats</h1>

Workload Protection monitors file, network, and process activity across your environment to detect real-time threats to your infrastructure. See [Workload Protection](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/workload_protection/) for more information on setting up Workload Protection.

**Note**: These endpoints are split based on whether you are using the US1-FED site or not. Please reference the specific resource for the site you are using.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-case-management">Case Management</h1>

<a id="opIdAggregateCases"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cases/aggregate \
  -X POST \

}
```

## Create a case link

<a id="opIdCreateCaseLink"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cases/link \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "child_entity_id": "4417921d-0866-4a38-822c-6f2a0f65f77d",
        "child_entity_type": "CASE",
        "parent_entity_id": "bf0cbac6-4c16-4cfb-b6bf-ca5e0ec37a4f",
        "parent_entity_type": "CASE",
        "relationship": "BLOCKS"
      },
      "type": "link"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/cases/link`

Creates a directional link between two work items (for example, work item A blocks work item B). The parent and child work items and their relationship type must be specified.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "child_entity_id": "4417921d-0866-4a38-822c-6f2a0f65f77d",
      "child_entity_type": "CASE",
      "parent_entity_id": "bf0cbac6-4c16-4cfb-b6bf-ca5e0ec37a4f",
      "parent_entity_type": "CASE",
      "relationship": "BLOCKS"
    },
    "type": "link"
  }
```

## Add insights to a case

<a id="opIdAddCaseInsights"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cases/f98a5a5b-e0ff-45d4-b2f5-afe6e74de504/insights \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "insights": [
          {
            "ref": "/monitors/12345?q=total",
            "resource_id": "12345",
            "type": "SECURITY_SIGNAL"
          }
        ]
      },
      "type": "case"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/cases/{case_id}/insights`

Adds one or more insights to a work item. Insights are references to related Datadog resources (such as monitors, security signals, incidents, or error tracking issues) that provide investigative context. Up to 100 insights can be added per request. Each insight requires a type (see `CaseInsightType` for allowed values), a ref (URL path to the resource), and a resource_id.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "insights": [
        {
          "ref": "/monitors/12345?q=total",
          "resource_id": "12345",
          "type": "SECURITY_SIGNAL"
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "case"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-insights-to-a-case-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|case_id|path|string|true|Work item's UUID or key|
|body|body|[CaseInsightsRequest](#schemacaseinsightsrequest)|true|Work item insights request.|
|» data|body|[CaseInsightsData](#schemacaseinsightsdata)|true|Data object containing the insights to add or remove.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
      "key": "CASEM-1234",
      "priority": "NOT_DEFINED",
      "status": "OPEN",
      "status_name": "Open",
      "title": "Memory leak investigation on API"
```

<a id="opIdCreateChangeRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/change-management/change-request \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \

  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "change_request_linked_incident_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",

        "change_request_plan": "1. Deploy to staging 2. Run tests 3. Deploy to production",
        "change_request_risk": "LOW",
        "change_request_type": "NORMAL",
        "description": "Deploying new payment service v2.1",
        "end_date": "2024-01-02T15:00:00Z",
        "project_id": "d4bbe1af-f36e-42f1-87c1-493ca35c320e",
        "requested_teams": [
          "team-handle-1"
        ],
        "start_date": "2024-01-01T03:00:00Z",

      "type": "change_request"

  }'
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-cloud-cost-management">Cloud Cost Management</h1>

The Cloud Cost Management API allows you to set up, edit, and delete Cloud Cost Management accounts for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. You can query your cost data by using the [Metrics endpoint](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/metrics/#query-timeseries-data-across-multiple-products) and the `cloud_cost` data source. For more information, see the [Cloud Cost Management documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/cloud_cost_management/).

## List cost anomalies

<a id="opIdListCostAnomalies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cost/anomalies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/cost/anomalies`

List detected Cloud Cost Management anomalies for the organization.

<h3 id="list-cost-anomalies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|query|integer(int64)|false|Start time as Unix milliseconds. Defaults to the start of the latest stable seven-day window.|
|end|query|integer(int64)|false|End time as Unix milliseconds. Defaults to the end of the latest stable seven-day window.|
|filter|query|string|false|Optional JSON object mapping cost tag keys to allowed values, for example `{"team":["payments"],"env":["prod"]}`. Filters match anomaly dimensions or correlated tags.|
|min_anomalous_threshold|query|string|false|Minimum absolute anomalous cost change to include. Numeric value; defaults to `1`.|
|min_cost_threshold|query|string|false|Minimum absolute actual cost to include. Numeric value; defaults to `0`.|
|dismissal_cause|query|string|false|Filter by resolution state. Use `none` for unresolved anomalies, `all` or `*` for resolved anomalies, or a comma-separated list of causes.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Sort field. One of `start_date`, `end_date`, `duration`, `max_cost`, `anomalous_cost`, or `dismissal_date`. Defaults to `anomalous_cost`.|
|order|query|string|false|Sort direction. One of `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `desc`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of anomalies to return. Defaults to `200`.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Pagination offset. Defaults to `0`.|
|provider_ids|query|[string]|false|Optional repeated cloud or SaaS provider filters, such as `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `Oracle`, `datadog`, `OpenAI`, or `Anthropic`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "anomalies": [
        {
          "actual_cost": 3001.24,
          "anomalous_cost_change": 1250.75,
          "anomaly_end": 1730429150000,
          "anomaly_start": 1730259950000,
          "correlated_tags": {
            "region": [
              "us-east-1",
              "us-west-2"
            ]
          },
          "dimensions": {
            "service": "ec2"
          },
          "max_cost": 5000.5,
          "provider": "aws",
          "query": "sum:aws.cost.net.amortized{aws_cost_type IN (Usage,DiscountedUsage,SavingsPlanCoveredUsage) AND aws_product NOT IN (supportenterprise) AND service:\"ec2\"}.rollup(sum, daily)",
          "uuid": "b0a6aaa9-3c4c-48cb-9447-a0d1338b3e09"
        }
      ],
      "avg_daily_anomalous_cost": 625.375,
      "total_actual_cost": 3001.24,
      "total_anomalous_cost": 1250.75,
      "total_count": 1
    },
    "id": "anomalies",
    "type": "anomalies"
  }
```
