```bash
      "limit": 25
    },
    "sort": "timestamp"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/logs/events/search`

List endpoint returns logs that match a log search query.
[Results are paginated][1].

Use this endpoint to search and filter your logs.

**If you are considering archiving logs for your organization,
consider use of the Datadog archive capabilities instead of the log list API.
See [Datadog Logs Archive documentation][2].**

[1]: /logs/guide/collect-multiple-logs-with-pagination
[2]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/archives

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "from": "now-15m",
    "indexes": [
      "main",
      "web"
    ],
    "query": "service:web-api AND @http.status_code:[200 TO 299]",
    "storage_tier": "indexes",
    "to": "now"
  },
  "options": {
    "timezone": "GMT"
  },
  "page": {
    "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
    "limit": 25
  },
  "sort": "timestamp"
}
```

|» page|body|[LogsListRequestPage](#schemalogslistrequestpage)|false|Paging attributes for listing logs.|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-logs-archive-searches">Logs Archive Searches</h1>

Archive Search queries logs directly from long-term storage archives without prior
rehydration and charges only for the data scanned.

A search runs in one of two modes. By default, it scans the archive and retains up to
100,000 matching logs for 24 hours on a dedicated results page. Include a `rehydration`
object to run a Search & Rehydration instead, which retains the matches for a longer
custom retention period and makes them available beyond Log Explorer, such as in Dashboards and Notebooks.

A search requires the `logs_write_historical_view` or `logs_write_archive_search`
permission. Rehydration requires `logs_write_historical_view`.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/explorer/archive_search/">Find out more at</a>

## Create an Archive Search

<a id="opIdCreateArchiveSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/logs/archive_searches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "archive_id": "mhmyYmyLTOaFYKvhNadu1w",
        "description": "Investigating the checkout latency spike.",
        "from": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "name": "checkout-latency-investigation",
        "query": "service:checkout status:error",
        "rehydration": {
          "max_rehydrated_events": 1000000,
          "retention_days": 15,
          "tier": "standard"
        },
        "to": "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z"
      },
      "type": "archive_search"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/logs/archive_searches`

Start a search over the logs stored in an archive.

Without a `rehydration` object, the search only scans the archive and reports how much data
matched. With one, the matched logs are also indexed into a retained historical view, which
requires the `logs_write_historical_view` permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "archive_id": "mhmyYmyLTOaFYKvhNadu1w",
      "description": "Investigating the checkout latency spike.",
      "from": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "name": "checkout-latency-investigation",
      "query": "service:checkout status:error",
      "rehydration": {
        "max_rehydrated_events": 1000000,
        "retention_days": 15,
        "tier": "standard"
      },
      "to": "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "type": "archive_search"
  }
}
```

`PATCH /api/v2/logs/archive_searches/{archive_search_id}`

retained historical view. Rehydration is the only thing this endpoint can change, and it only
applies to a search that has already finished scanning.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-logs-archives">Logs Archives</h1>

Archives forward all the logs ingested to a cloud storage system.

See the [Archives Page](https://app.datadoghq.com/logs/pipelines/archives)
for a list of the archives currently configured in Datadog.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/archives/">Find out more at</a>

## Get archive order

<a id="opIdGetLogsArchiveOrder"></a>

> Code samples

```json
      },
```

```bash
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/logs/config/archive-order`

Update the order of your archives. Since logs are processed sequentially, reordering an archive may change
the structure and content of the data processed by other archives.

**Note**: Using the `PUT` method updates your archive's order by replacing the current order
with the new one.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "archive_ids": [
        "a2zcMylnM4OCHpYusxIi1g",
        "a2zcMylnM4OCHpYusxIi2g",
        "a2zcMylnM4OCHpYusxIi3g"
      ]
    },
    "type": "archive_order"
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» data|body|[LogsArchiveOrderDefinition](#schemalogsarchiveorderdefinition)|false|The definition of an archive order.|

> Example responses

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-logs-custom-destinations">Logs Custom Destinations</h1>

Custom Destinations forward all the logs ingested to an external destination.

**Note**: Log forwarding is not available for the Government (US1-FED) site. Contact your account representative for more information.

See the [Custom Destinations Page](https://app.datadoghq.com/logs/pipelines/log-forwarding/custom-destinations)
for a list of the custom destinations currently configured in web UI.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/log_configuration/forwarding_custom_destinations/">Find out more at</a>

## Get all custom destinations

<a id="opIdListLogsCustomDestinations"></a>

> Code samples


<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-logs-restriction-queries">Logs Restriction Queries</h1>

**Note: This endpoint is in public beta. If you have any feedback, contact [Datadog support](https://docs.datadoghq.com/help/).**

A Restriction Query is a logs query that restricts which logs the `logs_read_data` permission grants read access to.
For users whose roles have Restriction Queries, any log query they make only returns those log events that also match
one of their Restriction Queries. This is true whether the user queries log events from any log-related feature, including
the log explorer, Live Tail, re-hydration, or a dashboard widget.

Restriction Queries currently only support use of the following components of log events:

- Reserved attributes
- The log message
- Tags

To restrict read access on log data, add a team tag to log events to indicate which teams own them, and then scope Restriction Queries to the relevant values of the team tag. Tags can be applied to log events in many ways, and a log event can have multiple tags with the same key (like team) and different values. This means the same log event can be visible to roles whose restriction queries are scoped to different team values.

See [How to Set Up RBAC for Logs](https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/logs-rbac/?tab=api#restrict-access-to-logs) for details on how to add restriction queries.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-metrics">Metrics</h1>

The metrics endpoint allows you to:

- Post metrics data so it can be graphed on Datadog’s dashboards
- Query metrics from any time period (timeseries and scalar)
- Modify tag configurations for metrics
- View tags and volumes for metrics

**Note**: A graph can only contain a set number of points
and as the timeframe over which a metric is viewed increases,
aggregation between points occurs to stay below that set number.

The Post, Patch, and Delete `manage_tags` API methods can only be performed by
a user who has the `Manage Tags for Metrics` permission.

See the [Metrics page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/metrics/) for more information.

## Get a list of metrics

<a id="opIdListTagConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/metrics`

Get a list of actively reporting metrics for your organization. Pagination is optional using the `page[cursor]` and `page[size]` query parameters.

Query parameters use bracket notation (for example, `filter[tags]`, `filter[queried][window][seconds]`). Pass them as standard URL query strings, URL-encoding the brackets if your client does not handle them. For example: `GET /api/v2/metrics?filter[tags]=env:prod&window[seconds]=86400&page[size]=500`.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[configured]|query|boolean|false|Only return custom metrics that have been configured (`true`) or not configured (`false`) with Metrics Without Limits.|
|filter[is_configurable]|query|boolean|false|Only return metrics that are eligible (`true`) or ineligible (`false`) for configuration with Metrics Without Limits.|
|filter[tags_configured]|query|string|false|Only return metrics that have the given tag key(s) in their Metrics Without Limits configuration (included or excluded).|
|filter[metric_type]|query|[MetricTagConfigurationMetricTypeCategory](#schemametrictagconfigurationmetrictypecategory)|false|Only return metrics of the given metric type.|
|filter[include_percentiles]|query|boolean|false|Only return distribution metrics that have percentile aggregations enabled (true) or disabled (false).|
|filter[queried]|query|boolean|false|Only return metrics that have been queried (true) or not queried (false) in the look back window. Set the window with `filter[queried][window][seconds]`; if omitted, a default window is used.|
|filter[queried][window][seconds]|query|integer(int64)|false|The look-back window for `filter[queried]`, in seconds. You must also set `filter[queried]`, or the request returns a 400 error. The default value is 2,592,000 seconds (30 days), the maximum value is 15,552,000 seconds (180 days), and the minimum value is 0. With `0`, the window ends now, so `filter[queried]=true` returns almost no metrics and `filter[queried]=false` returns all metrics. For example: `filter[queried]=true&filter[queried][window][seconds]=604800`.|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Only return metrics that were submitted with tags matching this expression. You can use AND, OR, IN, and wildcards. For example: `filter[tags]=env IN (staging,test) AND service:web*`.|
|filter[related_assets]|query|boolean|false|Only return metrics that are used in at least one dashboard, monitor, notebook, or SLO.|
|include|query|string|false|Include related resources in the response. Set to `metric_volumes` to include indexed and ingested volume counts for each metric.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort results by metric volume. Prefix a key with `-` for descending order. Supported keys: `metric_volumes.indexed_volume`, `metric_volumes.ingested_volume`, `metric_volumes.indexed_volume_delta`, `metric_volumes.ingested_volume_delta`. Requires a paginated request (`page[size]` or `page[cursor]`).|
|window[seconds]|query|integer(int64)|false|Only return metrics that have been actively reporting in this window. The default value is 3,600 seconds (1 hour), the maximum value is 5,184,000 seconds (60 days), and the minimum value is 0. With `0`, the API returns only metrics that reported in the last few minutes.|
|page[size]|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of results per page. Send `page[size]` on the first request to opt in to pagination. On subsequent requests, send `page[cursor]` set to the value of `meta.pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response. To retain a custom page size, include `page[size]` on every request. The default value is 10000, the maximum value is 10000, and the minimum value is 1.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Cursor for pagination. Use `page[size]` to opt-in to pagination and get the first page; for subsequent pages, use the value from `meta.pagination.next_cursor` in the response. Pagination is complete when `next_cursor` is null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[metric_type]|non_distribution|
|filter[metric_type]|distribution|
|filter[metric_type]|exponential_histogram|
|filter[metric_type]|explicit_histogram|

## Configure tags for multiple metrics

<a id="opIdCreateBulkTagsMetricsConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/config/bulk-tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "emails": [
          "sue@example.com",
          "bob@example.com"
        ],
        "tags": [
          "host",
          "pod_name",
          "is_shadow"
        ]
      },
      "id": "kafka.lag",
      "type": "metric_bulk_configure_tags"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/metrics/config/bulk-tags`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Note**: This endpoint is deprecated. Use [Tag Indexing Rules](/api/latest/metrics/#create-a-tag-indexing-rule) (`POST /api/v2/metrics/tag-indexing-rules`) instead.

Create and define a list of queryable tag keys for a set of existing count, gauge, rate, and distribution metrics.
Metrics are selected by passing a metric name prefix. Use the Delete method of this API path to remove tag configurations.
Results can be sent to a set of account email addresses, just like the same operation in the Datadog web app.
If multiple calls include the same metric, the last configuration applied (not by submit order) is used, do not
expect deterministic ordering of concurrent calls. The `exclude_tags_mode` value will set all metrics that match the prefix to
the same exclusion state, metric tag configurations do not support mixed inclusion and exclusion for tags on the same metric.
Can only be used with application keys of users with the `Manage Tags for Metrics` permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "emails": [
        "sue@example.com",
        "bob@example.com"
      ],
      "tags": [
        "host",
        "pod_name",
        "is_shadow"
      ]
    },
    "id": "kafka.lag",
    "type": "metric_bulk_configure_tags"
  }
}
```

## Create a derived metric

<a id="opIdCreateDerivedMetric"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/derived-metrics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "definition": {
          "formula": "a",
          "queries": [
            {

              "name": "a",
              "query": "avg:system.cpu.user{*}"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "id": "my.derived.metric",
      "type": "derived_metrics"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/metrics/derived-metrics`

Create a derived metric for the org. The metric name is supplied as the resource `id`,
and the `definition` sets the formula and the queries the formula is computed from.
Requires the `Manage Tags for Metrics` permission.

## List tag indexing rule exemptions

<a id="opIdListTagIndexingRuleExemptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/list-tag-indexing-rule-exemptions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/metrics/list-tag-indexing-rule-exemptions`

Returns explicit exemptions and legacy tag configurations that exclude metrics from tag indexing rules.
You can filter results by metric name prefix, whether an exemption is safe to remove, or the UUID of a matching
tag indexing rule. You can sort results by metric name or by estimated change in indexed volume.

<h3 id="list-tag-indexing-rule-exemptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[metric_prefix]|query|string|false|Filter exemptions to metrics whose names start with this literal prefix.<br>Matching is case-sensitive. Wildcard characters are treated literally.|
|filter[safe]|query|boolean|false|Filter exemptions by whether they are safe to remove. An exemption is considered safe when a fresh, usable<br>estimate indicates that removing it would not increase indexed volume and would not drop tags used to query<br>the metric in monitors, dashboards, notebooks, or SLOs. Set to `true` to return safe-to-remove exemptions,<br>or `false` to return all other exemptions, including those with unavailable or stale estimates.|
|filter[tag_indexing_rule_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter exemptions to metrics matched by the tag indexing rule with this UUID.|
|sort|query|[TagIndexingRuleExemptionSort](#schematagindexingruleexemptionsort)|false|Sort field. Prefix the field with `-` for descending order. The default is `estimated_change_in_volume` in ascending order, with the largest reductions (most negative values) first.|
|page[size]|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of results per page. Defaults to 10000; accepts values from 1 to 10000. If<br>`meta.pagination.next_cursor` is non-null, request the next page by passing that value as `page[cursor]`.<br>Continue until `next_cursor` is null.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Cursor for pagination. Use `page[size]` to opt-in to pagination and get the first page; for subsequent pages, use the value from `meta.pagination.next_cursor` in the response. Pagination is complete when `next_cursor` is null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|name|
|sort|-name|
|sort|estimated_change_in_volume|
|sort|-estimated_change_in_volume|

> Example responses

## Reorder tag indexing rules

<a id="opIdReorderTagIndexingRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/tag-indexing-rules/order \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "rule_ids": [
          "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
          "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
        ]
      },
      "type": "tag_indexing_rules"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/metrics/tag-indexing-rules/order`

Atomically re-sequence the tag indexing rules for an org to match the supplied list of rule UUIDs.
The server assigns `rule_order` 1, 2, … matching each rule UUID by position in the list.
The UUIDs of all active rules must be provided; omitting any active rule UUID returns a 400 error.
Requires the `Manage Tags for Metrics` permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "rule_ids": [
        "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
        "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
      ]
    },
    "type": "tag_indexing_rules"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="reorder-tag-indexing-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TagIndexingRuleOrderRequest](#schematagindexingruleorderrequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[TagIndexingRuleOrderData](#schematagindexingruleorderdata)|true|Data object for the reorder operation.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
```

`PUT /api/v2/metrics/tag-indexing-rules/{id}`

`DELETE /api/v2/metrics/tag-indexing-rules/{id}`

Soft-delete a tag indexing rule. Idempotent: returns 204 whether the rule existed or was already deleted.
Remaining rules in the org are automatically re-sequenced to keep `rule_order` dense and 1-based.

## List tags by metric name

<a id="opIdListTagsByMetricName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/dist.http.endpoint.request/all-tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/metrics/{metric_name}/all-tags`

View indexed and ingested tags for a given metric name.
Results are filtered by the `window[seconds]` parameter, which defaults to 14400 (4 hours).

<h3 id="list-tags-by-metric-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric_name|path|string|true|The name of the metric.|
|window[seconds]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of seconds of look back (from now) to query for tag data.<br>Default value is 14400 (4 hours), minimum value is 14400 (4 hours).|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Filter results to tags from data points that have the specified tags.<br>For example, `filter[tags]=env:staging,host:123` returns tags only from data points with both `env:staging` and `host:123`.|
|filter[match]|query|string|false|Filter returned tags to those matching a substring.<br>For example, `filter[match]=env` returns tags like `env:prod`, `environment:staging`, etc.|
|filter[include_tag_values]|query|boolean|false|Whether to include tag values in the response.<br>Defaults to true.|
|filter[allow_partial]|query|boolean|false|Whether to allow partial results.<br>Defaults to false.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "tags": [
        "env:prod",
        "host:myhost"
      ]
    },
    "id": "system.cpu.user",
    "type": "metrics"
  }
}
```

## Tag Configuration Cardinality Estimator

<a id="opIdEstimateMetricsOutputSeries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/dist.http.endpoint.request/estimate \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/metrics/{metric_name}/estimate`

Returns the estimated cardinality for a metric with a given tag, percentile and number of aggregations configuration using Metrics without Limits&trade;.

<h3 id="tag-configuration-cardinality-estimator-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric_name|path|string|true|The name of the metric.|
|filter[groups]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of tag keys that the metric is configured to query with. For example: `filter[groups]=app,host`.|
|filter[exclude_tags_mode]|query|boolean|false|When `true`, `filter[groups]` is treated as an exclude list instead of an include list. Defaults to `false`.|
|filter[hours_ago]|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of hours of look back (from now) to estimate cardinality with. If unspecified, it defaults to 0 hours.|
|filter[num_aggregations]|query|integer(int32)|false|Deprecated. Number of aggregations has no impact on volume.|
|filter[pct]|query|boolean|false|Deprecated. This query parameter has no effect on the estimate.|
|filter[timespan_h]|query|integer(int32)|false|A window, in hours, from the look back to estimate cardinality with. The minimum and default is 1 hour.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "estimate_type": "count_or_gauge",
      "estimated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
```

## Create a tag configuration

<a id="opIdCreateTagConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/metrics/dist.http.endpoint.request/tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "include_percentiles": false,
        "metric_type": "distribution",
        "tags": [
          "app",
          "datacenter"
        ]
      },
      "id": "http.endpoint.request",
      "type": "manage_tags"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/metrics/{metric_name}/tags`

Create and define a list of queryable tag keys for an existing count/gauge/rate/distribution metric.
Optionally, include percentile aggregations on any distribution metric. By setting `exclude_tags_mode`
to true, the behavior is changed from an allow-list to a deny-list, and tags in the defined list are
not queryable. Can only be used with application keys of users with the `Manage Tags for Metrics`
permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "include_percentiles": false,
      "metric_type": "distribution",
      "tags": [
        "app",
        "datacenter"
```

`PATCH /api/v2/metrics/{metric_name}/tags`

Update the tag configuration of a metric or percentile aggregations of a distribution metric or custom aggregations
of a count, rate, or gauge metric. By setting `exclude_tags_mode` to true the behavior is changed
from an allow-list to a deny-list, and tags in the defined list will not be queryable.
Can only be used with application keys from users with the `Manage Tags for Metrics` permission. This endpoint requires
a tag configuration to be created first.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "group_by": [
        "app",
        "datacenter"
      ],
      "include_percentiles": false

}
```

## Submit metrics

<a id="opIdSubmitMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/series \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "series": [
      {
        "metric": "system.load.1",
        "points": [
          {
            "timestamp": 1636629071,
            "value": 1.1
          }
        ],
        "resources": [
          {
            "name": "dummyhost",
            "type": "host"
          }
        ],
        "type": 0
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/series`

The metrics end-point allows you to post time-series data that can be graphed on Datadog’s dashboards.
The maximum payload size is 500 kilobytes (512000 bytes). Compressed payloads must have a decompressed size of less than 5 megabytes (5242880 bytes).

If you’re submitting metrics directly to the Datadog API without using DogStatsD, expect:

- 64 bits for the timestamp
- 64 bits for the value
- 20 bytes for the metric names
- 50 bytes for the timeseries
- The full payload is approximately 100 bytes.

Host name is one of the resources in the Resources field.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "series": [
    {
      "metric": "system.load.1",
      "points": [
        {
          "timestamp": 1636629071,
          "value": 1.1
        }
      ],
      "resources": [
        {
          "name": "dummyhost",
          "type": "host"
        }
      ],
      "type": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="submit-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|header|[MetricContentEncoding](#schemametriccontentencoding)|false|HTTP header used to compress the media-type.|
|body|body|[MetricPayload](#schemametricpayload)|true|none|
|» series|body|[[MetricSeries](#schemametricseries)]|true|A list of timeseries to submit to Datadog.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|deflate|
|Content-Encoding|zstd1|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|

```json
  "errors": []
}
```

```json
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

```json
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

## List Model Lab runs

<a id="opIdListModelLabRuns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/model-lab-api/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/model-lab-api/runs`

List all Model Lab runs for the current organization.

<h3 id="list-model-lab-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[id]|query|string|false|Filter by run ID(s). Comma-separated list for multiple IDs.|
|filter|query|string|false|Text search filter for run name or description.|
|filter[owner_id]|query|string|false|Filter by owner UUID.|
|filter[status]|query|[ModelLabRunStatus](#schemamodellabrunstatus)|false|Filter by run status. Valid values: pending, running, completed, failed, killed, unresponsive, paused.|
|filter[project_id]|query|integer(int64)|false|Filter by project ID.|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Filter by tags. Format: key:value,key2:value2.|
|filter[params]|query|string|false|Filter by params. Format: key:value,key2:>0.5,key3:true.|
|filter[parent_run_id]|query|string|false|Filter by parent run ID. Use 'null' to return only root runs (runs with no parent).|
|pinned_first|query|boolean|false|Sort pinned runs before non-pinned runs. Pinned runs are ordered by pin time descending.|
|include_pinned|query|boolean|false|Include all runs pinned by the current user, regardless of other filters.|
|include_descendant_matches|query|boolean|false|When true, also return runs whose descendants match the active filters. The descendant_match field in each result indicates whether the run was included via a descendant match.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort field. Valid values: name, created_at, updated_at, duration. Prefix with '-' for descending order (e.g., -updated_at).|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of items per page. Maximum is 100.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number (1-indexed).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[status]|pending|
|filter[status]|running|
|filter[status]|completed|
|filter[status]|failed|
|filter[status]|killed|
|filter[status]|unresponsive|
|filter[status]|paused|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-monitors">Monitors</h1>

[Monitors](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors) allow you to watch a metric or check that you care about and
notifies your team when a defined threshold has exceeded.

For more information, see [Creating Monitors](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/create/types/) and
[Tag Policies](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/settings/).

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/create/types/">Find out more at</a>


`GET /api/v2/monitor/notification_rule`

Returns a list of all monitor notification rules.

<h3 id="get-all-monitor-notification-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The page to start paginating from. If `page` is not specified, the argument defaults to the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of rules to return per page. If `per_page` is not specified, the argument defaults to 100.|
|sort|query|string|false|String for sort order, composed of field and sort order separated by a colon, for example `name:asc`. Supported sort directions: `asc`, `desc`. Supported fields: `name`, `created_at`.|
|filters|query|string|false|JSON-encoded filter object. Supported keys:<br>* `text`: Free-text query matched against rule name, tags, and recipients.<br>* `tags`: Array of strings. Return rules that have any of these tags.<br>* `recipients`: Array of strings. Return rules that have any of these recipients.|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of resource paths for related resources to include in the response. Supported resource<br>path is `created_by`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "filter": {
          "scope": "team:product"
        },
        "name": "A notification rule name",
        "recipients": [
          "slack-test-channel"
        ]
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-1234-0000-000000000000",
      "type": "monitor-notification-rule"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "errors": [

  ]
}
```

```json
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-network-device-monitoring">Network Device Monitoring</h1>

The Network Device Monitoring API allows you to fetch devices and interfaces and their attributes. See the [Network Device Monitoring page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/network_monitoring/) for more information.

## Get the list of devices

<a id="opIdListDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/ndm/devices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/ndm/devices`

Get the list of devices.

<h3 id="get-the-list-of-devices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Size for a given page. The maximum allowed value is 500. Defaults to 50.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Specific page number to return. Defaults to 0.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort devices by. Defaults to `name`. Prefix the field with `-` to sort in descending order, for example, `-name`.|
|filter[tag]|query|string|false|Filter devices by tag.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "device_type": "other",
        "integration": "snmp",
        "ip_address": "1.2.3.4",
        "name": "example device",
        "status": "ok"
      },
      "id": "foiwf7rgw38fh",
      "type": "device"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page": {
      "total_filtered_count": 1
    }
  }
}
```

```json
        "header": "Authorization",
        "parameter": "limit",
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/title"
      },
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

## Register an OAuth2 client

<a id="opIdRegisterOAuthClient"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/oauth2/register \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "client_name": "Example MCP Client",
    "grant_types": [
      "authorization_code",
      "refresh_token"
    ],
    "redirect_uris": [
      "https://example.com/oauth/callback"
    ],
    "response_types": [
      "code"
    ],
    "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/oauth2/register`

Register an OAuth2 client using the Dynamic Client Registration protocol defined in RFC 7591.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_name": "Example MCP Client",
  "grant_types": [
    "authorization_code",
    "refresh_token"
  ],
  "redirect_uris": [
    "https://example.com/oauth/callback"
  ],
  "response_types": [
    "code"
  ],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}
```

<h3 id="register-an-oauth2-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OAuthClientRegistrationRequest](#schemaoauthclientregistrationrequest)|true|none|
|» client_name|body|string|true|Human-readable name of the client. Control characters are rejected.|
|» client_uri|body|string|false|URL of the home page of the client.|
|» grant_types|body|[[OAuthClientRegistrationGrantType](#schemaoauthclientregistrationgranttype)]|false|OAuth 2.0 grant types the client may use.<br>Defaults to `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` when omitted.|
|» jwks_uri|body|string|false|URL referencing the client's JSON Web Key Set.|
|» logo_uri|body|string|false|URL referencing a logo for the client.|
|» policy_uri|body|string|false|URL pointing to the client's privacy policy.|
|» redirect_uris|body|[string]|true|Array of redirection URI strings used by the client in redirect-based flows.|
|» response_types|body|[[OAuthClientRegistrationResponseType](#schemaoauthclientregistrationresponsetype)]|false|OAuth 2.0 response types the client may use. Only `code` is supported.|
|» scope|body|string|false|Space-separated list of scope values the client may request.|
|» token_endpoint_auth_method|body|string|false|Requested authentication method for the token endpoint. Only `none` is supported.|
|» tos_uri|body|string|false|URL pointing to the client's terms of service.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_types|authorization_code|
|» grant_types|refresh_token|
|» response_types|code|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "client_id": "72b68208-36a6-11f0-b21b-da7ad0900002",
  "client_name": "Example MCP Client",
  "grant_types": [
    "authorization_code",
    "refresh_token"
  ],
  "redirect_uris": [
    "https://example.com/oauth/callback"
  ],
  "response_types": [
    "code"
  ],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client_metadata",
  "error_description": "redirect URI is not well-formed"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="register-an-oauth2-client-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[OAuthClientRegistrationResponse](#schemaoauthclientregistrationresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[OAuthClientRegistrationError](#schemaoauthclientregistrationerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

## List On-Call escalation policies

<a id="opIdListOnCallEscalationPolicies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/on-call/escalation-policies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/on-call/escalation-policies`

Retrieve a paginated list of On-Call escalation policies, sorted by name.

<h3 id="list-on-call-escalation-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of escalation policies to return per page. The maximum allowed value is 50.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Specific page number to return.|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|Search query to filter escalation policies. Supports free-text search on the policy name (case-insensitive) and structured filters on `team.id` and `tags`. When set, `filter[team_id]`, `filter[user_id]`, and `filter[schedule_id]` are ignored. Can't be combined with `filter[tags]` or `filter[tags_any]`.|
|filter[team_id]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of team IDs. Returns escalation policies that belong to any of these teams or have a step targeting any of them.|
|filter[user_id]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of user IDs. Returns escalation policies with a step targeting any of these users.|
|filter[schedule_id]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of schedule IDs. Returns escalation policies with a step targeting any of these schedules.|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of `key:value` tags. Returns escalation policies that have all of these tags.|
|filter[tags_any]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of `key:value` tags. Returns escalation policies that have at least one of these tags.|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of included relationships to be returned. Allowed values: `teams`, `steps`, `steps.targets`, `steps.targets.schedule`, `user.color`. `user.color` populates the `color` attribute of users included through `steps.targets`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "name": "Escalation Policy 1",
        "resolve_page_on_policy_end": true,
        "retries": 2,
        "tags": [
          "env:prod"
        ]
      },
      "id": "00000000-aba1-0000-0000-000000000000",
      "relationships": {
        "steps": {
          "data": [
            {
              "id": "00000000-aba1-0000-0000-000000000000",
              "type": "steps"
            }
          ]
        },
        "teams": {
          "data": [
            {
              "id": "00000000-da3a-0000-0000-000000000000",
              "type": "teams"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "policies"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page": {
      "first_number": 0,
      "last_number": 0,
      "next_number": null,
      "number": 0,
      "prev_number": null,
      "size": 20,
      "total": 1,
      "type": "number_size"
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

```json
  ]
```

```json
  ]
```

```bash
        "resolve_page_on_policy_end": true,

            "assignment": "default",

            "targets": [
              {
                "id": "00000000-aba1-0000-0000-000000000000",

                "type": "teams"
              }
            ]
          },
          {
            "assignment": "round-robin",
            "escalate_after_seconds": 3600,
            "targets": [
              {
                "id": "00000000-aba1-0000-0000-000000000000",
                "type": "users"
              },
              {
                "id": "00000000-abb1-0000-0000-000000000000",
                "type": "users"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "relationships": {
        "teams": {

              "id": "00000000-da3a-0000-0000-000000000000",
              "type": "teams"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "policies"
    }
  }'
```

## Get on-call responders for a schedule

<a id="opIdGetScheduleOnCallResponders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/on-call/schedules/3653d3c6-0c75-11ea-ad28-fb5701eabc7d/responders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/on-call/schedules/{schedule_id}/responders`

Retrieves the on-call responders for the specified schedule, grouped by position (previous, current, next), at a given time. Supports schedules with multiple concurrent on-call responders at a position, by returning a list of shifts per position.

<h3 id="get-on-call-responders-for-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of included relationships to be returned. Allowed values: `schedule`, `responders`, `responders.shifts`, `responders.shifts.user`.|
|schedule_id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|filter[position]|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of positions to retrieve. Allowed values: `previous`, `current`, `next`. Defaults to `current` if omitted.|
|filter[at_ts]|query|string|false|Retrieves the on-call responders at the given timestamp in RFC3339 format (for example, `2025-05-07T02:53:01Z` or `2025-05-07T02:53:01+00:00`). If you use a time zone offset with `+`, URL-encode the `+` as `%2B`. Defaults to the current time if omitted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "scheduled_at": "2024-05-07T02:53:01.000000000Z"
    },
    "id": "3653d3c6-0c75-11ea-ad28-fb5701eabc7d-1715054400",
    "relationships": {
      "responders": {
        "data": [
          {
            "id": "3653d3c6-0c75-11ea-ad28-fb5701eabc7d-1715054400-current",
            "type": "schedule_oncall_responder"
          }
        ]
      },
      "schedule": {
        "data": {
          "id": "3653d3c6-0c75-11ea-ad28-fb5701eabc7d",
          "type": "schedules"
        }
      }
    },
    "type": "schedule_oncall_responders"
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "position": "current"
      },
      "id": "3653d3c6-0c75-11ea-ad28-fb5701eabc7d-1715054400-current",
      "relationships": {
        "shifts": {
          "data": [
            {
              "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
              "type": "shifts"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "schedule_oncall_responder"
    },
    {
      "attributes": {
        "end": "2024-05-08T02:53:01.000000000Z",
        "start": "2024-05-07T02:53:01.000000000Z"
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
      "relationships": {
        "user": {
          "data": {
            "id": "00000000-aba1-0000-0000-000000000000",
            "type": "users"
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "shifts"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-on-call-paging">On-Call Paging</h1>

Trigger and manage [Datadog On-Call](https://docs.datadoghq.com/service_management/on-call/)
pages directly through the Datadog API.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/service_management/on-call/">External documentation</a>

## Create On-Call Page

<a id="opIdCreateOnCallPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/on-call/pages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "description": "Page details.",
        "tags": [
          "service:test"
        ],
        "target": {
          "identifier": "my-team",
          "type": "team_handle"
        },
        "title": "Page title",
        "urgency": "low"
      },
      "type": "pages"
    }
  }'
```

`GET /api/v2/org_authorized_clients`

|filter[oauth2_client][name]|query|string|false|Filter results by the OAuth2 client name.|
|filter[disabled]|query|string|false|Filter results by the org-level disabled status.|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of related resources to include.<br>Options: `oauth2_client`, `oauth2_client.app`, `user_authorized_clients.user`.|

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-org-connections">Org Connections</h1>

Manage connections between organizations. Org connections allow for controlled sharing of data between different Datadog organizations. See the [Cross-Organization Visibiltiy](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/org_settings/cross_org_visibility/) page for more information.

## List Org Connections

<a id="opIdListOrgConnections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/org_connections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

<a id="opIdListOrgGroupMemberships"></a>

`GET /api/v2/org_group_memberships`

List organization group memberships. Filter by org group ID or org UUID. At least one of `filter[org_group_id]` or `filter[org_uuid]` must be provided. When filtering by org UUID, returns a single-item list with the membership for that org.

<h3 id="list-org-group-memberships-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[org_group_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter memberships by org group ID. Required when `filter[org_uuid]` is not provided.|
|filter[org_uuid]|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter memberships by org UUID. Returns a single-item list.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|The page number to return.|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of items per page. Maximum is 1000.|
|sort|query|[OrgGroupMembershipSortOption](#schemaorggroupmembershipsortoption)|false|Field to sort memberships by. Supported values: `name`, `uuid`, `-name`, `-uuid`. Defaults to `uuid`.|

`POST /api/v2/org_group_memberships`

Add a batch of organizations to an existing organization group. This operation is not supported for organization groups with `group_type` set to `config_management`. This is an atomic operation: either all organizations are added or none are. Each request must include between 1 and 100 organizations. Each organization must be identified by a unique `org_uuid` and `org_site` pair, and must be in the same site as the requesting organization. The requesting organization must own the organization group.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "orgs": [
        {
          "org_site": "us1",
          "org_uuid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-012345678901"
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "org_group": {
        "data": {
          "id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef0123456789",
          "type": "org_groups"
        }
      }
    },
    "type": "org_group_memberships"
  }
}
```

```json
      }
    ]
```


`POST /api/v2/org_group_memberships/bulk_delete`

Delete a batch of memberships from an organization group. This operation is not supported for organization groups with `group_type` set to `config_management`. The memberships to delete are provided as membership resource identifiers, and the organization group they belong to must be specified using `filter[org_group_id]`. Each request must include between 1 and 100 unique membership IDs, and the requesting organization must own the organization group. The request does not fail if a membership ID refers to a membership that has already been deleted, does not exist, or does not belong to the organization group.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "f1e2d3c4-b5a6-7890-1234-567890abcdef",
      "type": "org_group_memberships"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2d3c4b5-a6f7-8901-2345-67890abcdef1",
      "type": "org_group_memberships"
    },
    {
      "id": "d3c4b5a6-f7e8-9012-3456-7890abcdef12",
      "type": "org_group_memberships"
    }
  ]
}
```

`DELETE /api/v2/org_group_memberships/{org_group_membership_id}`

Remove an organization from an organization group by deleting its membership. This operation is not supported for organization groups with `group_type` set to `config_management`. The organization group that the membership belongs to must be specified using `filter[org_group_id]`, and the requesting organization must own that organization group. `GET /api/v2/org_group_policies`

|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of items per page. Maximum is 1000.|
|sort|query|[OrgGroupPolicySortOption](#schemaorggrouppolicysortoption)|false|Field to sort policies by. Supported values: `id`, `name`, `-id`, `-name`. Defaults to `id`.|

`PATCH /api/v2/saml_configurations/{saml_config_uuid}`

Update a single SAML configuration for the current organization.

Use this endpoint to enable or disable identity-provider-initiated login, set the
just-in-time provisioning domains, and set the default role assigned to
just-in-time provisioned users. A default role is required to enable just-in-time provisioning.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "idp_initiated": true,
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-powerpack">Powerpack</h1>

The Powerpack endpoints allow you to:

- Get a Powerpack
- Create a Powerpack
- Delete a Powerpack
- Get a list of all Powerpacks

The Patch and Delete API methods can only be performed on a Powerpack by
a user who has the powerpack create permission for that specific Powerpack.

Read [Scale Graphing Expertise with Powerpacks](https://docs.datadoghq.com/dashboards/guide/powerpacks-best-practices/) for more information.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-processes">Processes</h1>

The processes API allows you to query processes data for your organization. See the [Live Processes page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/infrastructure/process/) for more information.

## Get all processes

<a id="opIdListProcesses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/processes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/processes`

Get processes collected by Live Processes for your organization. One request covers a window of
at most 1 hour that starts within the past 36 hours. To cover a longer period, make one request
per hour. Older data is not available from this endpoint.

When a process includes `identifying_tags`, pass them as `tag_filters` in a `process` data source
query to `/api/v2/query/scalar` or `/api/v2/query/timeseries` to get CPU or memory metrics for that
one process. If absent, don't substitute an empty filter, which would query all processes.

<h3 id="get-all-processes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|search|query|string|false|Free-text search over process fields such as the executable and user. When it contains several<br>words, a process must match all of them. Use `tags` for exact values such as host.|
|tags|query|string|false|Comma-separated `key:value` tags. A process must match every tag. Wildcards, negation<br>(`-key:value`), spaces, and `IN (...)` are not supported. To cover several hosts, make one<br>request per host.|
|from|query|integer(int64)|false|Start of the query window, in Unix seconds. Must be within the past 36 hours and at most 1 hour<br>before `to`. If not provided, the start of the query window is 15 minutes before the `to` timestamp.<br>If neither `from` nor `to` is provided, the query window is `[now - 15m, now]`.|
|to|query|integer(int64)|false|End of the query window, in Unix seconds. Must be at most 1 hour after `from`. If not provided, the<br>end of the query window is 15 minutes after the `from` timestamp. If neither `from` nor `to` is<br>provided, the query window is `[now - 15m, now]`.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of results returned.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|String to query the next page of results.<br>This key is provided with each valid response from the API in `meta.page.after`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "cmdline": "/usr/bin/python3",
        "executable": "/usr/bin/python3",
        "host": "my-host",
        "identifying_tags": [
          "host:my-host",
          "pid:123"
        ],
        "pid": 123
      },
      "id": "abc-123",
      "type": "process"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-all-processes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ProcessSummariesResponse](#schemaprocesssummariesresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Authentication Error|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

apiKeyAuth & appKeyAuth, AuthZ
</aside>

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-product-analytics">Product Analytics</h1>

Send server-side events to Product Analytics. Server-Side Events Ingestion allows you to collect custom events
from any server-side source, and retains events for 15 months. Server-side events are helpful for understanding
causes of a funnel drop-off which are external to the client-side (for example, payment processing error).

**Note**: Sending server-side events impacts billing. Review the [pricing page](https://www.datadoghq.com/pricing/?product=product-analytics#products)
and contact your Customer Success Manager for more information.

## Send server-side events

<a id="opIdSubmitProductAnalyticsEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/prodlytics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "application": {
      "id": "123abcde-123a-123b-1234-123456789abc"
    },
    "event": {
      "name": "payment.processed"
    },
    "type": "server",
    "usr": {
      "id": "123"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/prodlytics`

Send server-side events to Product Analytics. Server-side events are retained for 15 months.

Server-Side events in Product Analytics are helpful for tracking events that occur on the server,
as opposed to client-side events, which are captured by Real User Monitoring (RUM) SDKs.
This allows for a more comprehensive view of the user journey by including actions that happen on the server.
Typical examples could be `checkout.completed` or `payment.processed`.

Ingested server-side events are integrated into Product Analytics to allow users to select and filter
these events in the event picker, similar to how views or actions are handled.

**Requirements:**
- At least one of `usr`, `account`, or `session` must be provided with a valid ID.
- The `application.id` must reference a Product Analytics-enabled application.

**Custom Attributes:**
Any additional fields in the payload are flattened and searchable as facets.
For example, a payload with `{"customer": {"tier": "premium"}}` is searchable with
the syntax `@customer.tier:premium` in Datadog.

The status codes answered by the HTTP API are:
- 202: Accepted: The request has been accepted for processing
- 400: Bad request (likely an issue in the payload formatting)
- 401: Unauthorized (likely a missing API Key)
- 403: Permission issue (likely using an invalid API Key)
- 408: Request Timeout, request should be retried after some time
- 413: Payload too large (batch is above 5MB uncompressed)
- 429: Too Many Requests, request should be retried after some time
- 500: Internal Server Error, the server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request, request should be retried after some time
- 503: Service Unavailable, the server is not ready to handle the request probably because it is overloaded, request should be retried after some time

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "application": {
    "id": "123abcde-123a-123b-1234-123456789abc"
  },
  "event": {
    "name": "payment.processed"
  },
  "type": "server",
  "usr": {
    "id": "123"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-product-catalog">Product Catalog</h1>

Look up the Datadog SKUs that are generally available, together with the public list
prices, allotments, and tiered pricing that apply to them on a given date.

## List SKUs

<a id="opIdListProductCatalogSKUs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/product-catalog/skus?version=v1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/product-catalog/skus`

Get every generally available Datadog SKU, with the pricing and allotment metadata that
applies to it, for the Datadog site serving the request. A SKU is generally available
when it is billed through a metered commitment or through automatic billing; SKUs in any
other phase are not returned.

Prices, allotments, and pricing tiers are returned as they were in effect on
`as_of_date`, which defaults to the date of the request. Prices are public list prices:
they do not reflect discounts, commitments, or negotiated rates on an account.

Each SKU is a separate resource in `data`, identified by its SKU code, and sorted by
that code in ascending order. The whole catalog is returned in a single response, so
this endpoint is not paginated.

<h3 id="list-skus-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|query|[ProductCatalogSKUsAPIVersion](#schemaproductcatalogskusapiversion)|true|The version of the product catalog response contract to return. `v1` is the latest.<br>This is independent of the `/api/v2` path segment, which is the version of the<br>Datadog API itself.|
|as_of_date|query|string(date)|false|The date the returned prices, allotments, and pricing tiers are effective as of, in<br>`YYYY-MM-DD` format. Defaults to the date of the request, and must not be later<br>than it. Set it to a date in a past billing period to reconcile that period against<br>the prices that were in effect then, rather than today.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|version|v1|

> Example responses

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-rum">RUM</h1>

Manage your Real User Monitoring (RUM) applications, and search or aggregate your RUM events over HTTP. See the [RUM & Session Replay page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/real_user_monitoring/) for more information

## Aggregate RUM events

<a id="opIdAggregateRUMEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/rum/analytics/aggregate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "compute": [
      {
        "aggregation": "pc90",
        "interval": "5m",
        "metric": "@duration",
        "type": "timeseries"
      }
    ],
    "filter": {
      "from": "now-15m",
      "query": "@type:session AND @session.type:user",
      "to": "now"
    },
    "group_by": [
      {
        "facet": "@view.time_spent",
        "histogram": {
          "interval": 10,
          "max": 100,
          "min": 50
        },
        "sort": {
          "aggregation": "count",
          "order": "asc"
        }
      }
    ],
    "options": {
      "timezone": "GMT"
    },
    "page": {
      "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
      "limit": 25
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/rum/analytics/aggregate`

The API endpoint to aggregate RUM events into buckets of computed metrics and timeseries.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "compute": [
    {
      "aggregation": "pc90",
      "interval": "5m",
      "metric": "@duration",
      "type": "timeseries"
    }
  ],
  "filter": {
    "from": "now-15m",
    "query": "@type:session AND @session.type:user",
    "to": "now"
  },
  "group_by": [
    {
      "facet": "@view.time_spent",
      "histogram": {
        "interval": 10,
        "max": 100,
        "min": 50
      },
      "sort": {
        "aggregation": "count",
        "order": "asc"
      }
    }
  ],
  "options": {
    "timezone": "GMT"
  },
  "page": {
    "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
    "limit": 25
  }
}
```

<h3 id="aggregate-rum-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RUMAggregateRequest](#schemarumaggregaterequest)|true|none|
|» compute|body|[[RUMCompute](#schemarumcompute)]|false|The list of metrics or timeseries to compute for the retrieved buckets.|
|» filter|body|[RUMQueryFilter](#schemarumqueryfilter)|false|The search and filter query settings.|
|» group_by|body|[[RUMGroupBy](#schemarumgroupby)]|false|The rules for the group by.|
|» options|body|[RUMQueryOptions](#schemarumqueryoptions)|false|Global query options that are used during the query.<br>Note: Only supply timezone or time offset, not both. Otherwise, the query fails.|
|» page|body|[RUMQueryPageOptions](#schemarumquerypageoptions)|false|Paging attributes for listing events.|

> Example responses

```json
  "data": {
    "buckets": [

        }
      }
    ]

    "elapsed": 132,
    "request_id": "abc-123",
    "status": "done"
  }
}
```

## Get a list of RUM events

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/rum/events \
```

`GET /api/v2/rum/events`

List endpoint returns events that match a RUM search query.
[Results are paginated][1].

Use this endpoint to see your latest RUM events.

[1]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/collect-multiple-logs-with-pagination

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-rum-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|Search query following RUM syntax.|
|filter[from]|query|string(date-time)|false|Minimum timestamp for requested events.|

## Search RUM events

<a id="opIdSearchRUMEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/rum/events/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "from": "now-15m",
      "query": "@type:session AND @session.type:user",
      "to": "now"
    },
    "options": {
      "timezone": "GMT"
    },
    "page": {
      "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
      "limit": 25
    },
    "sort": "timestamp"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/rum/events/search`

List endpoint returns RUM events that match a RUM search query.
[Results are paginated][1].

Use this endpoint to build complex RUM events filtering and search.

[1]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/collect-multiple-logs-with-pagination

```json
  "filter": {
    "from": "now-15m",
    "query": "@type:session AND @session.type:user",
    "to": "now"
  },
  "options": {
    "timezone": "GMT"
  },
  "page": {

    "limit": 25
  },
  "sort": "timestamp"
}
```

|» options|body|[RUMQueryOptions](#schemarumqueryoptions)|false|Global query options that are used during the query.<br>Note: Only supply timezone or time offset, not both. Otherwise, the query fails.|
|» page|body|[RUMQueryPageOptions](#schemarumquerypageoptions)|false|Paging attributes for listing events.|
|» sort|body|[RUMSort](#schemarumsort)|false|Sort parameters when querying events.|

## Get a JavaScript source map

<a id="opIdGetSourcemaps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/sourcemaps`

Retrieves the content of a specific JavaScript source map file. Provide either
`debug_id` with a UUID, or all three of `filename`, `service`, and `version`.
When `debug_id` is provided, filename, service, and version are not required
and are ignored.

**Examples:** the following commands use the US1 API host. Replace the host
with the API host for your site, and the filename, service, version, and
debug ID with values from your organization. Use `--get` so curl sends the
parameters in the query string.

**1. Retrieve a source map by debug ID**

Provide `debug_id` with a UUID. No filename, service, or version is required.

```bash
curl -sS --get "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DD_BEARER_TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "debug_id=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
```

**2. Retrieve a source map by service and version**

Provide `filename` together with `service` and `version`.

```bash
curl -sS --get "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DD_BEARER_TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "filename=js/bundle.min.js.map" \
  --data-urlencode "service=my-web-service" \
  --data-urlencode "version=1.0.0"
```

<h3 id="get-a-javascript-source-map-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|debug_id|query|string(uuid)|false|The debug ID of the JavaScript source map, in UUID format. When provided,<br>filename, service, and version are not required and are ignored.|
|filename|query|string|false|The path to the source map file. Required when `debug_id` is omitted.|
|service|query|string|false|The service name associated with the source map. Required when `debug_id` is omitted.|
|version|query|string|false|The version of the service associated with the source map. Required when `debug_id` is omitted.|

> Example responses

```json
  "data": {
    "attributes": {

        50,

      ],

        "console",

      ],
      "sourceRoot": "/",
```

## Delete source maps

<a id="opIdDeleteSourcemaps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps?mapkind=js&dry_run=true' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/sourcemaps`

Deletes source maps matching the specified filter criteria. Supports
dry-run mode to preview which source maps would be deleted without
performing the actual deletion.

<h3 id="delete-source-maps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mapkind|query|[SourcemapMapKind](#schemasourcemapmapkind)|true|The type of source map. Valid values are `js`, `jvm`, `ios`,<br>`react`, `flutter`, `elf`, `ndk`, `il2cpp`, `wasm`, `portable_pdb`.|
|dry_run|query|boolean|true|When set to `true`, returns the source maps that would be deleted<br>without performing the actual deletion. When set to `false`,<br>performs the deletion.|
|filter[service]|query|[string]|false|Filter by service names (multiple values allowed). Required for<br>`js`, `jvm`, `react`, and `flutter` map kinds.|
|filter[version]|query|[string]|false|Filter by version values (multiple values allowed, maximum 10).<br>Required for `js`, `jvm`, `react`, and `flutter` map kinds.|
|filter[variant]|query|[string]|false|Filter by variant values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `jvm`.|
|filter[id]|query|[string]|false|Filter by source map ID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for all map kinds.|
|filter[build_id]|query|[string]|false|Filter by build ID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `jvm`, `ndk`, `il2cpp`, `wasm`, and `portable_pdb`.|
|filter[uuid]|query|[string]|false|Filter by UUID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `ios`.|
|filter[platform]|query|[string]|false|Filter by platform values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|

|filter[arch]|query|[string]|false|Filter by architecture values (multiple values allowed). Supported<br>for `flutter`, `elf`, and `ndk`.|
|filter[symbol_source]|query|[string]|false|Filter by symbol source values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[origin]|query|[string]|false|Filter by origin values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[origin_version]|query|[string]|false|Filter by origin version values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[filename]|query|string|false|Filter by filename (single value). Supported for `js`, `elf`, `ndk`, `wasm`, and `portable_pdb`.|
|filter[debug_id]|query|string|false|Filter by debug ID (single value). Supported for `react`.|

## List source maps

<a id="opIdListSourcemaps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/sourcemaps/list`

Retrieves a paginated list of source maps. Send filters as query parameters,
not in a JSON request body. `mapkind` defaults to `js`.

For JavaScript source maps, choose one of the three request shapes below.

**Examples:** the following commands use the US1 API host. Replace the host with
the API host for your site, and the service, version, debug ID, and cursor with
values from your organization. Use `--get` so curl sends the filters in the query
string; `-X GET` with `--data-urlencode` sends them in the request body instead.

**1. List by service and version**

Provide both `filter[service]` and `filter[version]` to search source maps
indexed by service and version. Omit `search_by`.

**Pagination:** prefer cursor pagination. Omit `page[after]` and `page[number]`
on the first request. To get the next page, pass `meta.page.next_cursor` as
`page[after]`, keeping the same filters. Continue until
`meta.page.has_more_results` is `false`. Do not decode or modify the cursor.
Legacy page-number pagination is also supported, starting at `page[number]=1`.

```bash
curl -sS --get "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps/list" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DD_BEARER_TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "mapkind=js" \
  --data-urlencode "filter[service]=my-web-service" \
  --data-urlencode "filter[version]=1.0.0" \
  --data-urlencode "page[size]=10"
```

**2. Find a specific JavaScript debug ID**

Provide `filter[debug_id]` with a UUID. Service and version filters are not
required. Omit `search_by`.

**Pagination:** the lookup returns at most one result, so no pagination is
needed. `page[after]` is not supported.

```bash
curl -sS --get "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps/list" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DD_BEARER_TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "mapkind=js" \
  --data-urlencode "filter[debug_id]=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
```

**3. Browse source maps indexed by debug ID**

Set `search_by=debug_id` without specifying a debug ID. Do not send service,
version, or filename filters in this mode.

**Pagination:** this mode requires cursor pagination; `page[number]` is not
supported. Omit `page[after]` on the first request. To get the next page, pass
`meta.page.next_cursor` as `page[after]`, keeping the same search mode and
filters. Continue until `meta.page.has_more_results` is `false`. Do not decode
or modify the cursor.

First page:

```bash
curl -sS --get "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps/list" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DD_BEARER_TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "mapkind=js" \
  --data-urlencode "search_by=debug_id" \
  --data-urlencode "page[size]=10"
```

Next page:

```bash
curl -sS --get "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps/list" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DD_BEARER_TOKEN}" \
  --data-urlencode "mapkind=js" \
  --data-urlencode "search_by=debug_id" \
  --data-urlencode "page[size]=10" \
  --data-urlencode "page[after]=<meta.page.next_cursor>"
```

For other map kinds, use `page[number]`, starting at 1.

<h3 id="list-source-maps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|search_by|query|[SourcemapSearchBy](#schemasourcemapsearchby)|false|Set to `debug_id` to browse JavaScript source maps indexed by debug ID.<br>Only supported for `mapkind=js`. Omit for service/version searches or a<br>specific `filter[debug_id]` lookup. In debug-ID browse mode, service,<br>version, and filename filters are not supported.|
|mapkind|query|[SourcemapMapKind](#schemasourcemapmapkind)|false|The type of source map. Defaults to `js`.|
|page[after]|query|string|false|Cursor for the next page of a JavaScript listing. Use the value from<br>`meta.page.next_cursor` and keep the same search mode and filters.<br>Omit on the first request. Not supported for other map kinds or for<br>a specific `filter[debug_id]` lookup without `search_by=debug_id`.|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of results per page. Defaults to 100. Must be at least 1; values above 1000 are capped at 1000.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Legacy page number, starting from 1. Prefer `page[after]` for JavaScript<br>listings. Not supported with `search_by=debug_id`. Other map kinds<br>default to page 1 when pagination parameters are omitted.|
|filter[service]|query|[string]|false|Filter by service names (multiple values allowed). Required for<br>`jvm`, `react`, and `flutter` map kinds. Also required for `js` unless<br>searching by `filter[debug_id]` or browsing with `search_by=debug_id`.|
|filter[version]|query|[string]|false|Filter by version values (multiple values allowed). Required for<br>`jvm`, `react`, and `flutter` map kinds. Also required for `js` unless<br>searching by `filter[debug_id]` or browsing with `search_by=debug_id`.|
|filter[variant]|query|[string]|false|Filter by variant values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `jvm`.|
|filter[id]|query|[string]|false|Filter by source map ID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for all map kinds.|
|filter[build_id]|query|[string]|false|Filter by build ID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `jvm`, `ndk`, `il2cpp`, `wasm`, and `portable_pdb`.|
|filter[uuid]|query|[string]|false|Filter by UUID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `ios`.|
|filter[platform]|query|[string]|false|Filter by platform values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[build_number]|query|[string]|false|Filter by build number values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[bundle_name]|query|[string]|false|Filter by bundle name values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[arch]|query|[string]|false|Filter by architecture values (multiple values allowed). Supported<br>for `flutter`, `elf`, and `ndk`.|
|filter[symbol_source]|query|[string]|false|Filter by symbol source values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[origin]|query|[string]|false|Filter by origin values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[origin_version]|query|[string]|false|Filter by origin version values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[filename]|query|string|false|Filter by filename (single value). Supported for `js`, `elf`, `ndk`, `wasm`, and `portable_pdb`.|
|filter[debug_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by a single debug ID in UUID format. Supported for `js` and `react`.<br>For `js`, the lookup returns at most one result and does not require<br>service/version filters. For `react`, service/version filters remain required.|
|filter[gnu_build_id]|query|string|false|Filter by GNU build ID (single value). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[go_build_id]|query|string|false|Filter by Go build ID (single value). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[file_hash]|query|string|false|Filter by file hash (single value). Supported for `elf`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|search_by|debug_id|
|mapkind|js|
|mapkind|jvm|
|mapkind|ios|
|mapkind|react|
|mapkind|flutter|
|mapkind|elf|
|mapkind|ndk|
|mapkind|il2cpp|
|mapkind|wasm|
|mapkind|portable_pdb|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "debug_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
        "mapkind": "js",
        "size": 1024
      },
      "id": "7",
      "type": "sourcemaps"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page": {
      "has_more_results": true,
      "next_cursor": "opaque-debug-id-cursor",
      "total_filtered_count": 0
    }
  }
}
```

```json
    {
      "detail": "Missing required attribute in body",

        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      },
      "source": {
        "header": "Authorization",
        "parameter": "limit",
```
