## Restore source maps

<a id="opIdRestoreSourcemaps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sourcemaps/restore?mapkind=js&dry_run=true' \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`PATCH /api/v2/sourcemaps/restore`

Restores previously deleted source maps matching the specified filter
criteria. Supports dry-run mode to preview which source maps would be
restored without performing the actual restoration.

<h3 id="restore-source-maps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mapkind|query|[SourcemapMapKind](#schemasourcemapmapkind)|true|The type of source map. Valid values are `js`, `jvm`, `ios`,<br>`react`, `flutter`, `elf`, `ndk`, `il2cpp`, `wasm`, `portable_pdb`.|
|dry_run|query|boolean|true|When set to `true`, returns the source maps that would be restored<br>without performing the actual restoration. When set to `false`,<br>performs the restoration.|
|filter[service]|query|[string]|false|Filter by service names (multiple values allowed). Required for<br>`js`, `jvm`, `react`, and `flutter` map kinds.|
|filter[version]|query|[string]|false|Filter by version values (multiple values allowed, maximum 10).<br>Required for `js`, `jvm`, `react`, and `flutter` map kinds.|
|filter[variant]|query|[string]|false|Filter by variant values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `jvm`.|
|filter[id]|query|[string]|false|Filter by source map ID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for all map kinds.|
|filter[build_id]|query|[string]|false|Filter by build ID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `jvm`, `ndk`, `il2cpp`, `wasm`, and `portable_pdb`.|
|filter[uuid]|query|[string]|false|Filter by UUID values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `ios`.|
|filter[platform]|query|[string]|false|Filter by platform values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[build_number]|query|[string]|false|Filter by build number values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[bundle_name]|query|[string]|false|Filter by bundle name values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[arch]|query|[string]|false|Filter by architecture values (multiple values allowed). Supported<br>for `flutter`, `elf`, and `ndk`.|
|filter[symbol_source]|query|[string]|false|Filter by symbol source values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[origin]|query|[string]|false|Filter by origin values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[origin_version]|query|[string]|false|Filter by origin version values (multiple values allowed). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[filename]|query|string|false|Filter by filename (single value). Supported for `js`, `elf`, `ndk`, `wasm`, and `portable_pdb`.|
|filter[debug_id]|query|string|false|Filter by debug ID (single value). Supported for `react`.|
|filter[gnu_build_id]|query|string|false|Filter by GNU build ID (single value). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[go_build_id]|query|string|false|Filter by Go build ID (single value). Supported for `elf`.|
|filter[file_hash]|query|string|false|Filter by file hash (single value). Supported for `elf`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|mapkind|js|
|mapkind|jvm|
|mapkind|ios|
|mapkind|react|
|mapkind|flutter|
|mapkind|elf|
|mapkind|ndk|
|mapkind|il2cpp|
|mapkind|wasm|
|mapkind|portable_pdb|

> Example responses

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-rum-operations">RUM Operations</h1>

Manage [RUM Operations](https://docs.datadoghq.com/real_user_monitoring/), business
transactions detected from RUM events through a configurable journey, and their links
to journeys. See the [RUM & Session Replay page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/real_user_monitoring/)
for more information.

## Create a RUM operation

<a id="opIdCreateRUMOperation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/rum/operations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "application_id": "abc12345-1234-5678-abcd-ef1234567890",
        "category": "conversion",
        "description": "Tracks users completing the checkout flow.",
        "display_name": "Checkout completed",
        "journey_rum": {
          "rum_steps": [
            {
              "nodes": [
                {
                  "query": "@type:action @action.type:click @action.target.name:\"Checkout\""
                }
              ],
              "type": "start"
            },
            {
              "nodes": [
                {
                  "query": "@type:action @action.type:click @action.target.name:\"Confirm order\""
                }
              ],
              "type": "stop"
            }
          ]
        },
        "name": "checkout_completed",
        "tags": [
          "team:checkout"
        ]
      },
      "type": "operations"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/rum/operations`

`GET /api/v2/rum/operations/search`

|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of items per page. Maximum of 200.|

`POST /api/v2/rum/operations/strong_links`

Create a link between a RUM operation and a journey, confirming that the journey
belongs to the operation. The operation can be identified by `operation_id` or `operation_name`;
if `operation_name` does not match an existing operation, a stub operation is created.

> Body parameter

```json

  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "description": "Confirmed link between checkout_completed and journey-123.",
      "feature_id": "journey-123",

      "status": "CONFIRMED",
```

## Create reference table

<a id="opIdCreateReferenceTable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/reference-tables/tables \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "description": "Customer reference data synced from S3",
        "file_metadata": {
          "access_details": {
            "aws_detail": {
              "aws_account_id": "924305315327",
              "aws_bucket_name": "my-data-bucket",
              "file_path": "customers.csv"
            }
          },
          "sync_enabled": true
        },
        "schema": {
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "customer_id",
              "type": "STRING"
            },
            {
              "name": "customer_name",
              "type": "STRING"
            },
            {
              "name": "email",
              "type": "STRING"
            }
          ],
          "primary_keys": [
            "customer_id"
          ]
        },
        "source": "S3",
        "table_name": "customer_reference_data",
        "tags": [
          "team:data-platform"
        ]
      },
      "type": "reference_table"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/reference-tables/tables`

Creates a reference table. You can provide data in two ways:
1. Call POST /api/v2/reference-tables/upload to get an upload ID. Then, PUT the CSV data
   (not the file itself) in chunks to each URL in the request body. Finally, call this
   POST endpoint with `upload_id` in `file_metadata`.
2. Provide `access_details` in `file_metadata` pointing to a CSV file in cloud storage.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "description": "Customer reference data synced from S3",
      "file_metadata": {
        "access_details": {
          "aws_detail": {
            "aws_account_id": "924305315327",
            "aws_bucket_name": "my-data-bucket",
            "file_path": "customers.csv"
          }
        },
        "sync_enabled": true
      },
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "customer_id",
            "type": "STRING"
          },
          {
            "name": "customer_name",
            "type": "STRING"
          },
          {
            "name": "email",
            "type": "STRING"
          }
        ],
        "primary_keys": [
          "customer_id"
        ]
      },
      "source": "S3",
      "table_name": "customer_reference_data",
      "tags": [
        "team:data-platform"
      ]
    },
    "type": "reference_table"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-reference-table-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateTableRequest](#schemacreatetablerequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[CreateTableRequestData](#schemacreatetablerequestdata)|false|The data object containing the table definition.|

```json
    "attributes": {
      "status": "DONE",
```

## Update reference table

<a id="opIdUpdateReferenceTable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/reference-tables/tables/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "description": "this is a cloud table generated via a cloud bucket sync",
        "file_metadata": {
          "access_details": {
            "aws_detail": {
              "aws_account_id": "test-account-id",
              "aws_bucket_name": "test-bucket",
              "file_path": "test_rt.csv"
            }
          },
          "sync_enabled": true
        },
        "schema": {
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "id",
              "type": "INT32"
            },
            {
              "name": "name",
              "type": "STRING"
            }
          ],
          "primary_keys": [
            "id"
          ]
        },
        "tags": [
          "test_tag"
        ]
      },
      "type": "reference_table"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/reference-tables/tables/{id}`

Update a reference table by ID. You can update the table's data, description, and tags. Note: The source type cannot be changed after table creation. For data updates: For existing tables of type `source:LOCAL_FILE`, call POST api/v2/reference-tables/uploads first to get an upload ID, then PUT chunks of CSV data to each provided URL, and finally call this PATCH endpoint with the upload_id in file_metadata. For existing tables with `source:` types of `S3`, `GCS`, or `AZURE`, provide updated access_details in file_metadata pointing to a CSV file in the same type of cloud storage.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "description": "this is a cloud table generated via a cloud bucket sync",
      "file_metadata": {
        "access_details": {
          "aws_detail": {
            "aws_account_id": "test-account-id",
            "aws_bucket_name": "test-bucket",
            "file_path": "test_rt.csv"
          }
        },
        "sync_enabled": true
      },
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "id",
            "type": "INT32"
          },
          {
            "name": "name",
            "type": "STRING"
          }
        ],
        "primary_keys": [
          "id"
        ]
      },
      "tags": [
        "test_tag"
      ]
    },
    "type": "reference_table"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-reference-table-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the reference table to update|
|body|body|[PatchTableRequest](#schemapatchtablerequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[PatchTableRequestData](#schemapatchtablerequestdata)|false|The data object containing the partial table definition updates.|

## List rows

<a id="opIdListReferenceTableRows"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/reference-tables/tables/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/rows/list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/reference-tables/tables/{id}/rows/list`

List all rows in a reference table using cursor-based pagination. Pass the `page[continuation_token]` from the previous response to fetch the next page on the same consistent snapshot. Returns 400 for tables with more than 10,000,000 rows.

<h3 id="list-rows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the reference table to list rows from.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of rows to return per page. Defaults to 100, maximum is 1000.|
|page[continuation_token]|query|string|false|Opaque cursor from the previous response's next link. Pass this to retrieve the next page on the same consistent snapshot.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "values": {
          "category": "tor",
          "intention": "suspicious",
          "ip_address": "102.130.113.9"
        }
      },
      "id": "102.130.113.9",
      "type": "row"
    }
  ],
  "links": {
    "first": "/api/v2/reference-tables/tables/<TABLE_ID>/rows/list?page[limit]=100",
    "next": "/api/v2/reference-tables/tables/<TABLE_ID>/rows/list?page[continuation_token]=<NEXT_CONTINUATION_TOKEN>",
    "self": "/api/v2/reference-tables/tables/<TABLE_ID>/rows/list?page[continuation_token]=<CONTINUATION_TOKEN>"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]

```

```json
  ]
}
```

```json

  ]
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-report-schedules">Report Schedules</h1>

Create and manage scheduled reports. A scheduled report renders a dashboard or integration
dashboard on a recurring cadence and delivers it to a set of recipients over email, Slack,
or Microsoft Teams.

`GET /api/v2/reporting/dataset/{dataset_id}/schedules`

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/reporting/schedule \

        ],
        "timeframe": "1w",
        "timezone": "America/New_York",
        "title": "Weekly Infrastructure Report"
      },
      "type": "schedule"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/reporting/schedule`

Create a new scheduled report. A schedule renders a dashboard or integration dashboard
on a recurring cadence and delivers it to the configured recipients over email, Slack,
or Microsoft Teams.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-reporting-and-sharing">Reporting And Sharing</h1>

The Reporting and Sharing endpoints allow you to create snapshots of graph widgets and other shareable resources.

## Create a graph snapshot

<a id="opIdCreateSnapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/snapshot \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "additional_config": {
          "template_variables": [
            {
              "name": "host",
              "prefix": "host",
              "values": [
                "web-server-1",
                "web-server-2"
              ]
            }
          ],
          "timeseries_legend_type": "expanded",
          "timezone_offset_minutes": 300
        },
        "end": 1692464800000,
        "height": 185,
        "is_authenticated": false,
        "start": 1692464000000,
        "ttl": "60d",
        "widget_definition": {
          "requests": [
            {
              "q": "avg:system.cpu.user{*}"
            }
          ],
          "type": "timeseries"
        },
        "width": 300
      },
      "type": "create_snapshot"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/snapshot`

Create a snapshot of a graph widget. The snapshot is rendered asynchronously; the returned URL can be polled until the image is ready.

```json
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-restriction-policies">Restriction Policies</h1>

A restriction policy defines the access control rules for a resource, mapping a set of relations
(such as editor and viewer) to a set of allowed principals (such as roles, teams, or users).
The restriction policy determines who is authorized to perform what actions on the resource.

## Get a restriction policy

<a id="opIdGetRestrictionPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/restriction_policy/dashboard%3Aabc-def-ghi \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/restriction_policy/{resource_id}`

Retrieves the restriction policy associated with a specified resource.

<h3 id="get-a-restriction-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource_id|path|string|true|Identifier, formatted as `type:id`. Supported types: `dashboard`, `integration-service`, `integration-webhook`, `notebook`, `powerpack`, `reference-table`, `security-rule`, `slo`, `synthetics-global-variable`, `synthetics-test`, `synthetics-private-location`, `monitor`, `workflow`, `app-builder-app`, `connection`, `connection-group`, `rum-application`, `cross-org-connection`, `spreadsheet`, `on-call-schedule`, `on-call-escalation-policy`, `on-call-team-routing-rules`, `logs-pipeline`, `case-management-project`, `monitor-notification-rule`, `status-page`, `feature-flag`, `network-path-config`.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "bindings": [
        {
          "principals": [
            "role:00000000-0000-1111-0000-000000000000"
          ],
          "relation": "editor"
        }
      ]
    },
    "id": "dashboard:abc-def-ghi",
    "type": "restriction_policy"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-roles">Roles</h1>

The Roles API is used to create and manage Datadog roles, what
[global permissions](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/rbac/)
they grant, and which users belong to them.

Permissions related to specific account assets can be granted to roles
in the Datadog application without using this API. For example, granting
read access on a specific log index to a role can be done in Datadog from the
[Pipelines page](https://app.datadoghq.com/logs/pipelines).

Roles can also be managed in bulk through the Datadog UI, which provides
the capability to assign a single permission to multiple roles simultaneously.

## Update a role

<a id="opIdUpdateRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/roles/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "name": "updated-role-name"
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-1111-0000-000000000000",
      "type": "roles"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/roles/{role_id}`

Edit a role. Can only be used with application keys belonging to administrators.

[Restricted permissions](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/rbac/permissions/#restricted-permissions),
such as Dashboards Read and Monitors Read, remain on the role by default, even if they are omitted from
the request. To exclude them, set `default_permissions_opt_out` to `true`.

Omitting the `permissions` relationship from the request leaves the role's existing permissions
unchanged. Sending `"permissions": {"data": []}` removes all permissions except restricted default
permissions, which remain unless `default_permissions_opt_out` is `true`. Some restricted permissions
can only be excluded after Minimal Access Roles is enabled for the organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "name": "updated-role-name"
    },
    "id": "00000000-0000-1111-0000-000000000000",
    "type": "roles"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the role.|
|body|body|[RoleUpdateRequest](#schemaroleupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[RoleUpdateData](#schemaroleupdatedata)|true|Data related to the update of a role.|

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/rum/config/metrics/string \
```

## Bulk create and remove teams ownership mappings

<a id="opIdCreateTeamsOwnershipMappingsBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/rum/config/teams-ownership/mappings/operations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "atomic:operations": [
      {
        "data": {
          "attributes": {
            "application_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
            "match_type": "exact",
            "service": "web-checkout",
            "team_handle": "team-rum",
            "view_name": "/checkout"
          },
          "type": "teams_ownership_mappings"
        },
        "op": "add"
      },
      {
        "op": "remove",
        "ref": {
          "id": "456",
          "type": "teams_ownership_mappings"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/rum/config/teams-ownership/mappings/operations`

Add and remove teams ownership mappings for your organization in a single atomic request, following
the JSON:API [atomic operations extension](https://jsonapi.org/ext/atomic/).
Operations are applied together: if any operation is invalid, none of the operations are applied.
Add operations are processed before remove operations, so results may not appear in the same
order as the request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "atomic:operations": [
    {
      "data": {
        "attributes": {
          "application_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
          "match_type": "exact",
          "service": "web-checkout",
          "team_handle": "team-rum",
          "view_name": "/checkout"
        },
        "type": "teams_ownership_mappings"
      },
      "op": "add"
    },
    {
      "op": "remove",
      "ref": {
        "id": "456",
        "type": "teams_ownership_mappings"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-create-and-remove-teams-ownership-mappings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TeamsOwnershipMappingBatchRequest](#schemateamsownershipmappingbatchrequest)|true|The list of add and remove operations to apply atomically.|
|» atomic:operations|body|[[TeamsOwnershipMappingBatchOperation](#schemateamsownershipmappingbatchoperation)]|true|The list of add and remove operations to apply atomically.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "atomic:results": [
    {
      "data": {
        "attributes": {
          "application_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
          "created_at": "2026-01-15T09:30:00.000Z",
          "created_by": "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee",
          "match_type": "exact",
          "org_id": 123456,
          "service": "web-checkout",
          "team_handle": "team-rum",
          "view_name": "/checkout"
        },
        "id": "123",
        "type": "teams_ownership_mappings"
      }
    },
    {}
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "prefix match_type is not enabled for this org",
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

`GET /api/v2/scorecard/scores/{aggregation}`

Returns a list of scorecard scores for each aggregation type, with score breakdowns.

<h3 id="list-all-scores-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregation|path|[ScorecardScoresAggregation](#schemascorecardscoresaggregation)|true|The type of scores being requested.|
|filter[rule][id]|query|string|false|Filter scores by rule ID(s), comma-separated.|
|filter[rule][name]|query|string|false|Filter scores by rule name.|
|filter[rule][level]|query|string|false|Filter scores by rule level(s), comma-separated.|
|filter[rule][scorecard_id]|query|string|false|Filter scores by scorecard ID(s), comma-separated.|
|filter[rule][is_custom]|query|boolean|false|Filter scores to show only custom rules.|
|filter[rule][is_enabled]|query|boolean|false|Filter scores to show only enabled rules.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort scores by field. Use a hyphen prefix for descending order. Options: score, numerator, denominator, total_pass, total_fail, total_skip, total_no_data.|
|page[offset]|query|integer(int64)|false|Offset for pagination.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of scores to return. Max is 1000.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

## List findings

<a id="opIdListFindings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/posture_management/findings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/posture_management/findings`

Get a list of findings. These include both misconfigurations and identity risks.

**Note**: To filter and return only identity risks, add the following query parameter: `?filter[tags]=dd_rule_type:ciem`

### Filtering

Filters can be applied by appending query parameters to the URL.

  - Using a single filter: `?filter[attribute_key]=attribute_value`
  - Chaining filters: `?filter[attribute_key]=attribute_value&filter[attribute_key]=attribute_value...`
  - Filtering on tags: `?filter[tags]=tag_key:tag_value&filter[tags]=tag_key_2:tag_value_2`

Here, `attribute_key` can be any of the filter keys described further below.

Query parameters of type `integer` support comparison operators (`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`). This is particularly useful when filtering by `evaluation_changed_at` or `resource_discovery_timestamp`. For example: `?filter[evaluation_changed_at]=>20123123121`.

You can also use the negation operator on strings. For example, use `filter[resource_type]=-aws*` to filter for any non-AWS resources.

The operator must come after the equal sign. For example, to filter with the `>=` operator, add the operator after the equal sign: `filter[evaluation_changed_at]=>=1678809373257`.

Query parameters must be only among the documented ones and with values of correct types. Duplicated query parameters (e.g. `filter[status]=low&filter[status]=info`) are not allowed.

### Additional extension fields

Additional extension fields are available for some findings.

The data is available when you include the query parameter `?detailed_findings=true` in the request.

The following fields are available for findings:
- `external_id`: The resource external ID related to the finding.
- `description`: The description and remediation steps for the finding.
- `datadog_link`: The Datadog relative link for the finding.
- `ip_addresses`: The list of private IP addresses for the resource related to the finding.

### Response

The response includes an array of finding objects, pagination metadata, and a count of items that match the query.

Each finding object contains the following:

- The finding ID that can be used in a `GetFinding` request to retrieve the full finding details.
- Core attributes, including status, evaluation, high-level resource details, muted state, and rule details.
- `evaluation_changed_at` and `resource_discovery_date` time stamps.
- An array of associated tags.

<h3 id="list-findings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Limit the number of findings returned. Must be <= 1000.|
|snapshot_timestamp|query|integer(int64)|false|Return findings for a given snapshot of time (Unix ms).|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Return the next page of findings pointed to by the cursor.|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Return findings that have these associated tags (repeatable).|
|filter[evaluation_changed_at]|query|string|false|Return findings that have changed from pass to fail or vice versa on a specified date (Unix ms) or date range (using comparison operators).|
|filter[muted]|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` to return findings that are muted. Set to `false` to return unmuted findings.|
|filter[rule_id]|query|string|false|Return findings for the specified rule ID.|
|filter[rule_name]|query|string|false|Return findings for the specified rule.|
|filter[resource_type]|query|string|false|Return only findings for the specified resource type.|
|filter[@resource_id]|query|string|false|Return only findings for the specified resource id.|
|filter[discovery_timestamp]|query|string|false|Return findings that were found on a specified date (Unix ms) or date range (using comparison operators).|
|filter[evaluation]|query|[FindingEvaluation](#schemafindingevaluation)|false|Return only `pass` or `fail` findings.|
|filter[status]|query|[FindingStatus](#schemafindingstatus)|false|Return only findings with the specified status.|
|filter[vulnerability_type]|query|[[FindingVulnerabilityType](#schemafindingvulnerabilitytype)]|false|Return findings that match the selected vulnerability types (repeatable).|
|detailed_findings|query|boolean|false|Return additional fields for some findings.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[evaluation]|pass|
|filter[evaluation]|fail|
|filter[status]|critical|
|filter[status]|high|
|filter[status]|medium|
|filter[status]|low|
|filter[status]|info|
|filter[vulnerability_type]|misconfiguration|
|filter[vulnerability_type]|attack_path|
|filter[vulnerability_type]|identity_risk|
|filter[vulnerability_type]|api_security|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
    {
```

`GET /api/v2/security/findings`

Get a list of security findings that match a search query. [See the schema for security findings](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/guide/findings-schema/).

### Query Syntax

This endpoint uses the logs query syntax. Findings attributes (living in the attributes.attributes. namespace) are prefixed by @ when queried. Tags are queried without a prefix.

Example: `@severity:(critical OR high) @status:open team:platform`

<h3 id="list-security-findings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|The search query following log search syntax.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Get the next page of results with a cursor provided in the previous query.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of findings in the response.|
|sort|query|[SecurityFindingsSort](#schemasecurityfindingssort)|false|Sorts by @detection_changed_at.|

|sort|@detection_changed_at|
|sort|-@detection_changed_at|

`PATCH /api/v2/security/findings/assignee`

Assign or unassign security findings.
You can assign up to 100 security findings per request. Set `assignee_id` to the unique identifier of the Datadog user you want to assign the findings to. Omit `assignee_id` (or set it to `null`) to unassign the findings. Per-finding warnings and failures are returned in the response `meta` object.

> Body parameter

```json
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "assignee_id": "f315bdaf-9ee7-4808-a9c1-99c15bf0f4d0"
    },
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "relationships": {

        "data": [
          {
            "id": "ZGVmLTAwcC1pZXJ-aS0wZjhjNjMyZDNmMzRlZTgzNw==",
            "type": "findings"

    "type": "assignee"
  }
}
```

`DELETE /api/v2/security/findings/cases`

Detach security findings from their case.
This operation dissociates security findings from their associated cases without deleting the cases themselves. You can detach security findings from multiple different cases in a single request, with a limit of 50 security findings per request. Security findings that are not currently attached to any case will be ignored.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "c1234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef",
    "relationships": {
      "findings": {
        "data": [
          {
            "id": "ZGVmLTAwcC1pZXJ-aS0wZjhjNjMyZDNmMzRlZTgzNw==",
            "type": "findings"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "type": "cases"

}
```

```bash
      },
```


`PATCH /api/v2/security/findings/mute`

Mute or unmute security findings.
You can mute or unmute up to 100 security findings per request. The request body must include `is_muted` and `reason` attributes. The allowed reasons depend on whether the finding is being muted or unmuted:
  - To mute a finding: `PENDING_FIX`, `FALSE_POSITIVE`, `OTHER`, `NO_FIX`, `DUPLICATE`, `RISK_ACCEPTED`.
  - To unmute a finding: `NO_PENDING_FIX`, `HUMAN_ERROR`, `NO_LONGER_ACCEPTED_RISK`, `OTHER`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "mute": {
        "description": "To be resolved later.",
        "expire_at": 1778721573794,
        "is_muted": true,
        "reason": "RISK_ACCEPTED"
      }
    },
    "relationships": {
      "findings": {
        "data": [
          {
            "id": "ZGVmLTAwcC1pZXJ-aS0wZjhjNjMyZDNmMzRlZTgzNw==",
            "type": "findings"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "type": "mute"
  }
}
```

`POST /api/v2/security/findings/search`

Get a list of security findings that match a search query. [See the schema for security findings](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/guide/findings-schema/).

### Query Syntax

The API uses the logs query syntax. Findings attributes (living in the attributes.attributes. namespace) are prefixed by @ when queried. Tags are queried without a prefix.

Example: `@severity:(critical OR high) @status:open team:platform`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "filter": "@severity:(critical OR high) @status:open team:platform",
      "page": {
        "cursor": "eyJhZnRlciI6IkF3QUFBWnPcm1pd0FBQUJbVlBQUKBa1pqRTVdZUzSTBNemN0YWiIsLTE3Mjk0MzYwMjFdfQ==",
        "limit": 25
      },
      "sort": "@detection_changed_at"
    }
  }
}
```

`POST /api/v2/security/findings/servicenow_tickets`

This operation creates a case in Datadog and a ServiceNow ticket linked to that case for bidirectional sync between Datadog and ServiceNow. Security findings that are already attached to another ServiceNow ticket will be detached from their previous ServiceNow ticket and attached to the newly created ServiceNow ticket.

## Override the severity of security findings

<a id="opIdUpdateFindingsSeverity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security/findings/severity \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "severity": {
          "action": "set",
          "description": "Database contains sensitive data.",
          "value": "high"
        }
      },
      "relationships": {
        "findings": {
          "data": [
            {
              "id": "ZGVmLTAwcC1pZXJ-aS0wZjhjNjMyZDNmMzRlZTgzNw==",
              "type": "findings"
            },
            {
              "id": "ZGVmLTAwMC0wYmd-MDE4NjcyMDJkMzE4MDE5ODY5MGE4ZmQ2MmFlMjg0Y2M=",
              "type": "findings"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "severity_override"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/security/findings/severity`

Set or clear the manual severity override of security findings.

You can update up to 100 security findings per request.
Use the `set` action with a `value` to apply a manual severity override.
`value` is required for `set` and must be omitted for `clear`.
The `info` value sets the lowest severity the finding type allows.
Use the `clear` action to remove a manual severity override.
`clear` does not remove a severity set by an automation rule.
The optional `description` is accepted with both actions and has a limit of 280 characters.

Auto-closed findings are excluded.
Findings whose severity was set by an automation rule are skipped and listed in the response `meta.warnings`.
If every finding is skipped this way, the request fails with a `400` error.
Findings that cannot be found are skipped without a warning.
The request fails with a `404` error only if none of the findings can be found.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "severity": {
        "action": "set",
        "description": "Database contains sensitive data.",
        "value": "high"
      }
    },
    "relationships": {
      "findings": {
        "data": [
          {
            "id": "ZGVmLTAwcC1pZXJ-aS0wZjhjNjMyZDNmMzRlZTgzNw==",
            "type": "findings"
          },
          {
            "id": "ZGVmLTAwMC0wYmd-MDE4NjcyMDJkMzE4MDE5ODY5MGE4ZmQ2MmFlMjg0Y2M=",
            "type": "findings"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "type": "severity_override"
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SeverityOverrideRequest](#schemaseverityoverriderequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[SeverityOverrideRequestData](#schemaseverityoverriderequestdata)|true|Data of the severity override request.|

> Example responses

## List assets SBOMs

<a id="opIdListAssetsSBOMs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security/sboms \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security/sboms`

Get a list of assets SBOMs for an organization.

The `filter[asset_type]` parameter is required for initial requests (when no `page[token]` is provided).
Subsequent pages encode the asset type in the pagination token, so `filter[asset_type]` is not required
for paginated requests. Mixing infrastructure asset types (`Host`, `HostImage`, `Image`, `ServerlessFunction`)
with code asset types (`Repository`, `Service`) in the same request is not supported and returns a 400 error.

### Pagination

Please review the [Pagination section](#pagination) for the "List Vulnerabilities" endpoint.

### Filtering

Please review the [Filtering section](#filtering) for the "List Vulnerabilities" endpoint.

### Metadata

Please review the [Metadata section](#metadata) for the "List Vulnerabilities" endpoint.

<h3 id="list-assets-sboms-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[token]|query|string|false|Its value must come from the `links` section of the response of the first request. Do not manually edit it.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|The page number to be retrieved. It should be equal to or greater than 1.|
|filter[asset_type]|query|[AssetType](#schemaassettype)|false|The type of the assets for the SBOM request. Required for initial requests (when no `page[token]` is provided). Infrastructure types (`Host`, `HostImage`, `Image`, `ServerlessFunction`) and code types (`Repository`, `Service`) cannot be mixed in the same request.|
|filter[asset_name]|query|string|false|The name of the asset for the SBOM request.|
|filter[package_name]|query|string|false|The name of the component that is a dependency of an asset.|
|filter[package_version]|query|string|false|The version of the component that is a dependency of an asset.|
|filter[license_name]|query|string|false|The software license name of the component that is a dependency of an asset.|
|filter[license_type]|query|[SBOMComponentLicenseType](#schemasbomcomponentlicensetype)|false|The software license type of the component that is a dependency of an asset.|

## List scanned assets metadata

<a id="opIdListScannedAssetsMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security/scanned-assets-metadata \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security/scanned-assets-metadata`

Get a list of security scanned assets metadata for an organization.

### Pagination

For the "List Vulnerabilities" endpoint, see the [Pagination section](#pagination).

### Filtering

For the "List Vulnerabilities" endpoint, see the [Filtering section](#filtering).

### Metadata

 For the "List Vulnerabilities" endpoint, see the [Metadata section](#metadata).

### Related endpoints

This endpoint returns additional metadata for cloud resources that is not available from the standard resource endpoints. To access a richer dataset, call this endpoint together with the relevant resource endpoint(s) and merge (join) their results using the resource identifier.

**Hosts**

To enrich host data, join the response from the [Hosts](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/hosts/) endpoint with the response from the scanned-assets-metadata endpoint on the following key fields:

| ENDPOINT | JOIN KEY | TYPE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [/api/v1/hosts](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/hosts/) | host_list.host_name | string |
| /api/v2/security/scanned-assets-metadata | data.attributes.asset.name | string |

**Host Images**

To enrich host image data, join the response from the [Hosts](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/hosts/) endpoint with the response from the scanned-assets-metadata endpoint on the following key fields:

| ENDPOINT | JOIN KEY | TYPE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [/api/v1/hosts](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/hosts/) | host_list.tags_by_source["Amazon Web Services"]["image"] | string |
| /api/v2/security/scanned-assets-metadata | data.attributes.asset.name | string |

**Container Images**

To enrich container image data, join the response from the [Container Images](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/container-images/) endpoint with the response from the scanned-assets-metadata endpoint on the following key fields:

| ENDPOINT | JOIN KEY | TYPE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [/api/v2/container_images](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/container-images/) | `data.attributes.name`@`data.attributes.repo_digest` | string |
| /api/v2/security/scanned-assets-metadata | data.attributes.asset.name | string |

<h3 id="list-scanned-assets-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[token]|query|string|false|Its value must come from the `links` section of the response of the first request. Do not manually edit it.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|The page number to be retrieved. It should be equal to or greater than 1.|
|filter[asset.type]|query|[CloudAssetType](#schemacloudassettype)|false|The type of the scanned asset.|
|filter[asset.name]|query|string|false|The name of the scanned asset.|
|filter[last_success.origin]|query|string|false|The origin of last success scan.|
|filter[last_success.env]|query|string|false|The environment of last success scan.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[asset.type]|Host|
|filter[asset.type]|HostImage|
|filter[asset.type]|Image|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "asset": {
```

## List vulnerabilities

<a id="opIdListVulnerabilities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security/vulnerabilities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security/vulnerabilities`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Get a list of vulnerabilities.

### Pagination

Pagination is enabled by default in both `vulnerabilities` and `assets`. The size of the page varies depending on the endpoint and cannot be modified. To automate the request of the next page, you can use the links section in the response.

This endpoint will return paginated responses. The pages are stored in the links section of the response:

```JSON
{
  "data": [...],
  "meta": {...},
  "links": {
    "self": "https://.../api/v2/security/vulnerabilities",
    "first": "https://.../api/v2/security/vulnerabilities?page[number]=1&page[token]=abc",
    "last": "https://.../api/v2/security/vulnerabilities?page[number]=43&page[token]=abc",
    "next": "https://.../api/v2/security/vulnerabilities?page[number]=2&page[token]=abc"
  }
}
```


- `links.previous` is empty if the first page is requested.
- `links.next` is empty if the last page is requested.

#### Token

Vulnerabilities can be created, updated or deleted at any point in time.

Upon the first request, a token is created to ensure consistency across subsequent paginated requests.

A token is valid only for 24 hours.

#### First request

We consider a request to be the first request when there is no `page[token]` parameter.

The response of this first request contains the newly created token in the `links` section.

This token can then be used in the subsequent paginated requests.

*Note: The first request may take longer to complete than subsequent requests.*

#### Subsequent requests

Any request containing valid `page[token]` and `page[number]` parameters will be considered a subsequent request.

If the `token` is invalid, a `404` response will be returned.

If the page `number` is invalid, a `400` response will be returned.

The returned `token` is valid for all requests in the pagination sequence. To send paginated requests in parallel, reuse the same `token` and change only the `page[number]` parameter.

### Filtering

The request can include some filter parameters to filter the data to be retrieved. The format of the filter parameters follows the [JSON:API format](https://jsonapi.org/format/#fetching-filtering): `filter[$prop_name]`, where `prop_name` is the property name in the entity being filtered by.

All filters can include multiple values, where data will be filtered with an OR clause: `filter[title]=Title1,Title2` will filter all vulnerabilities where title is equal to `Title1` OR `Title2`.

String filters are case sensitive.

Boolean filters accept `true` or `false` as values.

Number filters must include an operator as a second filter input: `filter[$prop_name][$operator]`. For example, for the vulnerabilities endpoint: `filter[cvss.base.score][lte]=8`.

Available operators are: `eq` (==), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), `gt` (>) and `gte` (>=).

### Metadata

Following [JSON:API format](https://jsonapi.org/format/#document-meta), object including non-standard meta-information.

This endpoint includes the meta member in the response. For more details on each of the properties included in this section, check the endpoints response tables.

```JSON
{
  "data": [...],
  "meta": {
    "total": 1500,
    "count": 18732,
    "token": "some_token"
  },
  "links": {...}
}
```
### Extensions

Requests may include extensions to modify the behavior of the requested endpoint. The filter parameters follow the [JSON:API format](https://jsonapi.org/extensions/#extensions) format: `ext:$extension_name`, where `extension_name` is the name of the modifier that is being applied.

Extensions can only include one value: `ext:modifier=value`.

<h3 id="list-vulnerabilities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[token]|query|string|false|Its value must come from the `links` section of the response of the first request. Do not manually edit it.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|The page number to be retrieved. It should be equal or greater than `1`|
|filter[type]|query|[VulnerabilityType](#schemavulnerabilitytype)|false|Filter by vulnerability type.|

## Import security vulnerabilities

<a id="opIdImportSecurityVulnerabilities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security/vulnerabilities \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
    "components": [
      {
        "bom-ref": "a3390fca-c315-41ae-ae05-af5e7859cdee",
        "name": "lodash",
        "purl": "pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.21",
        "type": "library",
        "version": "4.17.21"
      }
    ],
    "metadata": {
      "component": {
        "name": "i-12345",
        "type": "operating-system"
      },
      "tools": {
        "components": [
          {
            "name": "my-scanner",
            "type": "application"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "specVersion": "1.5",
    "version": 1,
    "vulnerabilities": [
      {
        "affects": [
          {
            "ref": "a3390fca-c315-41ae-ae05-af5e7859cdee"
          }
        ],
        "description": "Sample vulnerability detected in the application.",
        "id": "CVE-2021-1234",
        "ratings": [
          {
            "score": 9,
            "severity": "high",
            "vector": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/security/vulnerabilities`

Import security vulnerabilities from an external scanner in CycloneDX 1.5 format.

The payload is validated against the CycloneDX 1.5 JSON schema and the following
additional constraints:

- `metadata`, `metadata.component`, and `metadata.component.name` are required.
- `metadata.tools.components` must contain exactly one element with a `name` field.
- `components` cannot be empty. Each component requires `bom-ref`, `type`, `name`, and `version`.
- When `type` is `library`, `purl` is required and must be a valid PURL.
- When `type` is `operating-system`, `name` must be one of the supported OS values:
  `alma`, `alpine`, `amazon`, `azurelinux`, `bottlerocket`, `cbl-mariner`, `chainguard`,
  `centos`, `debian`, `fedora`, `opensuse`, `opensuse-leap`, `opensuse-tumbleweed`,
  `oracle`, `photon`, `redhat`, `rocky`, `slem`, `sles`, `ubuntu`, `wolfi`, `windows`, `macos`.
- `vulnerabilities` cannot be empty. Each vulnerability requires `id`, exactly one `ratings` entry,
  and at least one `affects` entry.
- Each `affects[].ref` must match a `bom-ref` value in `components`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
  "components": [
    {
      "bom-ref": "a3390fca-c315-41ae-ae05-af5e7859cdee",
      "name": "lodash",
      "purl": "pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.21",
      "type": "library",
      "version": "4.17.21"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "component": {
      "name": "i-12345",
      "type": "operating-system"
    },
    "tools": {
      "components": [
        {
          "name": "my-scanner",
          "type": "application"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "specVersion": "1.5",
  "version": 1,
  "vulnerabilities": [
    {
      "affects": [
        {
          "ref": "a3390fca-c315-41ae-ae05-af5e7859cdee"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Sample vulnerability detected in the application.",
      "id": "CVE-2021-1234",
      "ratings": [
        {
          "score": 9,
          "severity": "high",
          "vector": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="import-security-vulnerabilities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CycloneDXBom](#schemacyclonedxbom)|true|none|
|» bomFormat|body|string|true|The BOM format identifier. Must be `CycloneDX`.|
|» components|body|[[CycloneDXComponent](#schemacyclonedxcomponent)]|true|The list of scanned software components. Cannot be empty.|

|» version|body|integer(int64)|false|The version number of the BOM document.|
|» vulnerabilities|body|[[CycloneDXVulnerability](#schemacyclonedxvulnerability)]|true|The list of detected vulnerabilities. Cannot be empty.|

## List batch migrations

<a id="opIdListSecurityMonitoringBatchMigrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations`

List the batch migrations of your organization. A batch migration groups detection
rules from another SIEM that the Datadog Detection Agent translates into Cloud SIEM
detection rules. To retrieve a single batch migration, filter by its ID with
`filter[query]=id:<batch_id>`. Poll this endpoint to follow the progress of a batch
migration through its `status` and `resourceStatusCounts`.

<h3 id="list-batch-migrations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Size for a given page. The maximum allowed value is 500.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Specific page number to return, starting at 1.|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|A search query in Datadog search syntax to filter batch migrations, such as<br>`status:completed`. Filterable attributes are `id`, `name`, `description`, `status`,<br>`createdBy`, and `lastUpdatedBy`. Free text matches the batch migration name.|

## Create a batch migration

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations \

    "data": {
      "attributes": {

        "name": "Splunk migration",
        "resources": [
          {

    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations`

Create a batch migration in the `draft` status, together with 1 to 100 initial
resources. Each resource holds one source rule to translate into a Cloud SIEM detection
rule. To load more rules, add them with the add resources endpoint before starting the
batch migration. A batch migration can hold up to 1000 resources. The response does not
include the created resources: list the resources of the batch migration to retrieve them.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "description": "Rules imported from Splunk",
      "name": "Splunk migration",
      "resources": [
        {
          "description": "Detects repeated failed Windows authentication attempts.",
          "input": "index=wineventlog EventCode=4625",
          "inputType": "spl",
          "name": "Repeated Windows login failures"
        },
        {
          "input": "Alert when PowerShell is launched with a command line that downloads and executes a remote script, such as IEX with Net.WebClient or Invoke-WebRequest.",

          "name": "Suspicious PowerShell download cradle"
        }
      ],
      "tags": [
        "source:splunk"
      ]

    "type": "batchMigration"
  }
}
```

## Cancel a batch migration

<a id="opIdCancelSecurityMonitoringBatchMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations/7cdb3a75-64fb-46ce-9445-41969e78fe8e/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations/{batch_id}/cancel`

Cancel an `in_progress` batch migration. Resources that are `pending` or `in_progress`
become `canceled`. Resources that are already `completed` or `failed` keep their status
and output, so completed resources can still be published. Canceling a `canceled` batch
migration succeeds, so the request can be safely retried. Returns `409 Conflict` if the
batch migration is `draft` or `completed`.

## Publish a batch migration

<a id="opIdPublishSecurityMonitoringBatchMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations/7cdb3a75-64fb-46ce-9445-41969e78fe8e/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {},
      "type": "batchMigrationPublish"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations/{batch_id}/publish`

Create a Cloud SIEM detection rule from the `output` of each selected `completed`
resource of a batch migration. Completed resources can be published while the rest of
the batch migration is still being translated. When `resourceIds` is omitted or empty,
every `completed` resource is published. Published rules are created disabled.

Every requested resource must be publishable: `completed`, or left in `publishing` for
more than one minute after an uncertain result. Otherwise, the request returns
`409 Conflict` and nothing is published. Already published resources are not publishable.

The response reports the outcome of each resource, and some resources can be published
while others fail. A `failed` result that contains a `ruleId` means the rule was created:
do not retry that resource. Publishing a rule with a `block_ip` or `block_user` action
requires the `appsec_protect_write` permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {},
    "type": "batchMigrationPublish"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="publish-a-batch-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batch_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The UUID of the batch migration.|
|body|body|[SecurityMonitoringBatchMigrationPublishRequest](#schemasecuritymonitoringbatchmigrationpublishrequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[SecurityMonitoringBatchMigrationPublishData](#schemasecuritymonitoringbatchmigrationpublishdata)|true|Data of the batch migration publish request.|

```json
  "data": [
```

## Start a batch migration

<a id="opIdStartSecurityMonitoringBatchMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations/7cdb3a75-64fb-46ce-9445-41969e78fe8e/start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/batch-migrations/{batch_id}/start`

Start translating the `pending` resources of a `draft` batch migration into Cloud SIEM
detection rules. The batch migration moves to `in_progress`, and its resources are
translated asynchronously. Once no resource is `pending` or `in_progress`, the batch
migration moves to `completed`. Starting an `in_progress` batch migration again does not
queue duplicate work, so the request can be safely retried, including after a timeout or
a `5xx` error. Returns `409 Conflict` if the batch migration is `completed` or `canceled`.

An organization can translate up to 2000 resources in total across all of its batch
migrations. Resources that were already processed count toward this limit even after
they are deleted, and `pending` resources of `in_progress` batch migrations reserve
capacity. Returns `409 Conflict` if starting the batch migration would exceed this limit.
To request a higher limit for your organization, contact
[Datadog support](https://docs.datadoghq.com/help/).

```json
      }
```

```bash
        "action": "require"
      }

      "service"

    "options": {
      "anomalyDetectionOptions": {
        "bucketDuration": 300,
        "detectionTolerance": 5,
        "instantaneousBaseline": false
      },
      "complianceRuleOptions": {
        "regoRule": {
          "policy": "package datadog\n\nimport data.datadog.output as dd_output\nimport future.keywords.contains\nimport future.keywords.if\nimport future.keywords.in\n\neval(resource) = \"skip\" if {\n  # Logic that evaluates to true if the resource should be skipped\n  true\n} else = \"pass\" {\n  # Logic that evaluates to true if the resource is compliant\n  true\n} else = \"fail\" {\n  # Logic that evaluates to true if the resource is not compliant\n  true\n}\n\n# This part remains unchanged for all rules\nresults contains result if {\n  some resource in input.resources[input.main_resource_type]\n  result := dd_output.format(resource, eval(resource))\n}",

      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "tags": [
      "env:prod",
      "team:security"
    ],
    "thirdPartyCases": [],

  }'
```

## Get entity context

<a id="opIdGetEntityContext"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/entity_context \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security_monitoring/entity_context`

Search the Cloud SIEM entity context store for entities that match a query, and return the historical
revisions of each entity in the requested time range. The endpoint can either return revisions across an
interval (`from` / `to`) or the snapshot of each entity at a single point in time (`as_of`); the two modes
are mutually exclusive.

<h3 id="get-entity-context-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|A free-text query (for example, an email address or principal ID) used to filter the entities returned.|
|entity_type|query|[EntityContextEntityType](#schemaentitycontextentitytype)|false|The type of entity to retrieve. Only `siem_entity_identity` is currently supported.<br>Defaults to `siem_entity_identity`.|
|from|query|string|false|The start of the time range to query, as an RFC3339 timestamp or a relative time (for example, `now-7d`).<br>Defaults to `now-7d`. Ignored when `as_of` is set.|
|to|query|string|false|The end of the time range to query, as an RFC3339 timestamp or a relative time (for example, `now`).<br>Defaults to `now`. Ignored when `as_of` is set.|
|as_of|query|string|false|A point in time at which to query the entity revisions, as an RFC3339 timestamp, a Unix timestamp<br>(in seconds), or a relative time (for example, `now-1d`). When set, `from` and `to` are ignored.<br>Cannot be combined with custom `from` / `to` values.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of entities to return.|
|page_token|query|string|false|An opaque token used to fetch the next page of results, as returned in `meta.page.next_token` of a previous response.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entity_type|siem_entity_identity|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "revisions": [
          {
            "attributes": {
              "accounts": [
                "linked-account-123"
              ],
              "display_name": "Test User",
              "email": "user@example.com",
              "principal_id": "user@example.com"
            },
            "first_seen_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
            "last_seen_at": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"
          }
        ]
      },
      "id": "user@example.com",
      "type": "siem_entity_identity"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page": {
      "next_token": ""
    },
    "total_count": 1
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-entity-context-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[EntityContextResponse](#schemaentitycontextresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Not Authorized|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKeyAuth & appKeyAuth, AuthZ ( Scopes: siem_entities_read )
</aside>

## Get recently updated entity context

<a id="opIdGetEntityContextRecentlyUpdated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/entity_context/recently_updated \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security_monitoring/entity_context/recently_updated`

Get the entities with the most recent updates in the Cloud SIEM entity context store. Entities are ranked
by the time of their most recent revision in the requested time range, and the top `limit` entities are
returned in that order. This endpoint is not paginated.

<h3 id="get-recently-updated-entity-context-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|A free-text query (for example, an email address or principal ID) used to filter the entities returned.|
|entity_type|query|[EntityContextEntityType](#schemaentitycontextentitytype)|false|The type of entity to retrieve. Only `siem_entity_identity` is currently supported.<br>Defaults to `siem_entity_identity`.|
|from|query|string|false|The start of the time range to query, as an RFC3339 timestamp or a relative time (for example, `now-7d`).<br>Defaults to `now-7d`.|
|to|query|string|false|The end of the time range to query, as an RFC3339 timestamp or a relative time (for example, `now`).<br>Defaults to `now`. Entities are ranked by their most recent revision within `[from, to]`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of entities to return. Must be between 1 and 100.|
|revisions|query|[EntityContextRevisionsMode](#schemaentitycontextrevisionsmode)|false|Which revisions to return for each entity: `latest` returns only the latest revision of each entity as of `to`,<br>and `all` returns every revision in the requested time range.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entity_type|siem_entity_identity|
|revisions|latest|
|revisions|all|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "revisions": [
          {
            "attributes": {
              "accounts": [
                "linked-account-123"
              ],
              "display_name": "Test User",
              "email": "user@example.com",
              "principal_id": "user@example.com"
            },
            "first_seen_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
            "last_seen_at": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"
          }
        ]
      },
      "id": "user@example.com",
      "type": "siem_entity_identity"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-recently-updated-entity-context-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[RecentlyUpdatedEntitiesResponse](#schemarecentlyupdatedentitiesresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Not Authorized|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

`GET /api/v2/security_monitoring/entity_context/{id}`

interval (`from` / `to`) or the snapshot of the entity at a single point in time (`as_of`); the two modes

|from|query|string|false|The start of the time range to query, as an RFC3339 timestamp or a relative time (for example, `now-7d`).<br>Defaults to `now-7d`. Ignored when `as_of` is set.|
|to|query|string|false|The end of the time range to query, as an RFC3339 timestamp or a relative time (for example, `now`).<br>Defaults to `now`. Ignored when `as_of` is set.|
|as_of|query|string|false|A point in time at which to query the entity revisions, as an RFC3339 timestamp, a Unix timestamp<br>(in seconds), or a relative time (for example, `now-1d`). When set, `from` and `to` are ignored.<br>Cannot be combined with custom `from` / `to` values.|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/rules/convert \

  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
```
```bash
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
```
```bash
    "calculatedFields": [
      {
        "expression": "@request_end_timestamp - @request_start_timestamp",
        "name": "response_time"
      }
    ],
    "cases": [
      {
        "condition": "a > 0",
        "name": "",
        "notifications": [],
        "status": "info"
      }
    ],
    "filters": [],
    "groupSignalsBy": [
      "service"
    ],
    "hasExtendedTitle": true,
    "isEnabled": true,
    "message": "My security monitoring rule.",
    "name": "My security monitoring rule.",
    "options": {
      "anomalyDetectionOptions": {
        "bucketDuration": 300,
        "detectionTolerance": 5,
        "instantaneousBaseline": false
      },
      "complianceRuleOptions": {
        "regoRule": {
          "policy": "package datadog\n\nimport data.datadog.output as dd_output\nimport future.keywords.contains\nimport future.keywords.if\nimport future.keywords.in\n\neval(resource) = \"skip\" if {\n  # Logic that evaluates to true if the resource should be skipped\n  true\n} else = \"pass\" {\n  # Logic that evaluates to true if the resource is compliant\n  true\n} else = \"fail\" {\n  # Logic that evaluates to true if the resource is not compliant\n  true\n}\n\n# This part remains unchanged for all rules\nresults contains result if {\n  some resource in input.resources[input.main_resource_type]\n  result := dd_output.format(resource, eval(resource))\n}",
          "resourceTypes": [
            "gcp_iam_service_account",
            "gcp_iam_policy"
          ]
        },
        "resourceType": "aws_acm"
      },
      "decreaseCriticalityBasedOnEnv": false,
      "detectionMethod": "threshold",
      "evaluationWindow": 900,
      "hardcodedEvaluatorType": "log4shell",
      "impossibleTravelOptions": {
        "baselineUserLocations": true,
        "baselineUserLocationsDuration": 7
      },
      "keepAlive": 3600,
      "maxSignalDuration": 86400,
      "newValueOptions": {
        "instantaneousBaseline": false,
        "learningMethod": "duration"
      },
      "thirdPartyRuleOptions": {
        "defaultStatus": "critical",
        "rootQueries": [
          {
            "query": "source:cloudtrail"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "queries": [
      {
        "aggregation": "count",
        "distinctFields": [],
        "groupByFields": [],
        "query": "source:cloudtrail"
      }
    ],
    "schedulingOptions": {
      "rrule": "FREQ=HOURLY;INTERVAL=1;",
      "start": "2025-07-14T12:00:00",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "tags": [
      "env:prod",
      "team:security"
    ],
    "thirdPartyCases": [],
    "type": "log_detection"
  }'
```

## Update an existing rule

<a id="opIdUpdateSecurityMonitoringRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/rules/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "cases": [
      {
        "condition": "a > 0",
        "name": "",
        "notifications": [],
        "status": "info"
      }
    ],
    "filters": [],
    "isEnabled": true,
    "message": "Test rule",
    "name": "My security monitoring rule.",
    "options": {
      "evaluationWindow": 900,
      "keepAlive": 3600,
      "maxSignalDuration": 86400
    },
    "queries": [
      {
        "aggregation": "count",
        "distinctFields": [],
        "groupByFields": [],
        "metrics": [],
        "query": "@test:true"
      }
    ],
    "tags": []
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/security_monitoring/rules/{rule_id}`

Update an existing rule. When updating `cases`, `queries` or `options`, the whole field
must be included. For example, when modifying a query all queries must be included.
Default rules can only be updated to be enabled, to change notifications, or to update
the tags (default tags cannot be removed).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "condition": "a > 0",
      "name": "",
      "notifications": [],
      "status": "info"
    }
  ],
  "filters": [],
  "isEnabled": true,
  "message": "Test rule",
  "name": "My security monitoring rule.",
  "options": {
    "evaluationWindow": 900,
    "keepAlive": 3600,
    "maxSignalDuration": 86400
  },
  "queries": [
    {
      "aggregation": "count",
      "distinctFields": [],
      "groupByFields": [],
      "metrics": [],
      "query": "@test:true"
    }
  ],
  "tags": []
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-existing-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rule_id|path|string|true|The ID of the rule.|
|body|body|[SecurityMonitoringRuleUpdatePayload](#schemasecuritymonitoringruleupdatepayload)|true|none|
|» calculatedFields|body|[[CalculatedField](#schemacalculatedfield)]|false|Calculated fields. Only allowed for scheduled rules - in other words, when schedulingOptions is also defined.|
|» cases|body|[[SecurityMonitoringRuleCase](#schemasecuritymonitoringrulecase)]|false|Cases for generating signals.|
|» complianceSignalOptions|body|[CloudConfigurationRuleComplianceSignalOptions](#schemacloudconfigurationrulecompliancesignaloptions)|false|How to generate compliance signals. Useful for cloud_configuration rules only.|
|» customMessage|body|string|false|Custom/Overridden Message for generated signals (used in case of Default rule update).|
|» customName|body|string|false|Custom/Overridden name (used in case of Default rule update).|
|» filters|body|[[SecurityMonitoringFilter](#schemasecuritymonitoringfilter)]|false|Additional queries to filter matched events before they are processed. This field is deprecated for log detection, signal correlation, and workload security rules.|
|» groupSignalsBy|body|[string]|false|Additional grouping to perform on top of the existing groups in the query section. Must be a subset of the existing groups.|
|» hasExtendedTitle|body|boolean|false|Whether the notifications include the triggering group-by values in their title.|
|» isEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the rule is enabled.|
|» message|body|string|false|Message for generated signals.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the rule.|
|» options|body|[SecurityMonitoringRuleOptions](#schemasecuritymonitoringruleoptions)|false|Options.|
|» queries|body|[[SecurityMonitoringRuleQuery](#schemasecuritymonitoringrulequery)]|false|Queries for selecting logs which are part of the rule.|
|» referenceTables|body|[[SecurityMonitoringReferenceTable](#schemasecuritymonitoringreferencetable)]|false|Reference tables for the rule.|
|» schedulingOptions|body|[SecurityMonitoringSchedulingOptions](#schemasecuritymonitoringschedulingoptions)|false|Options for scheduled rules. When this field is present, the rule runs based on the schedule. When absent, it runs real-time on ingested logs.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for generated signals.|
|» thirdPartyCases|body|[[SecurityMonitoringThirdPartyRuleCase](#schemasecuritymonitoringthirdpartyrulecase)]|false|Cases for generating signals from third-party rules. Only available for third-party rules.|
|» version|body|integer(int32)|false|The version of the rule being updated.|

`GET /api/v2/security_monitoring/rules/{rule_id}/convert`

Convert an existing rule from JSON to Terraform for Datadog provider
resource `datadog_security_monitoring_rule`. You can do so for the following rule types:
- App and API Protection
- Cloud SIEM (log detection and signal correlation)
- Workload Protection

You can convert Cloud Security configuration rules using Terraform's [Datadog Cloud Configuration Rule resource](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/DataDog/datadog/latest/docs/resources/cloud_configuration_rule).

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/rules/{rule_id}/restore/{version}`

## Get sample log generation subscriptions

<a id="opIdListSampleLogGenerationSubscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/sample_log_generation/subscriptions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/security_monitoring/sample_log_generation/subscriptions`

Get the sample log generation subscriptions for the organization.
Sample log generation injects representative example logs for a given Cloud SIEM content pack into the Logs platform,
which can be used to test detection rules without onboarding the underlying integration first.

**Availability**: this endpoint is restricted to Cloud SIEM trial organizations on an eligible
pricing model. Other organizations receive a `403 Forbidden` (non-trial orgs) or a `400 Bad Request`
(feature disabled), and legacy pricing tiers receive a response with `status: not_available`.

<h3 id="get-sample-log-generation-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|query|[SampleLogGenerationSubscriptionsStatusFilter](#schemasampleloggenerationsubscriptionsstatusfilter)|false|Filter the subscriptions by status. Use `active` to return only currently active<br>subscriptions, or `all` to return every subscription including expired ones.<br>Ignored when `start_timestamp` is provided. Defaults to `active`.|
|start_timestamp|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the time range, as an RFC3339 timestamp. When provided, the response includes<br>every subscription that was active at any point in `[start_timestamp, end_timestamp]`,<br>and the `status` filter is ignored.|
|end_timestamp|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the time range, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Ignored unless `start_timestamp` is set.<br>Defaults to the current time when `start_timestamp` is provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|all|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "content_pack_id": "aws-cloudtrail",
        "created_at": "2026-05-08T20:02:13.77481Z",
        "expires_at": "2026-05-11T20:02:13.77481Z",
        "is_active": true,
        "status": "subscribed"
      },
      "id": "999",
      "type": "subscriptions"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_subscriptions": 1
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-sample-log-generation-subscriptions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[SampleLogGenerationSubscriptionsResponse](#schemasampleloggenerationsubscriptionsresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Not Authorized|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

requests with `400 Bad Request`, and legacy pricing tiers receive a response with `status: not_available`.

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/sample_log_generation/subscriptions/bulk`

Subscribe to sample log generation for multiple Cloud SIEM content packs in a single call.
Each requested content pack is processed independently; the response includes a per-item
status so partial successes can be inspected.

**Availability**: this endpoint is restricted to Cloud SIEM trial organizations on an
eligible pricing model. Non-trial orgs receive `403 Forbidden`, the feature flag may also reject
requests with `400 Bad Request`, and legacy pricing tiers receive per-item responses with `status: not_available`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "content_pack_ids": [
        "aws-cloudtrail"
      ],
      "duration": "3d"
    },
    "type": "bulk_subscription_requests"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-subscribe-to-sample-log-generation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» data|body|[SampleLogGenerationBulkSubscriptionData](#schemasampleloggenerationbulksubscriptiondata)|true|The bulk subscription request body.|

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security_monitoring/terraform/suppressions/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/security_monitoring/terraform/{resource_type}/bulk`

Export multiple security monitoring resources to Terraform, packaged as a zip archive.
The `resource_type` path parameter specifies the type of resources to export
and must be one of `suppressions`, `critical_assets`, `security_filters`, or `rules`.
A maximum of 1000 resources can be exported in a single request.
For `rules`, partner rules cannot be exported and return a 400 error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "resource_ids": [
        "abc-123-def"
      ]
    },
    "type": "bulk_export_resources"
  }
}
```
