|body|body|[SecurityMonitoringTerraformBulkExportRequest](#schemasecuritymonitoringterraformbulkexportrequest)|true|The resource IDs to export.|
|» data|body|[SecurityMonitoringTerraformBulkExportData](#schemasecuritymonitoringterraformbulkexportdata)|true|The bulk export request data object.|

## Create Scanning Group

<a id="opIdCreateScanningGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sensitive-data-scanner/config/groups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "filter": {
          "query": "*"
        },
        "is_enabled": false,
        "product_list": [
          "logs"
        ],
        "samplings": [
          {
            "product": "logs",
            "rate": 100
          }
        ]
      },
      "relationships": {
        "configuration": {
          "data": {
            "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_configuration"
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_group"
    },
    "meta": {
      "version": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/sensitive-data-scanner/config/groups`

Create a scanning group.
The request MAY include a configuration relationship.
A rules relationship can be omitted entirely, but if it is included it MUST be
null or an empty array (rules cannot be created at the same time).
The new group will be ordered last within the configuration.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "filter": {
        "query": "*"
      },
      "is_enabled": false,
```

## Create Scanning Rule

<a id="opIdCreateScanningRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/sensitive-data-scanner/config/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \

    "data": {

        "excluded_namespaces": [

        ],
        "included_keyword_configuration": {
          "character_count": 30,
          "keywords": [
            "email",
            "address",
            "login"
          ]
        },
        "is_enabled": true,
        "namespaces": [
          "admin"
        ],
        "suppressions": {
          "ends_with": [
            "@example.com",
            "another.example.com"
          ],
          "exact_match": [
            "admin@example.com",
            "user@example.com"
          ],
          "starts_with": [
            "admin",
            "user"
          ]
        },
        "tags": [
          "sensitive_data:true"
        ],
        "text_replacement": {
          "type": "none"
        }
      },
      "relationships": {
        "group": {
          "data": {
            "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_group"
          }
        },
        "standard_pattern": {
          "data": {
            "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_standard_pattern"
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_rule"
    },
    "meta": {
      "version": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/sensitive-data-scanner/config/rules`

Create a scanning rule in a sensitive data scanner group, ordered last.
The posted rule MUST include a group relationship.
It MUST include either a standard_pattern relationship or a regex attribute, but not both.
If included_attributes is empty or missing, we will scan all attributes except
excluded_attributes. If both are missing, we will scan the whole event.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "excluded_namespaces": [
        "admin.name"
      ],
      "included_keyword_configuration": {
        "character_count": 30,
        "keywords": [
          "email",
          "address",
          "login"
        ]
      },
      "is_enabled": true,
      "namespaces": [
        "admin"
      ],
      "suppressions": {
        "ends_with": [
          "@example.com",
          "another.example.com"
        ],
        "exact_match": [
          "admin@example.com",
          "user@example.com"
        ],
        "starts_with": [
          "admin",
          "user"
        ]
      },
      "tags": [
        "sensitive_data:true"
      ],
      "text_replacement": {
        "type": "none"
      }
    },
    "relationships": {
      "group": {
        "data": {
          "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_group"
        }
      },
      "standard_pattern": {
        "data": {
          "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_standard_pattern"
        }
      }
    },
    "type": "sensitive_data_scanner_rule"
  },
  "meta": {
    "version": 0
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-service-accounts">Service Accounts</h1>

Create, edit, and disable service accounts. See the [Service Accounts page](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/org_settings/service_accounts/) for more information.

## Create a service account

<a id="opIdCreateServiceAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/service_accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
        "service_account": true
      },
      "relationships": {
        "roles": {
          "data": [
            {
              "id": "3653d3c6-0c75-11ea-ad28-fb5701eabc7d"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "users"
    }
  }'
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-service-level-objectives">Service Level Objectives</h1>

[Service Level Objectives](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/service_level_objectives/#configuration)
(SLOs) are a key part of the site reliability engineering toolkit.
SLOs provide a framework for defining clear targets around application performance,
which ultimately help teams provide a consistent customer experience,
balance feature development with platform stability,
and improve communication with internal and external users.

## Create a new SLO report

<a id="opIdCreateSLOReportJob"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/slo/report \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "from_ts": 1690901870,
        "interval": "weekly",
        "query": "slo_type:metric",
        "timezone": "America/New_York",
        "to_ts": 1706803070
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/slo/report`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Create a job to generate an SLO report. The report job is processed asynchronously and eventually results in a CSV report being available for download.

Check the status of the job and download the CSV report using the returned `report_id`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "from_ts": 1690901870,
      "interval": "weekly",
      "query": "slo_type:metric",
      "timezone": "America/New_York",
      "to_ts": 1706803070
    }
  }
}
```

## Get SLO status

<a id="opIdGetSloStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/slo/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/status?from_ts=1690901870&to_ts=1706803070' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/slo/{slo_id}/status`

Get the status of a Service Level Objective (SLO) for a given time period.

This endpoint returns the current SLI value, error budget remaining, and other status information for the specified SLO.

<h3 id="get-slo-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slo_id|path|string|true|The ID of the SLO.|
|from_ts|query|integer(int64)|true|The starting timestamp for the SLO status query in epoch seconds.|
|to_ts|query|integer(int64)|true|The ending timestamp for the SLO status query in epoch seconds.|
|disable_corrections|query|boolean|false|Whether to exclude correction windows from the SLO status calculation. Defaults to false.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "error_budget_remaining": 99.5,
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-software-catalog">Software Catalog</h1>

API to create, update, retrieve, and delete Software Catalog entities.

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/service_catalog/service_definitions#metadata-schema-v30-beta">External documentation</a>

## Get a list of entities

<a id="opIdListCatalogEntity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/catalog/entity \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/catalog/entity`

Get a list of entities from Software Catalog.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-entities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[offset]|query|integer(int64)|false|Specific offset to use as the beginning of the returned page.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of entities in the response.|
|filter[id]|query|string|false|Filter entities by UUID.|
|filter[ref]|query|string|false|Filter entities by reference|
|filter[name]|query|string|false|Filter entities by name.|
|filter[kind]|query|string|false|Filter entities by kind.|
|filter[owner]|query|string|false|Filter entities by owner.|
|filter[relation][type]|query|[RelationType](#schemarelationtype)|false|Filter entities by relation type.|
|filter[exclude_snapshot]|query|string|false|Filter entities by excluding snapshotted entities.|
|include|query|[IncludeType](#schemaincludetype)|false|Include relationship data.|
|includeDiscovered|query|boolean|false|If true, includes discovered services from APM and USM that do not have entity definitions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeOwns|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeOwnedBy|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeDependsOn|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeDependencyOf|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypePartsOf|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeHasPart|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeOtherOwns|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeOtherOwnedBy|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeImplementedBy|
|filter[relation][type]|RelationTypeImplements|
|include|schema|
|include|raw_schema|
|include|oncall|
|include|incident|
|include|relation|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "apiVersion": "v3",
        "kind": "service",
        "name": "myService",
        "namespace": "default"
      },
      "id": "4b163705-23c0-4573-b2fb-f6cea2163fcb",
      "type": "entity"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "count": 1,
    "includeCount": 0
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

## Create or update entities

<a id="opIdUpsertCatalogEntity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/catalog/entity \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "apiVersion": "v3",
    "integrations": {
      "opsgenie": {
        "serviceURL": "https://www.opsgenie.com/service/shopping-cart"
      },
      "pagerduty": {
        "serviceURL": "https://www.pagerduty.com/service-directory/Pshopping-cart"
      }
    },
    "kind": "service",
    "metadata": {
      "additionalOwners": [
        {
          "name": ""
        }
      ],
      "contacts": [
        {
          "contact": "https://slack/",
          "type": "slack"
        }
      ],
      "id": "4b163705-23c0-4573-b2fb-f6cea2163fcb",
      "inheritFrom": "application:default/myapp",
      "links": [
        {
          "name": "mylink",
          "type": "link",
          "url": "https://mylink"
        }
      ],
      "name": "myService",
      "namespace": "default",
      "tags": [
        "this:tag",
        "that:tag"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-spans">Spans</h1>

Search and aggregate your spans from your Datadog platform over HTTP.

## Aggregate spans

<a id="opIdAggregateSpans"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/spans/analytics/aggregate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "compute": [
          {
            "aggregation": "pc90",
            "interval": "5m",
            "metric": "@duration",
            "type": "timeseries"
          }
        ],
        "filter": {
          "from": "now-15m",
          "query": "service:web* AND @http.status_code:[200 TO 299]",
          "to": "now"
        },
        "group_by": [
          {
            "facet": "service",
            "limit": 20,
            "sort": {
              "aggregation": "pc90",
              "metric": "@duration",
              "order": "desc",
              "type": "measure"
            }
          }
        ],
        "options": {
          "timezone": "GMT"
        }
      },
      "type": "aggregate_request"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/spans/analytics/aggregate`

The API endpoint to aggregate spans into buckets and compute metrics and timeseries.
This endpoint is rate limited to `300` requests per hour.

A request can generate at most 10,000 groups across all `group_by` entries, or 400,000 groups
including time buckets when a `timeseries` compute is used. Set `limit` on each `group_by` entry
to stay within these bounds. Requests over long time ranges or with many groups are more resource-intensive
and can fail. To reduce load, narrow the time range or lower the `limit` on each `group_by` entry.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "compute": [
        {
          "aggregation": "pc90",
          "interval": "5m",
          "metric": "@duration",
          "type": "timeseries"
        }
      ],
      "filter": {
        "from": "now-15m",
        "query": "service:web* AND @http.status_code:[200 TO 299]",
        "to": "now"
      },
      "group_by": [
        {
          "facet": "service",
          "limit": 20,
          "sort": {
            "aggregation": "pc90",
            "metric": "@duration",
            "order": "desc",
            "type": "measure"
          }
        }
      ],
      "options": {
        "timezone": "GMT"
      }
    },
    "type": "aggregate_request"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="aggregate-spans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SpansAggregateRequest](#schemaspansaggregaterequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[SpansAggregateData](#schemaspansaggregatedata)|false|The object containing the query content.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "by": {
          "host": "my-hostname"
        },
        "computes": {
          "c0": 19
        }
      },
      "id": "abc-123",
      "type": "bucket"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "elapsed": 132,
    "status": "done"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

`GET /api/v2/spans/events`

List endpoint returns spans that match a span search query.
[Results are paginated][1].

Use this endpoint to see your latest spans.
This endpoint is rate limited to `300` requests per hour.

[1]: /logs/guide/collect-multiple-logs-with-pagination?tab=v2api

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-spans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|filter[query]|query|string|false|Search query following spans syntax.|
|filter[from]|query|string|false|Minimum timestamp for requested spans. Supports date-time ISO8601, date math, and regular timestamps (milliseconds).|
|filter[to]|query|string|false|Maximum timestamp for requested spans. Supports date-time ISO8601, date math, and regular timestamps (milliseconds).|
|sort|query|[SpansSort](#schemaspanssort)|false|Order of spans in results.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|List following results with a cursor provided in the previous query.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of spans in the response.|

## Submit libraries for vulnerability scanning

<a id="opIdCreateSCAScan"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/static-analysis-sca/dependencies/scan \

  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {

        "libraries": [
          {
            "exclusions": [],
            "is_dev": false,
            "is_direct": true,
            "package_manager": "nuget",
            "purl": "pkg:nuget/Newtonsoft.Json@13.0.1",
```

## Create Custom Rule Revision

<a id="opIdCreateCustomRuleRevision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/static-analysis/custom/rulesets/string/rules/string/revisions \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "arguments": [
          {
            "description": "Maximum call depth to analyze",
            "name": "max_depth"
          }
        ],
        "category": "SECURITY",
        "code": "def rule(node): return node.type == '\''call'\''",
        "creation_message": "Initial revision",
        "cve": "CVE-2024-1234",
        "cwe": "CWE-79",
        "description": "Detects insecure coding patterns that may lead to vulnerabilities",
        "documentation_url": "https://docs.example.com/rules/my-rule",
        "is_published": false,
        "is_testing": false,
        "language": "PYTHON",
        "severity": "ERROR",
        "short_description": "Rule to detect insecure patterns",
        "should_use_ai_fix": false,
        "tags": [
          "security",
          "custom"
        ],
        "tests": [
          {
            "annotation_count": 1,
            "code": "result = insecure_function()",
            "filename": "test.yaml"
          }
        ],
        "tree_sitter_query": "(call_expression) @call"
      },
      "type": "custom_rule_revision"
    }
  }'
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-status-pages">Status Pages</h1>

Manage your status pages and communicate service disruptions to stakeholders via Datadog's API. See the [Status Pages documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/status_pages/) for more information.

## List status pages

<a id="opIdListStatusPages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/statuspages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/statuspages`

Lists all status pages for the organization.

<h3 id="list-status-pages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[offset]|query|integer(int64)|false|Offset to use as the start of the page.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of status pages to return per page.|
|filter[domain_prefix]|query|string|false|Filter status pages by exact domain prefix match. Returns at most one result.|
|filter[name]|query|string|false|Filter status pages by name with case-insensitive substring matching.|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of resources to include. Supported values: created_by_user, last_modified_by_user.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "components": [],
        "domain_prefix": "status-page-us1",
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "Status Page US1",
        "subscriptions_enabled": true,
        "type": "public",
        "visualization_type": "bars_and_uptime_percentage"
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
      "type": "status_pages"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-status-pages-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[StatusPageArray](#schemastatuspagearray)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKeyAuth & appKeyAuth, AuthZ ( Scopes: status_pages_settings_read )
</aside>

## Create status page

<a id="opIdCreateStatusPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/statuspages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "company_logo": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAEAAIKMMMM",
        "components": [
          {
            "name": "API",
            "position": 0,
            "type": "component"
          },
          {
            "components": [
              {
                "name": "Login",
                "position": 0,
                "type": "component"
              },
              {
                "name": "Settings",
                "position": 1,
                "type": "component"
              }
            ],
            "name": "Web App",
            "position": 1,
            "type": "group"
          },
          {
            "name": "Webhooks",
            "position": 2,
            "type": "component"
          }
        ],
        "domain_prefix": "status-page-us1",
        "email_header_image": "data:image/png;base64,pQSLAw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAQ4AASJKFF",
        "favicon": "data:image/png;base64,kWMRNw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAEAAAABACA",
        "name": "Status Page US1",
        "subscriptions_enabled": true,
        "type": "public",
        "visualization_type": "bars_and_uptime_percentage"
      },
      "type": "status_pages"
```

`GET /api/v2/statuspages/degradations`

Lists all degradations for the organization. Optionally filter by status and page.

<h3 id="list-degradations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[page_id]|query|string|false|Optional page id filter.|
|page[offset]|query|integer(int64)|false|Offset to use as the start of the page.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of degradations to return per page.|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of resources to include. Supported values: created_by_user, last_modified_by_user, status_page.|
|filter[status]|query|string|false|Optional degradation status filter. Supported values: investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort order. Prefix with '-' for descending. Supported values: created_at, -created_at, modified_at, -modified_at.|
|filter[source_id]|query|string|false|Optional source ID filter. Returns only degradations whose source matches this ID (for example, an incident ID).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "components_affected": [],
        "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        "description": "Our API is experiencing elevated latency.",
        "modified_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        "status": "investigating",
        "title": "Elevated API Latency",
        "updates": []
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000005",
      "type": "degradations"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

## Publish status page

<a id="opIdPublishStatusPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/statuspages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /api/v2/statuspages/{page_id}/publish`

Publishes a status page. For pages of type `public`, makes the status page available on the public internet and requires the `status_pages_public_page_publish` permission. For pages of type `internal`, makes the status page available under the `status-pages/$domain_prefix/view` route within the Datadog organization and requires the `status_pages_internal_page_publish` permission.

<h3 id="publish-status-page-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the status page.|

> Example responses

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="publish-status-page-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiKeyAuth & appKeyAuth, AuthZ ( Scopes: status_pages_internal_page_publish status_pages_public_page_publish )
</aside>

`POST /api/v2/statuspages/{page_id}/unpublish`

For pages of type `internal`, removes the `status-pages/$domain_prefix/view` route from the Datadog organization and requires the `status_pages_internal_page_publish` permission.

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-stegadography">Stegadography</h1>

Extract watermarks embedded in dashboard screenshots to retrieve cached widget state.

## Get widgets from an image

<a id="opIdGetStegadographyWidgets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/stegadography/get-widgets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'image=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /api/v2/stegadography/get-widgets`

Extracts watermarks from a PNG image and returns the cached widget data
associated with each watermark found. The image must be uploaded as a
`multipart/form-data` request with the file in the `image` field.
Only widgets belonging to the authenticated organization are returned.

> Body parameter

```yaml
image: screenshot.png
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-storage-management">Storage Management</h1>

Enable Storage Management for S3 buckets, GCS buckets, and Azure containers. Each configuration registers the destination that holds inventory reports for the storage being monitored.

## Enable Storage Management for a bucket

<a id="opIdUpsertSyncConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cloudinventoryservice/syncconfigs \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "aws": {
          "aws_account_id": "123456789012",
          "destination_bucket_name": "my-inventory-bucket",
          "destination_bucket_region": "us-east-1",
          "destination_prefix": "logs/"
        }
      },
      "id": "aws",
      "type": "cloud_provider"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/cloudinventoryservice/syncconfigs`

Enable Storage Management for an S3 bucket, GCS bucket, or Azure container by registering the destination that holds its inventory reports. Set `data.id` to the cloud provider (`aws`, `gcp`, or `azure`) and provide the matching settings under data.attributes. Calling this endpoint with the same provider replaces the existing configuration.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "aws": {
        "aws_account_id": "123456789012",
        "destination_bucket_name": "my-inventory-bucket",
        "destination_bucket_region": "us-east-1",
        "destination_prefix": "logs/"
      }
    },
    "id": "aws",
    "type": "cloud_provider"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="enable-storage-management-for-a-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UpsertCloudInventorySyncConfigRequest](#schemaupsertcloudinventorysyncconfigrequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[UpsertCloudInventorySyncConfigRequestData](#schemaupsertcloudinventorysyncconfigrequestdata)|true|Storage Management configuration data for the create or update request.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "aws_account_id": "123456789012",
      "aws_bucket_name": "my-inventory-bucket",

    },
    "id": "aws",
    "type": "sync_configs"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-synthetics">Synthetics</h1>

Synthetic tests use simulated requests and actions so you can monitor the availability and performance of systems and applications. Datadog supports the following types of synthetic tests:
- [API tests](https://docs.datadoghq.com/synthetics/api_tests/)
- [Browser tests](https://docs.datadoghq.com/synthetics/browser_tests)
- [Network Path tests](https://docs.datadoghq.com/synthetics/network_path_tests/)
- [Mobile Application tests](https://docs.datadoghq.com/synthetics/mobile_app_testing)
You can use the Datadog API to create, manage, and organize tests and test suites programmatically.
For more information, see the [Synthetic Monitoring documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/synthetics/).

## Patch a test suite

<a id="opIdPatchTestSuite"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/synthetics/suites/123-abc-456/jsonpatch \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "json_patch": [
          {
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/name"
          }
        ]
      },
      "type": "suites_json_patch"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/synthetics/suites/{public_id}/jsonpatch`

Patch a Synthetic test suite using JSON Patch (RFC 6902).
Use partial updates to modify only specific fields of a test suite.

Common operations include:
- Replace field values: `{"op": "replace", "path": "/name", "value": "new_name"}`
- Add/update tags: `{"op": "add", "path": "/tags/-", "value": "new_tag"}`
- Remove fields: `{"op": "remove", "path": "/message"}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "json_patch": [
        {
          "op": "add",
          "path": "/name"
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "suites_json_patch"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="patch-a-test-suite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|public_id|path|string|true|The public ID of the Synthetic test suite to patch.|
|body|body|[SuiteJsonPatchRequest](#schemasuitejsonpatchrequest)|true|JSON Patch document with operations to apply.|
|» data|body|[SuiteJsonPatchRequestData](#schemasuitejsonpatchrequestdata)|true|Data object for a JSON Patch request on a Synthetic test suite.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "message": "Notification message",
      "monitor_id": 12345678,
      "name": "Example suite name",
      "options": {
        "alerting_threshold": 0.5
      },
      "public_id": "123-abc-456",
      "tags": [
        "env:production"
      ],
      "tests": [
        {
          "alerting_criticality": "critical",
          "public_id": ""
        }
      ],
      "type": "suite"
    },
    "id": "123-abc-456",
    "type": "suites"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

```json
    "Bad Request"

}
```

`POST /api/v2/synthetics/tests/{public_id}/files/multipart-upload-abort`

and releases any storage used by already-uploaded parts.

## Patch a global variable

<a id="opIdPatchGlobalVariable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/synthetics/variables/string/jsonpatch \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "json_patch": [
          {
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/name"
          }
        ]
      },
      "type": "global_variables_json_patch"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/synthetics/variables/{variable_id}/jsonpatch`

Patch a global variable using JSON Patch (RFC 6902).
This endpoint allows partial updates to a global variable by specifying only the fields to modify.

Common operations include:
- Replace field values: `{"op": "replace", "path": "/name", "value": "new_name"}`
- Update nested values: `{"op": "replace", "path": "/value/value", "value": "new_value"}`
- Add/update tags: `{"op": "add", "path": "/tags/-", "value": "new_tag"}`
- Remove fields: `{"op": "remove", "path": "/description"}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "json_patch": [
        {
          "op": "add",
          "path": "/name"
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "global_variables_json_patch"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="patch-a-global-variable-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|variable_id|path|string|true|The ID of the global variable.|
|body|body|[GlobalVariableJsonPatchRequest](#schemaglobalvariablejsonpatchrequest)|true|JSON Patch document with operations to apply.|
|» data|body|[GlobalVariableJsonPatchRequestData](#schemaglobalvariablejsonpatchrequestdata)|true|Data object for a JSON Patch request on a Synthetic global variable.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "description": "Example description",
      "name": "MY_VARIABLE",
      "tags": [
        "team:front"
      ],
      "value": {
        "secure": false,
        "value": "example-value"
      }
    },
    "id": "abc-123",
    "type": "global_variables"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  ]
}
```

```json
  ]
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-tag-rules">Tag Rules</h1>

Tag Rules define rules that govern which tag values are accepted for a given tag key,
scoped to a particular telemetry source (such as logs, spans, or metrics). Rules can be
`blocking` (data not matching the rule is rejected) or `surfacing` (matching data is
highlighted but not blocked). Each rule reports a compliance `score` derived from how
much recent telemetry adheres to the rule.

## List tag rules

<a id="opIdListTagRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/governance/tag_rules \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/governance/tag_rules`

Retrieve all tag rules for the organization. Optionally include disabled or deleted
rules, filter by telemetry source, and include each rule's current compliance score
via the `include=score` query parameter.

<h3 id="list-tag-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_disabled|query|boolean|false|Whether to include rules that are currently disabled. Defaults to `false`.|
|include_deleted|query|boolean|false|Whether to include rules that have been soft-deleted. Defaults to `false`.|
|include|query|[TagRuleInclude](#schematagruleinclude)|false|Comma-separated list of related resources to include alongside each rule in the response. Currently the only supported value is `score`.|
|filter[source]|query|[TagRuleSource](#schematagrulesource)|false|Restrict the result set to rules whose source matches the given value.|
|ts_start|query|integer(int64)|false|Start of the time window used for compliance score computation, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Defaults to a recent window appropriate for the source.|
|ts_end|query|integer(int64)|false|End of the time window used for compliance score computation, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be in the past and greater than `ts_start`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|score|
|filter[source]|logs|
|filter[source]|spans|
|filter[source]|metrics|
|filter[source]|rum|
|filter[source]|feed|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "created_at": "2026-05-21T22:11:06.108696Z",
        "created_by": "test-user",
        "enabled": true,
```

## Get a tag rule

<a id="opIdGetTagRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/governance/tag_rules/123 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/governance/tag_rules/{rule_id}`

Retrieve a single tag rule by ID. Optionally include the rule's current compliance
score via the `include=score` query parameter. Rules belonging to other organizations
cannot be retrieved.

|ts_start|query|integer(int64)|false|Start of the time window used for compliance score computation, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.|
|ts_end|query|integer(int64)|false|End of the time window used for compliance score computation, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be in the past and greater than `ts_start`.|

## Update a tag rule

`PATCH /api/v2/governance/tag_rules/{rule_id}`

request body are modified; omitted fields retain their current values. The rule's

## Get a tag rule compliance score

<a id="opIdGetTagRuleScore"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/governance/tag_rules/123/score \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/governance/tag_rules/{rule_id}/score`

Retrieve the compliance score for a single tag rule. The score is computed over the
requested time window (or a source-appropriate default) and represents the percentage of
telemetry within that window that conforms to the rule. A `null` score indicates that
no relevant telemetry was found.

<h3 id="get-a-tag-rule-compliance-score-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rule_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the tag rule.|
|ts_start|query|integer(int64)|false|Start of the time window used for compliance score computation, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.|
|ts_end|query|integer(int64)|false|End of the time window used for compliance score computation, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be in the past and greater than `ts_start`.|

## Get all teams

<a id="opIdListTeams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/team \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/team`

Get all teams.
Can be used to search for teams using the `filter[keyword]` and `filter[me]` query parameters.

<h3 id="get-all-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Specific page number to return.|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of items to return per page. The maximum allowed value is 100.|
|sort|query|[ListTeamsSort](#schemalistteamssort)|false|Specifies the order of the returned teams|
|include|query|[[ListTeamsInclude](#schemalistteamsinclude)]|false|Included related resources optionally requested. Allowed enum values: `team_links, user_team_permissions`|
|filter[keyword]|query|string|false|Search query. Can be team name, team handle, or email of team member|
|filter[me]|query|boolean|false|When true, only returns teams the current user belongs to|
|fields[team]|query|[[TeamsField](#schemateamsfield)]|false|List of fields that need to be fetched.|

## Link teams with external teams

<a id="opIdSyncTeams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/team/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "source": "github",
        "type": "link"
      },
      "type": "team_sync_bulk"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/team/sync`

This endpoint configures synchronization between your existing Datadog teams and teams from
GitHub or ServiceNow by matching team names.
It evaluates all current Datadog teams and compares them against teams in the external source
connected to your Datadog account.

This operation is read-only on the external source side, no teams will be modified or created there.
This only creates new teams in Datadog when type is set to `provision`.

Optionally, provide `selection_state` to limit synchronization
to specific teams or organizations and their subtrees, instead
of syncing all teams.

**GitHub**: [A GitHub organization must be connected to your Datadog account](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/github/),
and the GitHub App integrated with Datadog must have the `Members Read` permission. Matching is performed by comparing the Datadog team handle to the GitHub team slug
(lowercased and kebab-cased) using a normalized exact match; case is ignored and spaces are removed.

**ServiceNow**: [The ServiceNow integration must be configured for your Datadog account](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/servicenow/).
Active assignment groups from every configured ServiceNow instance are synchronized, and the ServiceNow
group hierarchy is preserved. When `sync_membership` is enabled, group members are matched to Datadog
users by email address.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "source": "github",
      "type": "link"
    },
    "type": "team_sync_bulk"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="link-teams-with-external-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TeamSyncRequest](#schemateamsyncrequest)|true|none|
|» data|body|[TeamSyncData](#schemateamsyncdata)|true|A configuration governing syncing between Datadog teams and teams from an external system.|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="link-teams-with-external-teams-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error - Unexpected error during linking.|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">

apiKeyAuth & appKeyAuth, AuthZ ( Scopes: teams_manage )
</aside>

## Update a team

<a id="opIdUpdateTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/team/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "avatar": "🥑",
        "handle": "example-team",
        "name": "Example Team"
      },
      "relationships": {
        "team_links": {
          "data": [
            {
              "id": "f9bb8444-af7f-11ec-ac2c-da7ad0900001"
            }
          ],
          "links": {
            "related": "/api/v2/team/c75a4a8e-20c7-11ee-a3a5-da7ad0900002/links"
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "team"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/team/{team_id}`

Update a team using the team's `id`.
If the `team_links` relationship is present, the associated links are updated to be in the order they appear in the array, and any existing team links not present are removed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "avatar": "🥑",
      "handle": "example-team",
      "name": "Example Team"
    },
    "relationships": {
      "team_links": {
        "data": [
          {
            "id": "f9bb8444-af7f-11ec-ac2c-da7ad0900001"
          }
        ],
        "links": {
          "related": "/api/v2/team/c75a4a8e-20c7-11ee-a3a5-da7ad0900002/links"
        }
      }
    },
    "type": "team"
  }
}
```

```bash
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/team/{team_id}/members`

List the direct and inherited members of a team, deduplicated by user.
Members of descendant teams are included unless `filter[is_direct_only]` is true.
Datadog support users are always excluded.

Use `page[number]` and `page[size]` to paginate through the results.
Invalid query parameters return a JSON:API error with status 400.
Invalid or unknown team UUIDs return status 404.

<h3 id="get-team-hierarchy-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|team_id|path|string|true|UUID of the requested root team.|
|filter[is_direct_only]|query|boolean|false|Return only direct members. By default, members inherited from descendant teams are also returned.|
|filter[include_service_accounts]|query|boolean|false|Include service accounts. Datadog support users are always excluded.|
|filter[keyword]|query|string|false|Filter by a case-insensitive substring of the user name, handle, or email.|
|include|query|string|false|Comma-separated resources to include: `user` and `team`. The included team is the requested team. Whitespace is trimmed, and duplicate or empty entries are ignored.|
|sort|query|string|false|Comma-separated sort fields: `name`, `handle`, `is_direct`, and `provisioned_by`. Fields are applied in order, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. By default, team admins come first, followed by other direct members, then inherited members, sorted by name within each group.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Zero-based page number. Negative values become 0. Defaults to 0.|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Requested number of members per page. Defaults to and maxes out at 100.|

## Update Flaky Tests Management policies

<a id="opIdUpdateFlakyTestsManagementPolicies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/ci/test-optimization/settings/policies \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "attempt_to_fix": {
          "retries": 3
        },
        "disabled": {
          "enabled": false
        },
        "quarantined": {
          "auto_quarantine_rule": {
            "enabled": true,
            "window_seconds": 3600
          },
          "branch_rule": {
            "branches": [
              "main"
            ],
            "enabled": true,
            "excluded_branches": [],
            "excluded_test_services": []
          },
          "enabled": true,
          "failure_rate_rule": {
            "branches": [
              "main"
            ],
            "enabled": true,
            "min_runs": 10,
            "threshold": 0.5
          }
        },
        "repository_id": "github.com/example-org/example-repo"
      },
      "type": "test_optimization_update_flaky_tests_management_policies_request"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/ci/test-optimization/settings/policies`

Partially update Flaky Tests Management repository-level policies for the given repository.
Only provided policy blocks are updated; omitted blocks are left unchanged.

> Body parameter

```json
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "attempt_to_fix": {
        "retries": 3
      },
      "disabled": {
        "enabled": false
      },
      "quarantined": {
        "auto_quarantine_rule": {
          "enabled": true,
          "window_seconds": 3600
        },
        "branch_rule": {
          "branches": [
            "main"
          ],
          "enabled": true,
          "excluded_branches": [],
          "excluded_test_services": []
        },
        "enabled": true,
        "failure_rate_rule": {
          "branches": [
            "main"
          ],
          "enabled": true,
          "min_runs": 10,
          "threshold": 0.5
        }
      },
      "repository_id": "github.com/example-org/example-repo"
    },
    "type": "test_optimization_update_flaky_tests_management_policies_request"
  }
}
```

`PATCH /api/v2/ci/test-optimization/settings/service`

Only provided fields are updated; setting a field to `null` is a no-op.

The `pr_comments_enabled` field is ignored as it cannot be overridden at the service level.

## Search flaky tests

<a id="opIdSearchFlakyTests"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/test/flaky-test-management/tests \

          "limit": 25

        "sort": "failure_rate"
      },
      "type": "search_flaky_tests_request"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/test/flaky-test-management/tests`

List endpoint returning flaky tests from Flaky Test Management. Results are paginated.

The response includes comprehensive test information including:
- Test identification and metadata (module, suite, name)
- Flaky state and categorization
- First and last flake occurrences (timestamp, branch, commit SHA)
- Test execution statistics from the last 7 days (failure rate)
- Pipeline impact metrics (failed pipelines count, total lost time)
- Complete status change history (optional, ordered from most recent to oldest)

Set `include_history` to `true` in the request to receive the status change history for each test.
History is disabled by default for better performance.

Results support filtering by various facets including service, environment, repository, branch, and test state.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "filter": {
        "query": "flaky_test_state:active @git.repository.id_v2:\"github.com/datadog/test-service\""
      },
      "page": {
        "cursor": "eyJzdGFydEF0IjoiQVFBQUFYS2tMS3pPbm40NGV3QUFBQUJCV0V0clRFdDZVbG8zY3pCRmNsbHJiVmxDWlEifQ==",
        "limit": 25
      },
      "sort": "failure_rate"
    },
    "type": "search_flaky_tests_request"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-threat-intelligence">Threat Intelligence</h1>

Ingest and manage threat intelligence data for security enrichment and investigation.

## Ingest STIX threat intelligence

<a id="opIdAddSTIXThreatIntel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/security/threat-intel/stix \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'ti_vendor: acme' \
  -d '{
    "id": "bundle--11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
    "objects": [
      {
        "created": "2026-07-22T12:00:00Z",
        "id": "indicator--22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
        "modified": "2026-07-22T12:00:00Z",
        "pattern": "[ipv4-addr:value = '\''198.51.100.42'\'']",
        "pattern_type": "stix",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "type": "indicator",
        "valid_from": "2026-07-22T12:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "type": "bundle"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/security/threat-intel/stix`

Ingest a STIX 2.1 bundle containing threat intelligence indicators. Only indicator objects are processed. Supported indicator patterns contain IPv4 addresses, IPv6 addresses, domain names, or SHA-256 file hashes.

Non-indicator objects are ignored and are not included in the response counters. Indicator objects with unsupported STIX versions or patterns that produce no supported observable values increment the `unsupported` counter. Patterns that cannot be parsed increment the `invalid` counter. Processing is best effort, so valid supported indicators in the same bundle are still added.

A successful response means ingestion has completed. Reference-table materialization and enrichment happen asynchronously. Requests are limited to 50 MB as received, 100 MB after decompression, and 10 requests per second per API key. Gzip-compressed request bodies are supported.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "bundle--11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "objects": [
    {
      "created": "2026-07-22T12:00:00Z",
      "id": "indicator--22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
      "modified": "2026-07-22T12:00:00Z",
      "pattern": "[ipv4-addr:value = '198.51.100.42']",
      "pattern_type": "stix",
      "spec_version": "2.1",
      "type": "indicator",
      "valid_from": "2026-07-22T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "spec_version": "2.1",
  "type": "bundle"
}
```

<h3 id="ingest-stix-threat-intelligence-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ti_vendor|header|string|true|Vendor identifier for the feed. The value must not exceed 10 characters. Datadog normalizes the accepted value to lowercase, converts non-alphanumeric characters to underscores, and trims leading and trailing underscores.|
|Content-Encoding|header|[STIXContentEncoding](#schemastixcontentencoding)|false|Content encoding for the request body. Use gzip for a compressed STIX bundle.|
|body|body|[STIXBundleRequest](#schemastixbundlerequest)|true|A STIX 2.1 bundle containing indicator objects. The request body must not exceed 50 MB as received or 100 MB after decompression.|
|» id|body|string|true|The STIX bundle identifier.|
|» objects|body|[[STIXObject](#schemastixobject)]|true|The STIX objects included in the bundle. Indicator objects are processed and ingested; all other STIX object types are ignored and are not included in the response counters.|
|» spec_version|body|[STIXSpecVersion](#schemastixspecversion)|false|The supported STIX specification version.|
|» type|body|[STIXBundleType](#schemastixbundletype)|true|The STIX object type for a bundle.|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|
|» spec_version|2.1|
|» type|bundle|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "accepted": 1,
      "invalid": 0,
      "unsupported": 0
    },
    "id": "acme",
    "type": "threat-intel-stix-ingest"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-timeseries-anomaly-investigations">Timeseries Anomaly Investigations</h1>

Investigate metrics timeseries anomalies and return deterministic findings.

## Investigate a timeseries anomaly

<a id="opIdCreateTimeseriesAnomalyInvestigation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/timeseries-anomaly-investigations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "requests": [
          {
            "formulas": [
              {
                "formula": "query1"
              }
            ],
            "from": 1754406000000,
            "queries": [
              {
                "data_source": "metrics",
                "name": "query1",
                "query": "avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {service}"
              }
            ],
            "to": 1754423940000
          }
        ]
      },
      "type": "timeseries_anomaly_investigation"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/timeseries-anomaly-investigations`

Investigates a metrics timeseries request for its most significant anomalies and returns
deterministic findings. Metrics queries with or without grouping are supported. This
API version accepts exactly one request and returns at most three anomalies.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "requests": [
        {
          "formulas": [
            {
              "formula": "query1"
            }
          ],
          "from": 1754406000000,
          "queries": [
            {
              "data_source": "metrics",
              "name": "query1",
              "query": "avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {service}"
            }
          ],
          "to": 1754423940000
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "timeseries_anomaly_investigation"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="datadog-api-v2-collection-usage-metering">Usage Metering</h1>

The usage metering API allows you to get hourly, daily, and
monthly usage across multiple facets of Datadog.
This API is available to all Pro and Enterprise customers.

**Note**: Usage data is delayed by up to 72 hours from when it was incurred.
It is retained for 15 months.

You can retrieve up to 24 hours of hourly usage data for multiple organizations,
and up to two months of hourly usage data for a single organization in one request.
Learn more on the [usage details documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/usage_details/).

<a href="https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/usage_details/">Find out more at</a>

## Get Monthly Cost Attribution

<a id="opIdGetMonthlyCostAttribution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/cost_by_tag/monthly_cost_attribution?start_month=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&fields=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/cost_by_tag/monthly_cost_attribution`

Get monthly cost attribution by tag across multi-org and single root-org accounts.
Cost Attribution data for a given month becomes available no later than the 19th of the following month.
This API endpoint is paginated. To make sure you receive all records, check if the value of `next_record_id` is
set in the response. If it is, make another request and pass `next_record_id` as a parameter.
Pseudo code example:
```
response := GetMonthlyCostAttribution(start_month, end_month)
cursor := response.metadata.pagination.next_record_id
WHILE cursor != null BEGIN
  sleep(5 seconds)  # Avoid running into rate limit
  response := GetMonthlyCostAttribution(start_month, end_month, next_record_id=cursor)
  cursor := response.metadata.pagination.next_record_id
END
```

This endpoint is only accessible for [parent-level organizations](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/multi_organization/). This endpoint is not available in the Government (US1-FED) site.

<h3 id="get-monthly-cost-attribution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_month|query|string(date-time)|true|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to month: `[YYYY-MM]` for cost beginning in this month.|
|end_month|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to month: `[YYYY-MM]` for cost ending this month.|
|fields|query|string|true|Comma-separated list specifying cost types (e.g., `<billing_dimension>_on_demand_cost`, `<billing_dimension>_committed_cost`, `<billing_dimension>_total_cost`) and the<br>proportions (`<billing_dimension>_percentage_in_org`, `<billing_dimension>_percentage_in_account`). Use `*` to retrieve all fields.<br>Example: `infra_host_on_demand_cost,infra_host_percentage_in_account`<br>To obtain the complete list of active billing dimensions that can be used to replace<br>`<billing_dimension>` in the field names, make a request to the [Get active billing dimensions API](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/usage-metering/#get-active-billing-dimensions-for-cost-attribution).|
|sort_direction|query|[SortDirection](#schemasortdirection)|false|The direction to sort by: `[desc, asc]`.|
|sort_name|query|string|false|The billing dimension to sort by. Always sorted by total cost. Example: `infra_host`.|
|tag_breakdown_keys|query|string|false|Comma separated list of tag keys used to group cost. If no value is provided the cost will not be broken down by tags.<br>To see which tags are available, look for the value of `tag_config_source` in the API response.|
|next_record_id|query|string|false|List following results with a next_record_id provided in the previous query.|
|include_descendants|query|boolean|false|Include child org cost in the response. Defaults to `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_direction|desc|
|sort_direction|asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "abc-123",
      "type": "cost_by_tag"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

`GET /api/v2/usage/application_security`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`GET /api/v2/usage/billing_dimension_mapping`

## Get estimated cost across your account

<a id="opIdGetEstimatedCostByOrg"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/usage/estimated_cost \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/usage/estimated_cost`

Get estimated cost across multi-org and single root-org accounts.
Estimated cost data is only available for the current month and previous month
and is delayed by up to 72 hours from when it was incurred.
To access historical costs prior to this, use the `/historical_cost` endpoint.

This endpoint is only accessible for [parent-level organizations](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/multi_organization/).

<h3 id="get-estimated-cost-across-your-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|view|query|string|false|String to specify whether cost is broken down at a parent-org level or at the sub-org level. Available views are `summary` and `sub-org`. Defaults to `summary`.|
|start_month|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to month: `[YYYY-MM]` for cost beginning this month. **Either start_month or start_date should be specified, but not both.** (start_month cannot go beyond two months in the past). Provide an `end_month` to view month-over-month cost.|
|end_month|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to month: `[YYYY-MM]` for cost ending this month.|
|start_date|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to day: `[YYYY-MM-DD]` for cost beginning this day. **Either start_month or start_date should be specified, but not both.** (start_date cannot go beyond two months in the past). Provide an `end_date` to view day-over-day cumulative cost.|
|end_date|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to day: `[YYYY-MM-DD]` for cost ending this day.|
|cost_aggregation|query|[CostAggregationType](#schemacostaggregationtype)|false|Controls how costs are aggregated when using `start_date`. The `cumulative` option returns month-to-date running totals.|
|include_connected_accounts|query|boolean|false|Boolean to specify whether to include accounts connected to the current account as partner customers in the Datadog partner network program. Defaults to `false`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|cost_aggregation|cumulative|

```json
}
```

```json
  ]
```

```json
  ]
}
```

```json
  ]
}
```

<a id="opIdGetHourlyUsage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/usage/hourly_usage?filter%5Btimestamp%5D%5Bstart%5D=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&filter%5Bproduct_families%5D=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/usage/hourly_usage`

Get hourly usage by product family.

<h3 id="get-hourly-usage-by-product-family-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[timestamp][start]|query|string(date-time)|true|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to hour: [YYYY-MM-DDThh] for usage beginning at this hour.|
|filter[timestamp][end]|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in ISO-8601 format, UTC, precise to hour: [YYYY-MM-DDThh] for usage ending **before** this hour.|
|filter[product_families]|query|string|true|Comma separated list of product families to retrieve. Available families are `all`, `ai`, `analyzed_logs`,<br>`application_performance_monitoring`, `application_security`, `audit_trail`, `bits_ai`, `serverless`, `ci_app`,<br>`cloud_cost_management`, `cloud_siem`, `csm_container_enterprise`, `csm_host_enterprise`, `csm_host_pro`, `cspm`,<br>`custom_events`, `cws`, `data_observability`, `dbm`, `digital_experience_management`, `error_tracking`,<br>`fargate`, `infra_hosts`, `incident_management`, `indexed_logs`, `indexed_spans`, `infrastructure_monitoring`,<br>`ingested_spans`, `iot`, `lambda_traced_invocations`, `llm_observability`, `log_management`, `logs`,<br>`network_flows`, `network_hosts`, `network_monitoring`, `observability_pipelines`, `online_archive`,<br>`platform_capabilities`, `product_analytics`, `profiling`, `rum`, `rum_browser_sessions`, `rum_mobile_sessions`,<br>`sds`, `security`, `snmp`, `software_delivery`, `synthetics_api`, `synthetics_browser`,<br>`synthetics_mobile`, `synthetics_parallel_testing`, `timeseries`, `vuln_management` and `workflow_executions`.<br>The following product family has been **deprecated**: `audit_logs`.|
|filter[include_descendants]|query|boolean|false|Include child org usage in the response. Defaults to false.|
|filter[include_connected_accounts]|query|boolean|false|Boolean to specify whether to include accounts connected to the current account as partner customers in the Datadog partner network program. Defaults to false.|
|filter[include_breakdown]|query|boolean|false|Include breakdown of usage by subcategories where applicable (for product family logs only). Defaults to false.|
|filter[versions]|query|string|false|Comma separated list of product family versions to use in the format `product_family:version`. For example,<br>`infra_hosts:1.0.0`. If this parameter is not used, the API will use the latest version of each requested<br>product family. Currently all families have one version `1.0.0`.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of results to return (between 1 and 500) - defaults to 500 if limit not specified.|
|page[next_record_id]|query|string|false|List following results with a next_record_id provided in the previous query.|

## List usage quotas

<a id="opIdListQuotas"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/usage/quotas/ai_credits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/usage/quotas/{quota_namespace}`

Lists usage quotas for the caller's organization in a quota namespace. You can optionally include
descendant organizations in the same datacenter as the caller. Requires the `billing_read` or
`billing_edit` permission.

<h3 id="list-usage-quotas-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|quota_namespace|path|string|true|The product-specific namespace whose usage quotas are being managed.|
|include_descendants|query|boolean|false|Whether to include quotas configured on descendant organizations in the caller's organization hierarchy. Only descendants in the same datacenter are supported.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|An opaque cursor from a previous response's `meta.page.next_cursor` used to retrieve the next page.|
|page[limit]|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of usage quotas to return per page.|

> Example responses

```json

  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "enforced": true,
        "org_public_id": "abcdef12345",
        "scope": {

        },

      },

      "type": "quotas"
    },
    {
      "attributes": {
        "enforced": true,
        "org_public_id": "abcdef12345",
        "pending_effective_from": "2026-11",
        "pending_usage_limit": 100000,
        "usage_limit": 600000
      },
      "id": "MTIzNB9haV9jcmVkaXRzH3VzZXJfaGFuZGxlOl9fQUxMX18",
      "type": "quotas"
```

## Create or update usage quotas

<a id="opIdCreateQuotas"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/usage/quotas/ai_credits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "enforced": true,
          "scope": {
            "user_handle": "jane@example.com"
          },
          "usage_limit": 100000
        },
        "type": "quotas"
      },
      {
        "attributes": {
          "enforced": false,
          "scope": {
            "user_handle": "*"
          },
          "usage_limit": 250000
        },
        "type": "quotas"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/usage/quotas/{quota_namespace}`

Creates or updates one or more usage quotas by scope. If a quota already exists for a supplied scope, it is updated.
Otherwise, a quota is created only when `usage_limit` and `enforced` are provided.
For the organization-wide quota, `pending_usage_limit` schedules a limit for the next usage period and can
accompany an immediate limit or update an existing quota by itself.
Scheduled changes follow `include_descendants` like the other fields. Requires the `billing_edit` permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "enforced": true,
        "scope": {
          "user_handle": "jane@example.com"
        },
        "usage_limit": 100000
      },
      "type": "quotas"
    },
    {
      "attributes": {
        "enforced": false,
        "scope": {
          "user_handle": "*"
        },
        "usage_limit": 250000
      },
      "type": "quotas"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-usage-quotas-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|quota_namespace|path|string|true|The product-specific namespace whose usage quotas are being managed.|
|include_descendants|query|boolean|false|Whether to write every item in the request to the caller's organization and all of its descendant organizations, instead of only the caller's organization. Only descendants in the same datacenter are supported. For a user-handle scope, the quota is applied only to the caller's organization and to descendant organizations where that user handle exists; the item fails only if the handle exists in none of them.|
|body|body|[UsageQuotasCreateRequest](#schemausagequotascreaterequest)|true|The usage quotas to create or update.|
|» data|body|[UsageQuotaCreateDataList](#schemausagequotacreatedatalist)|true|A bulk list of usage quota resources to create or update by scope.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "enforced": true,
        "org_public_id": "abcdef12345",
        "scope": {
          "user_handle": "jane@example.com"
        },
        "usage_limit": 100000
      },
      "id": "MTIzNB9haV9jcmVkaXRzH3VzZXJfaGFuZGxlOmphbmVAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20",
      "type": "quotas"
    },
    {
      "attributes": {
        "error": "usage_limit is out of range"
      },
      "id": "MTIzNB9haV9jcmVkaXRzH3VzZXJfaGFuZGxlOnVzZXJAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20",

}
```

## Cancel a scheduled usage quota limit

<a id="opIdDeletePendingQuota"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/usage/quotas/ai_credits/MTIzNB9haV9jcmVkaXRzH3VzZXJfaGFuZGxlOl9fQUxMX18/pending \
  -X DELETE \

  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/usage/quotas/{quota_namespace}/{id}/pending`

Cancels the limit change scheduled to take effect at the start of the next usage period, leaving the usage quota and its current limit unchanged. Returns `404` when the quota does not exist, has no scheduled change, or its scheduled change has already taken effect; in every case the quota is left unchanged. The quota must belong to the caller's organization or one of its descendants, and its opaque identifier must belong to the requested quota namespace. Requires the `billing_edit` permission.

## Get available fields for usage summary

<a id="opIdGetUsageSummaryAvailableFields"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/usage/summary/available_fields \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/usage/summary/available_fields`

List the field names returned by `GET /api/v1/usage/summary` at each of its
three response levels. Each list contains every key the data endpoint
emits—both typed fields declared in the OpenAPI spec and untyped keys
exposed through `additionalProperties` (the latter used for billing
dimensions and usage types added after the v1 schema freeze).

This endpoint is only accessible for [parent-level organizations](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/multi_organization/).

Go example:

```go
fields, _, err := api.GetUsageSummaryAvailableFields(ctx)
attr := fields.Data.GetAttributes()

// resp is the *UsageSummaryResponse returned by api.GetUsageSummary(ctx, ...)
// Layer 1: UsageSummaryResponse
for _, key := range attr.GetResponseFields() {
    if val, ok := resp.AdditionalProperties[key]; ok {
        fmt.Println(key, val.(json.Number))
    }
}
// Layer 2: UsageSummaryDate (per month)
for _, date := range resp.GetUsage() {
    for _, key := range attr.GetDateFields() {
        if val, ok := date.AdditionalProperties[key]; ok {
            fmt.Println(key, val.(json.Number))
        }
    }
    // Layer 3: UsageSummaryDateOrg (per org per month)
    for _, org := range date.GetOrgs() {
        for _, key := range attr.GetDateOrgFields() {
            if val, ok := org.AdditionalProperties[key]; ok {
                fmt.Println(key, val.(json.Number))
            }
        }
    }
}
```

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "date_fields": [
        "agent_host_top99p",
        "aws_host_top99p",
        "ccm_anthropic_spend_last"
      ],
      "date_org_fields": [
        "agent_host_top99p",
        "aws_host_top99p",
        "ccm_anthropic_spend_last"
      ],
      "response_fields": [
        "agent_host_top99p_sum",
        "aws_host_top99p_sum",
        "ccm_anthropic_spend_last_sum"
      ]
    },
    "id": "all",
    "type": "usage_summary_available_fields"
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests.|[APIErrorResponse](#schemaapierrorresponse)|

`PUT /api/v2/anonymize_users`

## Get current user

<a id="opIdGetCurrentUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/current_user \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/current_user`

Get the user associated with the current authentication context.
The response includes the user's profile attributes (name, email, handle,
status, MFA state), along with related resources: the user's organization,
assigned roles with their granted permissions, and team-scoped roles.
No additional permissions are required beyond valid authentication.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00",
      "disabled": false,
      "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
      "handle": "jane.doe",
      "icon": "https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/abc123",
      "mfa_enabled": true,
      "modified_at": "2024-06-01T12:00:00+00:00",
      "name": "Jane Doe",
      "service_account": false,
      "status": "Active",
      "title": "Senior Engineer",
      "verified": true
    },
    "id": "00000000-0000-9999-0000-000000000000",
    "type": "users"
  },
  "included": []
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

## Update current user

<a id="opIdUpdateCurrentUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/current_user \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
        "name": "Jane Doe",
        "title": "Staff Engineer"
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-9999-0000-000000000000",
      "type": "users"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/current_user`

Edit the profile of the currently authenticated user. Updatable fields
include `name`, `title`, `email`, and `disabled` status. The `id` field
in the request body must match the authenticated user's UUID; a mismatch
returns a 422 error. Email address changes are recorded in the audit trail.
Requires the `user_self_profile_write` permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
      "name": "Jane Doe",
      "title": "Staff Engineer"
    },
    "id": "00000000-0000-9999-0000-000000000000",
    "type": "users"
  }
}
```

## List all users

<a id="opIdListUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users`

Get the list of all users in the organization. This list includes
all users even if they are deactivated or unverified.

<h3 id="list-all-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[size]|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of items to return per page. The maximum allowed value is 100.|
|page[number]|query|integer(int64)|false|Specific page number to return.|
|sort|query|string|false|User attribute to order results by. Sort order is ascending by default.<br>Sort order is descending if the field<br>is prefixed by a negative sign, for example `sort=-name`. Options: `name`,<br>`modified_at`, `user_count`.|
|sort_dir|query|[QuerySortOrder](#schemaquerysortorder)|false|Direction of sort. Options: `asc`, `desc`.|
|filter|query|string|false|Filter all users by the given string. Defaults to no filtering.|
|filter[status]|query|string|false|Filter on status attribute.<br>Comma separated list, with possible values `Active`, `Pending`, and `Disabled`.<br>Defaults to no filtering.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_dir|asc|
|sort_dir|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "email": "test@example.com",
        "handle": "example-handle",
        "name": "Example Name",
        "status": "Active"
      },
      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
      "type": "users"
    }
  ],
  "included": [],
  "meta": {}
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    "Bad Request"
  ]
}
```

```json
}
```

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \

      "attributes": {

      "relationships": {
        "roles": {

          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "users"
    }
  }'
```

## Create a web integration account

<a id="opIdCreateWebIntegrationAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/web-integrations/string/accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "DD-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "attributes": {
        "name": "my-databricks-account",
        "secrets": {
          "client_secret": "my-client-secret"
        },
        "settings": {
          "workspace_url": "https://example.azuredatabricks.net"
        }
      },
      "type": "Account"
    }
  }'
```
