<h2 id="tocS_DeploymentGateRuleEvaluationConfiguration">DeploymentGateRuleEvaluationConfiguration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadeploymentgateruleevaluationconfiguration"></a>
<a id="schema_DeploymentGateRuleEvaluationConfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocSdeploymentgateruleevaluationconfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocsdeploymentgateruleevaluationconfiguration"></a>

```json
{
  "allowed_resources": [
    "string"
  ],
  "duration": 0,
  "excluded_resources": [
    "string"
  ],
  "fail_on_no_data": true,
  "fail_on_no_groups_found": true,
  "monitor_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "query": "string",
  "warmup": 0
}
```

Evaluated rule configuration. Fields depend on rule type and unset fields are omitted.
Monitor rules can include `duration`, `query`, `monitor_ids`, `warmup`, `fail_on_no_groups_found`, and `fail_on_no_data`.
Faulty deployment detection rules can include `duration`, `allowed_resources`, and `excluded_resources`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_resources|[string]|false|none|APM resources explicitly allowed by faulty deployment detection.|
|duration|integer(int64)|false|none|Evaluation duration configured for this rule.|
|excluded_resources|[string]|false|none|APM resources excluded from faulty deployment detection.|
|fail_on_no_data|boolean|false|none|Whether a monitor rule fails when no data is found.|
|fail_on_no_groups_found|boolean|false|none|Whether a monitor rule fails when no groups are found.|
|monitor_ids|[string]|false|none|Monitor IDs evaluated by a monitor rule.|
|query|string|false|none|Monitor query used by a monitor rule.|
|warmup|integer(int64)|false|none|Warm-up duration in seconds for a monitor rule. Omitted when zero.|

Inline rule definitions for a deployment gate evaluation. When provided, rules are evaluated

Downtiming gives you greater control over monitor notifications by
allowing you to globally exclude scopes from alerting.
Downtime settings, which can be scheduled with start and end times,
prevent all alerting related to specified Datadog tags.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[DowntimeResponseData](#schemadowntimeresponsedata)|false|none|Downtime data.|
|included|[[DowntimeResponseIncludedItem](#schemadowntimeresponseincludeditem)]|false|none|Array of objects related to the downtime that the user requested.|

Downtime details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|canceled|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Time that the downtime was canceled.|
|created|string(date-time)|false|none|Creation time of the downtime.|
|display_timezone|[DowntimeDisplayTimezone](#schemadowntimedisplaytimezone)|false|none|The timezone in which to display the downtime's start and end times in Datadog applications. This is not used<br>as an offset for scheduling.|
|message|[DowntimeMessage](#schemadowntimemessage)|false|none|A message to include with notifications for this downtime. Email notifications can be sent to specific users<br>by using the same `@username` notation as events.|
|modified|string(date-time)|false|none|Time that the downtime was last modified.|
|monitor_identifier|[DowntimeMonitorIdentifier](#schemadowntimemonitoridentifier)|false|none|Monitor identifier for the downtime.|
|mute_first_recovery_notification|[DowntimeMuteFirstRecoveryNotification](#schemadowntimemutefirstrecoverynotification)|false|none|If the first recovery notification during a downtime should be muted.|
|notify_end_states|[DowntimeNotifyEndStates](#schemadowntimenotifyendstates)|false|none|States that will trigger a monitor notification when the `notify_end_types` action occurs.|
|notify_end_types|[DowntimeNotifyEndTypes](#schemadowntimenotifyendtypes)|false|none|Actions that will trigger a monitor notification if the downtime is in the `notify_end_types` state.|
|run_as|[DowntimeRunAs](#schemadowntimerunas)|false|read-only|The principals (users, roles, or teams) allowed to act on behalf of the downtime.<br><br>**Note**: This feature is currently in Preview and may not be available for all organizations.|
|schedule|[DowntimeScheduleResponse](#schemadowntimescheduleresponse)|false|none|The schedule that defines when the monitor starts, stops, and recurs. There are two types of schedules:<br>one-time and recurring. Recurring schedules may have up to five RRULE-based recurrences. If no schedules are<br>provided, the downtime will begin immediately and never end.|
|scope|[DowntimeScope](#schemadowntimescope)|false|none|The scope to which the downtime applies. Must follow the [common search syntax](https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/explorer/search_syntax/).|
|status|[DowntimeStatus](#schemadowntimestatus)|false|none|The current status of the downtime.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|notify_end_states|alert|
|notify_end_states|no data|
|notify_end_states|warn|
|notify_end_types|canceled|
|notify_end_types|expired|
|status|active|
|status|canceled|
|status|ended|
|status|scheduled|

The most recent actual start and end dates for a recurring downtime. For a canceled downtime,
this is the previously occurring downtime. For active downtimes, this is the ongoing downtime, and for scheduled
downtimes it is the upcoming downtime.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|end|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The end of the current downtime.|
|start|string(date-time)|false|none|The start of the current downtime.|

|rrule|[DowntimeScheduleRecurrenceRrule](#schemadowntimeschedulerecurrencerrule)|true|none|The `RRULE` standard for defining recurring events.<br>For example, to have a recurring event on the first day of each month, set the type to `rrule` and set the `FREQ` to `MONTHLY` and `BYMONTHDAY` to `1`.<br>Most common `rrule` options from the [iCalendar Spec](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545) are supported.<br><br>**Note**: Attributes specifying the duration in `RRULE` are not supported (for example, `DTSTART`, `DTEND`, `DURATION`).<br>More examples available in this [downtime guide](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/guide/suppress-alert-with-downtimes/?tab=api).|
|start|string \| null|false|none|ISO-8601 Datetime to start the downtime. Must not include a UTC offset. If not provided, the<br>downtime starts the moment it is created.|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

|rrule|[DowntimeScheduleRecurrenceRrule](#schemadowntimeschedulerecurrencerrule)|false|none|The `RRULE` standard for defining recurring events.<br>For example, to have a recurring event on the first day of each month, set the type to `rrule` and set the `FREQ` to `MONTHLY` and `BYMONTHDAY` to `1`.<br>Most common `rrule` options from the [iCalendar Spec](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545) are supported.<br><br>**Note**: Attributes specifying the duration in `RRULE` are not supported (for example, `DTSTART`, `DTEND`, `DURATION`).<br>More examples available in this [downtime guide](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/guide/suppress-alert-with-downtimes/?tab=api).|

<h2 id="tocS_DowntimeScheduleRecurrenceRrule">DowntimeScheduleRecurrenceRrule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadowntimeschedulerecurrencerrule"></a>
<a id="schema_DowntimeScheduleRecurrenceRrule"></a>
<a id="tocSdowntimeschedulerecurrencerrule"></a>
<a id="tocsdowntimeschedulerecurrencerrule"></a>

```json
"FREQ=MONTHLY;BYSETPOS=3;BYDAY=WE;INTERVAL=1"
```

The `RRULE` standard for defining recurring events.
For example, to have a recurring event on the first day of each month, set the type to `rrule` and set the `FREQ` to `MONTHLY` and `BYMONTHDAY` to `1`.
Most common `rrule` options from the [iCalendar Spec](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545) are supported.

**Note**: Attributes specifying the duration in `RRULE` are not supported (for example, `DTSTART`, `DTEND`, `DURATION`).
More examples available in this [downtime guide](https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/guide/suppress-alert-with-downtimes/?tab=api).

<a id="schemadowntimeschedulerecurrencesresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_DowntimeScheduleRecurrencesResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSdowntimeschedulerecurrencesresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsdowntimeschedulerecurrencesresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "current_downtime": {
    "end": "2020-01-02 03:04:00+00:00",
    "start": "2020-01-02 03:04:00+00:00"
  },
  "recurrences": [
    {
      "duration": "123d",
      "rrule": "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYSETPOS=3;BYDAY=WE;INTERVAL=1",
      "start": "2020-01-02T03:04"
    }
  ],
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

A recurring downtime schedule definition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|current_downtime|[DowntimeScheduleCurrentDowntimeResponse](#schemadowntimeschedulecurrentdowntimeresponse)|false|none|The most recent actual start and end dates for a recurring downtime. For a canceled downtime,<br>this is the previously occurring downtime. For active downtimes, this is the ongoing downtime, and for scheduled<br>downtimes it is the upcoming downtime.|
|recurrences|[[DowntimeScheduleRecurrenceResponse](#schemadowntimeschedulerecurrenceresponse)]|true|none|A list of downtime recurrences.|
|timezone|string|false|none|The timezone in which to schedule the downtime. This affects recurring start and end dates.<br>Must match `display_timezone`.|

<h2 id="tocS_DowntimeScheduleResponse">DowntimeScheduleResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadowntimescheduleresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_DowntimeScheduleResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSdowntimescheduleresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsdowntimescheduleresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "current_downtime": {
    "end": "2020-01-02 03:04:00+00:00",
    "start": "2020-01-02 03:04:00+00:00"
  },
  "recurrences": [
    {
      "duration": "123d",
      "rrule": "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYSETPOS=3;BYDAY=WE;INTERVAL=1",
      "start": "2020-01-02T03:04"
    }
  ],
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

The schedule that defines when the monitor starts, stops, and recurs. There are two types of schedules:
one-time and recurring. Recurring schedules may have up to five RRULE-based recurrences. If no schedules are
provided, the downtime will begin immediately and never end.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[DowntimeScheduleRecurrencesResponse](#schemadowntimeschedulerecurrencesresponse)|false|none|A recurring downtime schedule definition.|
|*oneOf*|[DowntimeScheduleOneTimeResponse](#schemadowntimescheduleonetimeresponse)|false|none|A one-time downtime definition.|

```json
{
```

```json
  },

    "expired"
  ],
  "schedule": {
    "recurrences": [
      {
        "duration": "123d",
        "rrule": "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYSETPOS=3;BYDAY=WE;INTERVAL=1",
        "start": "2020-01-02T03:04",
        "property1": null,

      }
    ],

  },
```


Attributes of the downtime to update.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|display_timezone|[DowntimeDisplayTimezone](#schemadowntimedisplaytimezone)|false|none|The timezone in which to display the downtime's start and end times in Datadog applications. This is not used<br>as an offset for scheduling.|
|message|[DowntimeMessage](#schemadowntimemessage)|false|none|A message to include with notifications for this downtime. Email notifications can be sent to specific users<br>by using the same `@username` notation as events.|
|monitor_identifier|[DowntimeMonitorIdentifier](#schemadowntimemonitoridentifier)|false|none|Monitor identifier for the downtime.|
|mute_first_recovery_notification|[DowntimeMuteFirstRecoveryNotification](#schemadowntimemutefirstrecoverynotification)|false|none|If the first recovery notification during a downtime should be muted.|
|notify_end_states|[DowntimeNotifyEndStates](#schemadowntimenotifyendstates)|false|none|States that will trigger a monitor notification when the `notify_end_types` action occurs.|
|notify_end_types|[DowntimeNotifyEndTypes](#schemadowntimenotifyendtypes)|false|none|Actions that will trigger a monitor notification if the downtime is in the `notify_end_types` state.|
|schedule|[DowntimeScheduleUpdateRequest](#schemadowntimescheduleupdaterequest)|false|none|Schedule for the downtime.|
|scope|[DowntimeScope](#schemadowntimescope)|false|none|The scope to which the downtime applies. Must follow the [common search syntax](https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/explorer/search_syntax/).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|notify_end_states|alert|
|notify_end_states|no data|
|notify_end_states|warn|
|notify_end_types|canceled|
|notify_end_types|expired|

|dataflows|[ElasticCloudIntegrationDataflowsRequest](#schemaelasticcloudintegrationdataflowsrequest)|false|none|Data Datadog collects from Elastic Cloud, keyed by dataflow id. Node-level cluster statistics are always collected; each dataflow here adds a further set of metrics on top of that baseline, so set `enabled` to start or stop it. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Every dataflow queries the deployment as the user in `authentication`, so that user's role must hold the required Elasticsearch privileges; a dataflow enabled without them is stored but collects no data.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the Elastic Cloud integration account.|
|settings|[ElasticCloudIntegrationAccountSettingsRequest](#schemaelasticcloudintegrationaccountsettingsrequest)|true|none|Settings for creating the Elastic Cloud integration account.|

Writable attributes used to update an Elastic Cloud integration account. Every field is optional; only the fields provided are changed. When `dataflows` is provided, only the dataflow ids included in the request are modified; dataflows omitted from the map keep their current configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authentication|[ElasticCloudIntegrationAccountAuthenticationUpdate](#schemaelasticcloudintegrationaccountauthenticationupdate)|false|none|Authentication for updating the Elastic Cloud integration account. Exactly one method is set.|
|dataflows|[ElasticCloudIntegrationDataflowsRequest](#schemaelasticcloudintegrationdataflowsrequest)|false|none|Data Datadog collects from Elastic Cloud, keyed by dataflow id. Node-level cluster statistics are always collected; each dataflow here adds a further set of metrics on top of that baseline, so set `enabled` to start or stop it. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Every dataflow queries the deployment as the user in `authentication`, so that user's role must hold the required Elasticsearch privileges; a dataflow enabled without them is stored but collects no data.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable name of the Elastic Cloud integration account.|
|settings|[ElasticCloudIntegrationAccountSettingsUpdate](#schemaelasticcloudintegrationaccountsettingsupdate)|false|none|Settings for updating the Elastic Cloud integration account. Only the fields provided are changed.|

<h2 id="tocS_ElasticCloudIntegrationDataflowsRequest">ElasticCloudIntegrationDataflowsRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaelasticcloudintegrationdataflowsrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ElasticCloudIntegrationDataflowsRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSelasticcloudintegrationdataflowsrequest"></a>
<a id="tocselasticcloudintegrationdataflowsrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "elastic-cloud-detailed-index-stats": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "elastic-cloud-index-stats": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "elastic-cloud-pending-task-stats": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "elastic-cloud-primary-shard-graceful-timeout": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "elastic-cloud-primary-shard-stats": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "elastic-cloud-shard-allocation-stats": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "elastic-cloud-slm-stats": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

Data Datadog collects from Elastic Cloud, keyed by dataflow id. Node-level cluster statistics are always collected; each dataflow here adds a further set of metrics on top of that baseline, so set `enabled` to start or stop it. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Every dataflow queries the deployment as the user in `authentication`, so that user's role must hold the required Elasticsearch privileges; a dataflow enabled without them is stored but collects no data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|elastic-cloud-detailed-index-stats|[ElasticCloudDetailedIndexStatsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticclouddetailedindexstatsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Primary shard metrics broken down per index, rather than aggregated across the cluster.|
|elastic-cloud-index-stats|[ElasticCloudIndexStatsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticcloudindexstatsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Metrics for individual indices. Only the indices granted to the role of the user in `authentication` are collected.|
|elastic-cloud-pending-task-stats|[ElasticCloudPendingTaskStatsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticcloudpendingtaskstatsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Metrics for cluster-level changes that have been submitted but not yet executed.|
|elastic-cloud-primary-shard-graceful-timeout|[ElasticCloudPrimaryShardGracefulTimeoutIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticcloudprimaryshardgracefultimeoutintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Tolerance for slow primary shard requests. Primary shard metrics can grow large enough for the request to time out; enabling this keeps the rest of the collection running when that happens instead of failing the run. Only has an effect alongside `elastic-cloud-primary-shard-stats`.|
|elastic-cloud-primary-shard-stats|[ElasticCloudPrimaryShardStatsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticcloudprimaryshardstatsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Metrics covering only the cluster's primary shards.|
|elastic-cloud-shard-allocation-stats|[ElasticCloudShardAllocationStatsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticcloudshardallocationstatsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Metrics for how many shards are allocated to each data node, and the disk space they use.|
|elastic-cloud-slm-stats|[ElasticCloudSlmStatsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemaelasticcloudslmstatsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Metrics about the actions taken by snapshot lifecycle management. Requires the `read_slm` Elasticsearch cluster privilege on the role of the user in `authentication`; without it this dataflow collects no data.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregation_key|string|false|none|Aggregation key of the event.|

|device_name|string|false|none|A device name.|
|duration|integer(int64)|false|none|The duration between the triggering of the event and its recovery in nanoseconds.|
|event_object|string|false|none|The event title.|
|evt|[Event](#schemaevent)|false|none|The metadata associated with a request.|
|hostname|string|false|none|Host name to associate with the event.<br>Any tags associated with the host are also applied to this event.|
|monitor|[MonitorType](#schemamonitortype)|false|none|Attributes from the monitor that triggered the event.|
|monitor_groups|[string]|false|none|List of groups referred to in the event.|
|monitor_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|ID of the monitor that triggered the event. When an event isn't related to a monitor, this field is empty.|
|priority|[EventPriority](#schemaeventpriority)|false|none|The priority of the event alert. Legacy events use `normal` or `low`.<br>Alert events use `1` (highest priority) through `5` (lowest priority).|
|related_event_id|integer(int64)|false|none|Related event ID.|
|service|string|false|none|Service that triggered the event.|
|source_type_name|string|false|none|The type of event being posted.<br>For example, `nagios`, `hudson`, `jenkins`, `my_apps`, `chef`, `puppet`, `git` or `bitbucket`.<br>The list of standard source attribute values is [available here](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/faq/list-of-api-source-attribute-value).|
|sourcecategory|string|false|none|Identifier for the source of the event, such as a monitor alert, an externally-submitted event, or an integration.|
|status|[EventStatusType](#schemaeventstatustype)|false|none|The event status. Legacy events can use `failure`, `error`, `warning`,<br>`info`, `success`, `user_update`, `recommendation`, or `snapshot`.<br>Alert events can use `error`, `warn`, or `ok`.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|A list of tags to apply to the event.|
|timestamp|integer(int64)|false|none|POSIX timestamp of your event in milliseconds.|
|title|string|false|none|The event title.|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ExperimentsCreateExperimentV2RequestDataAttributesTrafficExposureStepsItems">ExperimentsCreateExperimentV2RequestDataAttributesTrafficExposureStepsItems</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaexperimentscreateexperimentv2requestdataattributestrafficexposurestepsitems"></a>
<a id="schema_ExperimentsCreateExperimentV2RequestDataAttributesTrafficExposureStepsItems"></a>
<a id="tocSexperimentscreateexperimentv2requestdataattributestrafficexposurestepsitems"></a>
<a id="tocsexperimentscreateexperimentv2requestdataattributestrafficexposurestepsitems"></a>

```json
{
  "duration_ms": null,
  "fraction": 0
}
```

Configured exposure plan rather than wall-clock history. At least two steps must have strictly increasing fractions and no gaps. Warehouse steps start at assignments_start_date and can use different durations. New Datadog plans have at most five steps and a first fraction above zero. Their nonfinal durations must be equal and exclude time paused. Datadog steps start with the experiment. Running warehouse experiments can replace step fractions, durations, and the exposure mode. After start, Datadog exposure plans cannot change through the public API. The final duration is null and its fraction holds until assignment ends.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|duration_ms|integer(int64) \| null|true|none|Positive step duration in milliseconds. Datadog durations exclude pauses. Send null for the final step.|
|fraction|number(double)|true|none|Fraction of traffic exposed during this step.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|analysis_plan|[ExperimentsPatchProtocolAnalysisPlanInput](#schemaexperimentspatchprotocolanalysisplaninput)|false|none|Partial statistical settings. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Null clears the whole plan. Null clears nullable fields; null or an empty string clears confidence_interval_method.|
|assignment_source_default_properties|[[ExperimentsPublicProtocolResponseDataAttributesAssignmentSourceDefaultPropertiesItems](#schemaexperimentspublicprotocolresponsedataattributesassignmentsourcedefaultpropertiesitems)]|false|none|Assignment properties. Omission or null preserves them; an array replaces them.|
|assignment_source_id|string \| null|false|none|ID of the assignment source selected by the protocol. Omission or null keeps the current value. An empty string clears it.|
|default_duration_days|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Default experiment duration supplied by the protocol, in days. Omission preserves it; null clears it. Sets analysis_plan.target_duration_days on experiments created from this protocol.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Description. Empty string clears it; omission or null preserves it.|
|enforcement|[ExperimentsPatchProtocolEnforcementInput](#schemaexperimentspatchprotocolenforcementinput)|false|none|Partial lock map. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Null clears the whole map. Empty or null field values become `EDITABLE`, except `subject_type`, `flag_source`, and `confidence_interval_method`, which remain `LOCKED`.|
|environment_id|string \| null|false|none|ID of the feature flag environment used by the experiment. Omission or null keeps the current value. An empty string clears it.|
|exposure_schedule|[ExperimentsPatchProtocolExposureScheduleInput](#schemaexperimentspatchprotocolexposurescheduleinput)|false|none|Partial traffic schedule. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Null clears the whole schedule. Null clears nullable fields and rollout_steps; null sets strategy to an empty string and `autostart` to false.|
|is_duration_required_to_start|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the protocol requires a duration before an experiment can start. Omission or null preserves it.|
|is_equal_split_enforced|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the protocol requires equal traffic allocation across variants. Omission or null preserves it.|
|is_metric_limit_enabled|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the protocol limits the number of metrics. Omission or null preserves it.|
|is_minimum_duration_enabled|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the protocol enforces a minimum experiment duration. Omission or null preserves it.|
|metric_groups|[[ExperimentsProtocolMetricGroupInput](#schemaexperimentsprotocolmetricgroupinput)]|false|none|Metric groups. Omission or null preserves them; an array replaces them.|
|metric_limit|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Maximum number of metrics allowed by the protocol. Omission preserves it; null clears it.|
|migration_metadata|object \| null|false|none|Metadata for imported resources. Must encode to at most 4096 bytes. Null clears it; omission preserves it on update.|
|minimum_duration_unit|string \| null|false|none|Minimum duration unit, `DAYS` or `WEEKS`. Empty string clears it. Omission or null preserves it.|
|minimum_duration_value|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Minimum experiment duration in the specified unit. Omission preserves it; null clears it.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Protocol name. Leading and trailing spaces are removed. The trimmed name must contain 1 to 255 characters.|
|primary_metric_id|string \| null|false|none|ID of the primary metric supplied by the protocol. Omission or null keeps the current value. An empty string clears it.|
|subject_type_id|string \| null|false|none|ID of the subject type used by this configuration. Omission or null keeps the current value. An empty string clears it.|
|targeting_rules|[[ExperimentsProtocolTargetingRuleInput](#schemaexperimentsprotocoltargetingruleinput)]|false|none|Targeting rules. Omission or null preserves them; an array replaces them.|

Traffic exposure fraction or schedule configured for the experiment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fraction|number(double)|false|none|STATIC exposure fraction. Draft experiments can change this value. After start only warehouse experiments without a Datadog flag can change a STATIC fraction through the public API.|
|mode|[ExperimentsCreateExperimentV2RequestDataAttributesTrafficExposureMode](#schemaexperimentscreateexperimentv2requestdataattributestrafficexposuremode)|true|none|Whether exposure uses a fixed fraction or a sequence of steps.|
|steps|[[ExperimentsCreateExperimentV2RequestDataAttributesTrafficExposureStepsItems](#schemaexperimentscreateexperimentv2requestdataattributestrafficexposurestepsitems)]|false|none|Configured exposure plan rather than wall-clock history. At least two steps must have strictly increasing fractions and no gaps. Warehouse steps start at assignments_start_date and can use different durations. New Datadog plans have at most five steps and a first fraction above zero. Their nonfinal durations must be equal and exclude time paused. Datadog steps start with the experiment. Running warehouse experiments can replace step fractions, durations, and the exposure mode. After start, Datadog exposure plans cannot change through the public API. The final duration is null and its fraction holds until assignment ends.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|STATIC|
|mode|STEPS|

Partial lock map. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Null clears the whole map. Empty or null field values become `EDITABLE`, except `subject_type`, `flag_source`, and `confidence_interval_method`, which remain `LOCKED`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|confidence_interval_method|string \| null|false|none|Always `LOCKED`. The server keeps this setting locked regardless of the supplied value.|
|confidence_level|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to confidence level. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|cuped_calculation|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to CUPED variance reduction. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|default_duration|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to default duration. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|environment|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to environment. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|flag_source|string \| null|false|none|Always LOCKED. The server keeps this setting locked regardless of the supplied value.|
|multiple_testing_correction|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to multiple testing correction. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|notifications|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to notifications. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|primary_metric|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to primary metric. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|secondary_metrics|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to secondary metrics. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|split_by_exploration_dimensions|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to result exploration dimensions. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|subject_type|string \| null|false|none|Always LOCKED. The server keeps this setting locked regardless of the supplied value.|
|targeting_rules|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to targeting rules. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|traffic_exposure|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to traffic exposure. EDITABLE permits changes.|
|warehouse_exposure_source|string \| null|false|none|LOCKED prevents changes to warehouse exposure source. EDITABLE permits changes.|

|subject_type_id|string(uuid)|true|none|ID of the subject type used by this configuration.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|evsi|number(double)|false|none|Expected reduction in minimum expected regret from collecting more sample data.|
|expectation_above_zero|number(double)|false|none|Expected effect when the effect is positive.|
|expectation_below_zero|number(double)|false|none|Expected effect when the effect is negative.|
|global_lift|number(double)|false|none|Estimated lift across the population. Calculated as metric coverage multiplied by the experiment lift.|
|global_lift_lower_bound|number(double)|false|none|Lower bound of the estimated lift across the population.|
|global_lift_upper_bound|number(double)|false|none|Upper bound of the estimated lift across the population.|
|is_cuped_adjusted|boolean|false|none|Whether CUPED used pre-experiment data to reduce variance in this result.|
|is_unreliable|boolean|false|none|Whether the statistical result is marked as unreliable.|
|lift_type|[ExperimentsVariantResultsV2DTODataAttributesMetricsItemsAnalysesItemsLiftType](#schemaexperimentsvariantresultsv2dtodataattributesmetricsitemsanalysesitemslifttype)|false|none|Whether the reported lift is relative or absolute.|
|method|[ExperimentsVariantResultsV2DTODataAttributesMetricsItemsAnalysesItemsMethod](#schemaexperimentsvariantresultsv2dtodataattributesmetricsitemsanalysesitemsmethod)|false|none|Statistical method used to calculate this result.|
|minimum_expected_regret|number(double)|false|none|The smaller expected opportunity cost of choosing treatment or control.|
|p_value|number(double)|false|none|Probability, under the no-effect hypothesis, of a result at least as extreme as the observed result.|
|point_estimate|number(double)|false|none|Estimated difference between the variant and control for this metric.|
|probability_above_zero|number(double)|false|none|Estimated probability that the effect is greater than zero.|
|probability_below_zero|number(double)|false|none|Estimated probability that the effect is less than zero.|
|standard_error|number(double)|false|none|Estimated uncertainty in the effect estimate.|
|unreliable_reason|[ExperimentsVariantResultsV2DTODataAttributesMetricsItemsAnalysesItemsUnreliableReason](#schemaexperimentsvariantresultsv2dtodataattributesmetricsitemsanalysesitemsunreliablereason)|false|none|Reason that the statistical result is marked as unreliable.|
|variant_metric_value|number(double) \| null|false|none|Metric value calculated for this variant.|
|z_score|number(double)|false|none|Standardized statistic used to compare the observed effect with zero.|

Settings for a metric aggregation that uses a Warehouse measure. The other measure must be omitted or null.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aging_threshold_days|integer(int64)|false|none|Stored aging threshold in days. The subject aging filter uses the aggregation window end and unit.|
|datadog_metric_measure|[ExperimentsNullableDatadogMetricMeasureInput](#schemaexperimentsnullabledatadogmetricmeasureinput)|false|none|Optional Datadog measure. Use null when the other measure is selected.|
|enable_aging_subject_filter|boolean|false|none|Whether to exclude subjects whose observation time is shorter than the aggregation window.|
|operation|string|true|none|Calculation applied to the measure values, such as sum.|
|property_filters|[[ExperimentsWarehouseFilterInputGroup](#schemaexperimentswarehousefilterinputgroup)]|false|none|Property filters that select data for this aggregation.|
|threshold_aggregation_type|string|false|none|Calculation used to evaluate the threshold.|
|threshold_breach_value|number(double)|false|none|Value used to determine whether the threshold is breached.|
|threshold_comparison_operator|string|false|none|Operator used to compare the calculated value with the threshold.|
|threshold_timeframe_dimension|string|false|none|Time unit for the threshold evaluation window. Supports seconds, minutes, hours, days, calendar_days, and<br>weeks. Calendar days start at midnight on the assignment day. Other units start at the assignment time.|
|threshold_timeframe_value|number(double)|false|none|End of the threshold evaluation window, measured from assignment in the configured time unit.|
|timeframe_end_value|number(double)|false|none|End offset of the aggregation window from assignment, in timeframe_unit.|
|timeframe_start_value|number(double)|false|none|Start offset of the aggregation window from assignment, in timeframe_unit.|
|timeframe_unit|string|false|none|Time unit for the aggregation window. Calendar days are measured from midnight on the assignment day.<br>Other units are measured from the assignment time.|
|warehouse_metric_measure|[ExperimentsWarehouseMetricMeasure](#schemaexperimentswarehousemetricmeasure)|true|none|Reference to a measure defined in a warehouse metric SQL model.|
|winsor_lower_fixed_value|number(double)|false|none|Fixed lower bound used to cap extreme measure values.|
|winsor_lower_percentile|number(double)|false|none|Percentile used to determine the lower bound for extreme measure values.|
|winsor_upper_fixed_value|number(double)|false|none|Fixed upper bound used to cap extreme measure values.|
|winsor_upper_percentile|number(double)|false|none|Percentile used to determine the upper bound for extreme measure values.|
|winsorization_strategy|string|false|none|Method used to cap extreme measure values before aggregation.|

|flag|string|false|none|Filter coverage by coverage flag. At most one of `service`, `codeowner`, or `flag` may be provided.|

|service|string|false|none|Filter coverage by service name. At most one of `service`, `codeowner`, or `flag` may be provided.|

|closed_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of when the case was closed.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of when the case was created.|
|creation_source|string|false|none|Source of the case creation.|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the case.|
|due_date|string|false|none|Due date of the case.|
|insights|[[CaseInsightsItems](#schemacaseinsightsitems)]|false|none|Insights of the case.|
|jira_issue|[FindingJiraIssue](#schemafindingjiraissue)|false|none|Jira issue associated with the case.|
|key|string|false|none|Key of the case.|
|linear_issue|[FindingLinearIssue](#schemafindinglinearissue)|false|none|Linear issue associated with the case.|
|modified_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of when the case was last modified.|
|priority|string|false|none|Priority of the case.|
|servicenow_ticket|[FindingServiceNowTicket](#schemafindingservicenowticket)|false|none|ServiceNow ticket associated with the case.|
|status|string|false|none|Status of the case.|
|status_group|string|false|none|Status group of the case.|
|status_name|string|false|none|Status name of the case.|
|title|string|false|none|Title of the case.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the case. For security cases, this is always "SECURITY".|

Attributes of a flaky test.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attempt_to_fix_id|string|false|none|Unique identifier for the attempt to fix this flaky test. Use this ID in the Git commit message in order to trigger the attempt to fix workflow.<br><br>When the workflow is triggered the test is automatically retried by the tracer a certain number of configurable times. When all retries pass, the test is automatically marked as fixed in Flaky Test Management.<br>Test runs are tagged with @test.test_management.attempt_to_fix_passed and @test.test_management.is_attempt_to_fix when the attempt to fix workflow is triggered.|
|codeowners|[string]|false|none|The name of the test's code owners as inferred from the repository configuration.|
|envs|[string]|false|none|List of environments where this test has been flaky.|
|first_flaked_branch|string|false|none|The branch name where the test exhibited flakiness for the first time.|
|first_flaked_sha|string|false|none|The commit SHA where the test exhibited flakiness for the first time.|
|first_flaked_ts|integer(int64)|false|none|Unix timestamp when the test exhibited flakiness for the first time.|
|flaky_category|string \| null|false|none|The category of a flaky test.|
|flaky_state|[FlakyTestAttributesFlakyState](#schemaflakytestattributesflakystate)|false|none|The current state of the flaky test.|
|history|[[FlakyTestHistory](#schemaflakytesthistory)]|false|none|Chronological history of status changes for this flaky test, ordered from most recent to oldest.<br>Includes state transitions like new -> quarantined -> fixed, along with the associated commit SHA when available.|
|impact_level|[FlakyTestImpactLevel](#schemaflakytestimpactlevel)|false|none|The impact level of the flaky test, derived from its impact score.|
|impact_score|number(double) \| null|false|none|A score from 0 to 1 indicating the impact of this flaky test, based on factors such as how often it fails and how many pipelines it affects.|
|last_flaked_branch|string|false|none|The branch name where the test exhibited flakiness for the last time.|
|last_flaked_sha|string|false|none|The commit SHA where the test exhibited flakiness for the last time.|
|last_flaked_ts|integer(int64)|false|none|Unix timestamp when the test exhibited flakiness for the last time.|
|module|string \| null|false|none|The name of the test module. The definition of module changes slightly per language:<br>- In .NET, a test module groups every test that is run under the same unit test project.<br>- In Swift, a test module groups every test that is run for a given bundle.<br>- In JavaScript, the test modules map one-to-one to test sessions.<br>- In Java, a test module groups every test that is run by the same Maven Surefire/Failsafe or Gradle Test task execution.<br>- In Python, a test module groups every test that is run under the same `.py` file as part of a test suite, which is typically managed by a framework like `unittest` or `pytest`.<br>- In Ruby, a test module groups every test that is run within the same test file, which is typically managed by a framework like `RSpec` or `Minitest`.|
|name|string|false|none|The test name. A concise name for a test case. Defined in the test itself.|
|pipeline_stats|[FlakyTestPipelineStats](#schemaflakytestpipelinestats)|false|none|CI pipeline related statistics for the flaky test. This information is only available if test runs are associated with CI pipeline events from CI Visibility.|
|services|[string]|false|none|List of test service names where this test has been flaky.<br><br>A test service is a group of tests associated with a project or repository. It contains all the individual tests for your code, optionally organized into test suites, which are like folders for your tests.|
|suite|string|false|none|The name of the test suite. A group of tests exercising the same unit of code depending on your language and testing framework.|
|test_run_metadata|[FlakyTestRunMetadata](#schemaflakytestrunmetadata)|false|none|Metadata about the latest failed test run of the flaky test.|
|test_stats|[FlakyTestStats](#schemaflakyteststats)|false|none|Test statistics for the flaky test.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|flaky_state|active|
|flaky_state|fixed|
|flaky_state|quarantined|
|flaky_state|disabled|
|impact_level|low|
|impact_level|medium|
|impact_level|high|

Only included<br>when fetching a single deployment by ID. Use the `limit` and `page` query parameters to<br>navigate through pages. Pagination metadata is included in the response `meta.hosts` field.|

<a id="schemafleetdeploymentfileop"></a>
<a id="schema_FleetDeploymentFileOp"></a>
<a id="tocSfleetdeploymentfileop"></a>
<a id="tocsfleetdeploymentfileop"></a>

```json
"merge-patch"
```

Type of file operation to perform on the target configuration file.
- `merge-patch`: Merges the provided patch data with the existing configuration file.
  Creates the file if it doesn't exist.
- `delete`: Removes the specified configuration file from the target hosts.

<h2 id="tocS_FleetDeploymentHost">FleetDeploymentHost</h2>

<a id="tocsfleetdeploymenthost"></a>

```json
{
  "error": "",
  "hostname": "web-server-01.example.com",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "versions": [
    {
      "current_version": "7.51.0",
      "initial_version": "7.51.0",
      "package_name": "datadog-agent",
      "target_version": "7.52.0"
    }
  ]
}
```

A host that is part of a deployment with its current status.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|false|none|Error message if the deployment failed on this host.|
|hostname|string|false|none|The hostname of the agent.|
|status|string|false|none|Current deployment status for this specific host.|
|versions|[[FleetDeploymentHostPackage](#schemafleetdeploymenthostpackage)]|false|none|List of packages and their versions currently installed on this host.|

```json

  "initial_version": "7.51.0",
  "package_name": "datadog-agent",

}
```

Package version information for a host, showing the initial version before deployment,
the target version to deploy, and the current version on the host.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|current_version|string|false|none|The current version of the package on the host.|
|initial_version|string|false|none|The initial version of the package on the host before the deployment started.|
|package_name|string|false|none|The name of the package.|
|target_version|string|false|none|The target version that the deployment is attempting to install.|

<h2 id="tocS_FleetDeploymentOperation">FleetDeploymentOperation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafleetdeploymentoperation"></a>
<a id="schema_FleetDeploymentOperation"></a>
<a id="tocSfleetdeploymentoperation"></a>
<a id="tocsfleetdeploymentoperation"></a>

```json
{
  "file_op": "merge-patch",
  "file_path": "/datadog.yaml",
  "patch": {
    "apm_config": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "log_level": "debug",
    "logs_enabled": true
  }
}
```

A single configuration file operation to perform on the target hosts.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_op|[FleetDeploymentFileOp](#schemafleetdeploymentfileop)|true|none|Type of file operation to perform on the target configuration file.<br>- `merge-patch`: Merges the provided patch data with the existing configuration file.<br>  Creates the file if it doesn't exist.<br>- `delete`: Removes the specified configuration file from the target hosts.|
|file_path|string|true|none|Absolute path to the target configuration file on the host.|
|patch|object|false|none|Patch data in JSON format to apply to the configuration file.<br>When using `merge-patch`, this object is merged with the existing configuration,<br>allowing you to add, update, or override specific fields without replacing the entire file.<br>The structure must match the target configuration file format (for example, YAML structure<br>for Datadog Agent config). Not applicable when using the `delete` operation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|file_op|merge-patch|
|file_op|delete|

```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "author": "alice@datadoghq.com",

    "query": "env:prod AND service:web",
    "schedule_id": "sched-123",
    "started_at": 1699990000,
    "status": "pending",
    "target_versions": [
      "7.52.0"
    ],
    "total_hosts": 42,
    "update_type": "update_config_operations"
  },
  "id": "k7Q-3mX-p9Z",
  "type": "deployment"
}
```

<h2 id="tocS_FleetDeploymentV2Attributes">FleetDeploymentV2Attributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafleetdeploymentv2attributes"></a>
<a id="schema_FleetDeploymentV2Attributes"></a>
<a id="tocSfleetdeploymentv2attributes"></a>
<a id="tocsfleetdeploymentv2attributes"></a>

```json
{
  "author": "alice@datadoghq.com",
  "config_operations": [
    {
      "file_op": "merge-patch",
      "file_path": "/datadog.yaml",
      "patch": {
        "apm_config": {
          "enabled": true
        },
        "log_level": "debug",
        "logs_enabled": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "duration_seconds": 1000,
  "error_summary": "A host failed to update",
  "estimated_finished_at": 1699999999,
  "finished_at": 0,
  "is_scheduled": true,
  "query": "env:prod AND service:web",
  "schedule_id": "sched-123",
  "started_at": 1699990000,
  "status": "pending",
  "target_versions": [
    "7.52.0"
  ],
  "total_hosts": 42,
  "update_type": "update_config_operations"
}
```

Attributes of a deployment in the v2 API response.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|author|string|false|none|Handle of the user who triggered the deployment.|
|config_operations|[[FleetDeploymentOperation](#schemafleetdeploymentoperation)]|false|none|Ordered list of configuration file operations applied by this deployment.<br>Absent for package deployments, which have no configuration file operations.|
|duration_seconds|integer(int64)|false|none|Duration of the deployment in seconds, computed as `finished_at - started_at`.<br>Zero if the deployment has not finished.|
|error_summary|string|false|none|Top-level error message for the deployment. Populated only when the deployment has failed.|
|estimated_finished_at|integer(int64)|false|none|Estimated completion time of the deployment as a Unix timestamp. Zero if not available.|
|finished_at|integer(int64)|false|none|Time the deployment finished as a Unix timestamp. Zero if not yet finished.|
|is_scheduled|boolean|false|none|Whether this deployment was triggered by a schedule (`schedule_id` is non-empty).|
|query|string|false|none|Query used to filter and select target hosts for the deployment.|
|schedule_id|string|false|none|Identifier of the schedule that triggered this deployment. Empty if triggered manually.|
|started_at|integer(int64)|false|none|Time the deployment started as a Unix timestamp. Zero if not yet started.|
|status|string|false|none|Current high-level status of the deployment (for example, "pending", "running",<br>"completed", "failed").|
|target_versions|[string]|false|none|Package versions targeted by this deployment.|
|total_hosts|integer(int64)|false|none|Total number of hosts targeted by this deployment.|
|update_type|string|false|none|Type of update operation performed by this deployment<br>(for example, "update_config_operations", "update_package").|

|is_cspm_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog will activate the Cloud Security Monitoring product for this service account. Note: This requires resource_collection_enabled to be set to true.|
|is_global_location_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog collects metrics where location is explicitly stated as "global" or where location information cannot be deduced from GCP labels.|
|is_org_folder_resource_collection_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog scans for organization and folder-level resources<br>under the organization the service account belongs to.|
|is_per_project_quota_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog applies the `X-Goog-User-Project` header, attributing Google Cloud billing and quota usage to the project being monitored rather than the default service account project.|
|is_resource_change_collection_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog scans for all resource change data in your Google Cloud environment.|
|is_security_command_center_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog will attempt to collect Security Command Center Findings. Note: This requires additional permissions on the service account.|
|metric_namespace_configs|[[GCPMetricNamespaceConfig](#schemagcpmetricnamespaceconfig)]|false|none|Configurations for GCP metric namespaces.|
|monitored_resource_configs|[[GCPMonitoredResourceConfig](#schemagcpmonitoredresourceconfig)]|false|none|Configurations for GCP monitored resources.|
|region_filter_configs|[string]|false|none|Configurations for GCP location filtering, such as region, multi-region, or zone. Only monitored resources that match the specified regions are imported into Datadog. By default, Datadog collects from all locations.|
|resource_collection_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Datadog scans for all project-level resources in your GCP environment.|

The `sub` claim is required; all other claims are optional. A token matches only when

<a id="tocsgithubwebhooktrigger"></a>

```json
{
  "rateLimit": {
    "count": 0,
    "interval": "string"
  }
}
```

Trigger a workflow from a GitHub webhook. To trigger a workflow from GitHub, you must set a `webhookSecret`. In your GitHub Webhook Settings, set the Payload URL to "base_url"/api/v2/workflows/"workflow_id"/webhook?orgId="org_id", select application/json for the content type, and be highly recommend enabling SSL verification for security. The workflow must be published.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rateLimit|[TriggerRateLimit](#schematriggerratelimit)|false|none|Defines a rate limit for a trigger.|

```json
    "reducer": "sum"
  }
}
```

The attributes of a governance insight. Exactly one of `metric_query`, `event_query`,
`usage_query`, `audit_query`, or `percentage_query` is populated, depending on the data
source the insight is computed from; the rest are `null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_query|[GovernanceInsightAuditQuery](#schemagovernanceinsightauditquery)|false|none|An audit log query used to compute an insight value.|
|description|string|true|none|A human-readable description of what the insight measures.|
|display_name|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the insight.|
|event_query|[GovernanceInsightEventQuery](#schemagovernanceinsighteventquery)|false|none|An event query used to compute an insight value.|
|metric_query|[GovernanceInsightMetricQuery](#schemagovernanceinsightmetricquery)|false|none|A metric query used to compute an insight value.|
|percentage_query|[GovernanceInsightPercentageQuery](#schemagovernanceinsightpercentagequery)|false|none|A percentage query that computes an insight value as a ratio of two metric queries.|
|product|string|true|none|The product the insight belongs to.|
|query_config|[GovernanceInsightQueryConfig](#schemagovernanceinsightqueryconfig)|false|none|Query execution context for running insight queries directly.|
|sub_product|string|true|none|The sub-product the insight belongs to, if any.|
|time_range|string|true|none|The time range the insight value is computed over, if applicable.|
|unit_name|string|true|none|The unit that the insight's value is measured in.|
|usage_query|[GovernanceInsightUsageQuery](#schemagovernanceinsightusagequery)|false|none|A usage query used to compute an insight value.|

<h2 id="tocS_HamrOrgConnectionStatus">HamrOrgConnectionStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahamrorgconnectionstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_HamrOrgConnectionStatus"></a>
<a id="tocShamrorgconnectionstatus"></a>
<a id="tocshamrorgconnectionstatus"></a>

```json
4
```

Status of the HAMR connection:
- 0: UNSPECIFIED - Connection status not specified
- 1: ONBOARDING - Initial setup of HAMR connection
- 2: PASSIVE - Secondary organization in passive standby mode
- 3: FAILOVER - Liminal status between PASSIVE and ACTIVE
- 4: ACTIVE - Organization is an active failover
- 5: RECOVERY - Recovery operation in progress

Query for selecting logs analyzed by the historical job.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additionalFilters|string|false|none|Additional filters appended to the query at evaluation time.|
|aggregation|[SecurityMonitoringRuleQueryAggregation](#schemasecuritymonitoringrulequeryaggregation)|false|none|The aggregation type.|
|correlatedByFields|[string]|false|none|Fields used to correlate results across queries in sequence detection rules.|
|correlatedQueryIndex|integer(int64)|false|none|Zero-based index of the query to correlate with in sequence detection rules. Up to 10 queries are supported, so valid values are 0 to 9.|
|customQueryExtension|string|false|none|Custom query extension used to refine the base query.|
|dataSource|[SecurityMonitoringStandardDataSource](#schemasecuritymonitoringstandarddatasource)|false|none|Source of events, either logs, audit trail, security signals, or Datadog events. `app_sec_spans` is deprecated in favor of `spans`.|
|datasetIds|[string]|false|none|IDs of reference datasets used by this query.|
|distinctFields|[string]|false|none|Field for which the cardinality is measured. Sent as an array.|
|groupByFields|[string]|false|none|Fields to group by.|
|hasOptionalGroupByFields|boolean|false|none|When false, events without a group-by value are ignored by the query. When true, events with missing group-by fields are processed with `N/A`, replacing the missing values.|
|index|string|false|none|Index used to load the data for this query.|
|indexes|[string]|false|none|Indexes used to load the data for this query. Mutually exclusive with `index`.|
|metrics|[string]|false|none|Group of target fields to aggregate over when using the sum, max, geo data, or new value aggregations. The sum, max, and geo data aggregations only accept one value in this list, whereas the new value aggregation accepts up to five values.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the query.|
|query|string|false|none|Query to run on logs.|
|queryLanguage|string|false|none|Language used to parse the query string.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|archived|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Timestamp when the incident was archived.|

|created_by_uuid|string \| null|false|none|UUID of the user who created the incident.|
|creation_idempotency_key|string \| null|false|none|A unique key used to ensure idempotent incident creation.|
|customer_impact_end|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when customers were no longer impacted by the incident.|
|customer_impact_scope|string \| null|false|none|A summary of the impact customers experienced during the incident.|
|customer_impact_start|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when customers began to be impacted by the incident.|
|declared|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when the incident was declared.|
|declared_by_uuid|string \| null|false|none|UUID of the user who declared the incident.|
|detected|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when the incident was detected.|
|fields|object|false|none|A condensed view of the user-defined fields attached to incidents.|
|incident_type_uuid|string|false|none|A unique identifier that represents an incident type.|
|is_test|boolean|false|none|A flag indicating whether the incident is a test incident.|
|last_modified_by_uuid|string \| null|false|none|UUID of the user who last modified the incident.|
|modified|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Timestamp when the incident was last modified.|
|non_datadog_creator|[IncidentNonDatadogCreator](#schemaincidentnondatadogcreator)|false|none|Incident's non Datadog creator.|
|notification_handles|[[IncidentNotificationHandle](#schemaincidentnotificationhandle)]|false|none|Notification handles that are notified of the incident during update.|
|public_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The monotonically increasing integer ID for the incident.|
|resolved|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when the incident's state was last changed from active or stable to resolved or completed.|
|severity|[IncidentSeverity](#schemaincidentseverity)|false|none|The incident severity.|
|state|string \| null|false|none|The state of the incident.|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the incident that summarizes what happened.|
|visibility|string \| null|false|none|The incident visibility status.|

|severity|SEV-3|
|severity|SEV-4|
|severity|SEV-5|

The incident's attributes from a response.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|archived|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Timestamp of when the incident was archived.|
|case_id|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The incident case id.|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Timestamp when the incident was created.|
|customer_impact_duration|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Length of the incident's customer impact in seconds.<br>Equals the difference between `customer_impact_start` and `customer_impact_end`.|
|customer_impact_end|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when customers were no longer impacted by the incident.|
|customer_impact_scope|string \| null|false|none|A summary of the impact customers experienced during the incident.|
|customer_impact_start|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when customers began being impacted by the incident.|
|customer_impacted|boolean|false|none|A flag indicating whether the incident caused customer impact.|
|declared|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Timestamp when the incident was declared.|
|declared_by|[IncidentNonDatadogCreator](#schemaincidentnondatadogcreator)|false|none|Incident's non Datadog creator.|
|declared_by_uuid|string \| null|false|none|UUID of the user who declared the incident.|
|detected|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when the incident was detected.|
|fields|object|false|none|A condensed view of the user-defined fields attached to incidents.|
|incident_type_uuid|string|false|none|A unique identifier that represents an incident type.|
|is_test|boolean|false|none|A flag indicating whether the incident is a test incident.|
|modified|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Timestamp when the incident was last modified.|
|non_datadog_creator|[IncidentNonDatadogCreator](#schemaincidentnondatadogcreator)|false|none|Incident's non Datadog creator.|
|notification_handles|[[IncidentNotificationHandle](#schemaincidentnotificationhandle)]|false|none|Notification handles that will be notified of the incident during update.|
|public_id|integer(int64)|false|none|The monotonically increasing integer ID for the incident.|
|resolved|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp when the incident's state was last changed from active or stable to resolved or completed.|
|severity|[IncidentSeverity](#schemaincidentseverity)|false|none|The incident severity.|
|state|string \| null|false|none|The state incident.|
|time_to_detect|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The amount of time in seconds to detect the incident.<br>Equals the difference between `customer_impact_start` and `detected`.|
|time_to_internal_response|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The amount of time in seconds to call incident after detection. Equals the difference of `detected` and `created`.|
|time_to_repair|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The amount of time in seconds to resolve customer impact after detecting the issue. Equals the difference between `customer_impact_end` and `detected`.|
|time_to_resolve|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The amount of time in seconds to resolve the incident after it was created. Equals the difference between `created` and `resolved`.|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the incident, which summarizes what happened.|
|visibility|string \| null|false|none|The incident visibility status.|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|severity|UNKNOWN|
|severity|SEV-0|
|severity|SEV-1|
|severity|SEV-2|
|severity|SEV-3|
|severity|SEV-4|
|severity|SEV-5|

|create_message|string|false|none|An optional message shown to users when they declare an incident of this type.|
|editable_timestamps|boolean|false|none|Whether responders can edit incident timestamps for incidents of this type.|
|private_incidents|boolean|false|none|Whether responders can create private incidents of this type. This is an opt-in setting, distinct from `private_incidents_by_default`, which controls whether incidents are created private automatically.|
|private_incidents_by_default|boolean|false|none|Whether incidents of this type are created as private by default.|
|slug_source|[IncidentTypeSlugSource](#schemaincidenttypeslugsource)|false|none|When set to `servicenow`, incidents will display the ServiceNow record ID instead of the public ID. If no ServiceNow integration exists, the public ID will be displayed.|
|test_incidents|boolean|false|none|Whether incidents of this type are treated as test incidents.|

Object containing the information of a sample.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application_id|string|false|none|RUM application identifier of the error.|
|biases|[[IssueSampleBias](#schemaissuesamplebias)]|false|none|Biases the sample satisfies. A single error can satisfy several biases.|
|build_id|string|false|none|Build identifier of the mobile application.|
|bundle_version|string|false|none|Bundle version of the mobile application.|
|data_source|[IssueSampleDataSource](#schemaissuesampledatasource)|false|none|Product that reported the error. The value is `NONE` when the error has no known origin.|
|debug_id|string|false|none|Debug identifier used to resolve the stack trace of the error to source code.|
|debug_info_captured|boolean|false|none|Whether an Exception Replay snapshot was captured for the error.|
|error_source_type|string|false|none|Source type set by the SDK or tracer that reported the error, such as `browser` for RUM browser errors<br>or `Crashtracking` for backend crash reports. Usually not set for APM and logs errors.|
|error_stack|[IssueSampleErrorStack](#schemaissuesampleerrorstack)|true|none|Parsed stack trace of the error. Only the sample picked by the `git_metadata` bias has frames.|
|event|[IssueSampleEvent](#schemaissuesampleevent)|false|none|Raw error event, as stored by its data source. Its fields differ between APM, logs, and RUM.|
|git_commit_sha|string|false|none|Git commit SHA of the service version.|
|git_repository_id|string|false|none|Git repository identifier of the service.|
|git_repository_url|string|false|none|Git repository URL of the service.|
|has_session_replay|boolean|false|none|Whether a RUM session replay is available for the error.|
|language|string|false|none|Programming language of the service.|
|links|[[IssueSampleFrameLink](#schemaissuesampleframelink)]|false|none|Source code locations of the stack frames that resolve to a repository file.|
|os_name|string|false|none|Operating system of the device that reported the error.|
|service|string|false|none|Service name.|
|session_id|string|false|none|RUM session identifier of the error.|
|session_replay_url|string|false|none|URL of the RUM session replay of the error.|
|snapshot_id|string|false|none|Identifier of the Exception Replay snapshot of the error.|
|span_id|string|false|none|APM span identifier of the error.|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the error.|
|trace_id|string|false|none|APM trace identifier of the error.|
|variant|string|false|none|Build variant of the mobile application.|
|version|string|false|none|Version of the service.|
|view_id|string|false|none|RUM view identifier of the error.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|biases|git_metadata|
|biases|trace|
|biases|session_replay|
|biases|exception_replay|
|data_source|APM|
|data_source|LOGS|
|data_source|RUM|
|data_source|LLMOBS|
|data_source|SYNTHETICS|

<h2 id="tocS_IssueSampleBias">IssueSampleBias</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaissuesamplebias"></a>
<a id="schema_IssueSampleBias"></a>
<a id="tocSissuesamplebias"></a>
<a id="tocsissuesamplebias"></a>

```json
"latest"
```

Criterion used to pick a sample. `latest` picks the most recent error. `git_metadata` picks the most
recent error with source code metadata, whose stack trace is parsed. `trace` picks the most recent error
with an APM trace. `session_replay` picks the most recent error with a RUM session replay.
`exception_replay` picks the most recent error with an Exception Replay snapshot.

<h2 id="tocS_LLMObsAnnotationLabelValue">LLMObsAnnotationLabelValue</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemallmobsannotationlabelvalue"></a>
<a id="schema_LLMObsAnnotationLabelValue"></a>
<a id="tocSllmobsannotationlabelvalue"></a>
<a id="tocsllmobsannotationlabelvalue"></a>

```json
{
  "assessment": "pass",
  "label_schema_id": "abc-123",
  "reasoning": "The response was accurate and well-structured.",
  "value": 0
}
```

A single label value entry in an annotation.
The `value` type must match the label schema type:
- `score`: a number within the schema `min`/`max` range (integer if `is_integer` is `true`).
- `categorical`: a string that is one of the schema `values`.
- `boolean`: `true` or `false`.
- `text`: any non-empty string.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assessment|[LLMObsAnnotationAssessment](#schemallmobsannotationassessment)|false|none|Assessment result for a label value.|
|label_schema_id|string|true|none|ID of the label schema this value corresponds to.|
|reasoning|string|false|none|Free text reasoning for this label value.|
|value|[LLMObsAnnotationLabelValueValue](#schemallmobsannotationlabelvaluevalue)|true|none|The value for this label. Must comply with the label schema type constraints.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assessment|pass|
|assessment|fail|

<h2 id="tocS_LLMObsAnnotationLabelValueResponse">LLMObsAnnotationLabelValueResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemallmobsannotationlabelvalueresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_LLMObsAnnotationLabelValueResponse"></a>

<a id="tocsllmobsannotationlabelvalueresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "assessment": "pass",
  "label_schema_id": "abc-123",
  "name_when_saved": "quality",
  "reasoning": "The response was accurate and well-structured.",
  "type": "score",
  "value": 0
}
```

A single label value entry in an annotation response.
In addition to the submitted fields, the server populates `type` and
`name_when_saved` to mirror the schema state at the time the annotation
was created — these help clients display values correctly when the schema
has since changed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assessment|[LLMObsAnnotationAssessment](#schemallmobsannotationassessment)|false|none|Assessment result for a label value.|
|label_schema_id|string|true|none|ID of the label schema this value corresponds to.|
|name_when_saved|string|false|none|Name of the label schema at the time the annotation was created.|
|reasoning|string|false|none|Free text reasoning for this label value.|
|type|[LLMObsLabelSchemaType](#schemallmobslabelschematype)|false|none|Type of a label in an annotation queue label schema.|
|value|[LLMObsAnnotationLabelValueValue](#schemallmobsannotationlabelvaluevalue)|true|none|The value for this label. Must comply with the label schema type constraints.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assessment|pass|
|assessment|fail|
|type|score|
|type|categorical|
|type|boolean|
|type|text|

```json
  "code": "<div class=\"status-card\">Ready for review</div>",
  "content": "## Triage Instructions",
  "height": 240,
  "interactionType": "trace",
  "label": "Triage Instructions",
  "level": "md",
  "tileDef": {
    "requests": [
      {
        "queries": [
          {
            "data_source": "metrics",
            "name": "q",
            "query": "avg:system.cpu.user{*}"
          }
        ],
        "response_format": "timeseries",
        "type": "line"
      }
    ],
    "viz": "timeseries"
  },
  "timeFrame": {
    "end": 1705315800000,
    "start": 1705312200000
  },
  "traceId": "69fcc2bb0000000003113989d83069ba",
  "type": "markdown",
  "url": "https://example.com/image.png"
}
```

A single content block rendered inside a `display_block` interaction.
`type` discriminates which other fields are meaningful:

- `markdown` / `text`: `content` must be a string.
- `header`: `content` must be a string; `level`, when set, must be one of `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`.
- `json`: `content` must be a well-formed JSON value (object, array, or scalar).
- `image`: `url` is required.
- `univiz`: `tileDef` is required (any well-formed JSON; the frontend owns the renderable schema).
- `llmobs_trace`: `traceId` is required; `interactionType`, when set, must be `trace` or `experiment_trace`.
- `frontend`: `code` is required and must be a non-empty string; `label` is optional.

`height`, when set, must be positive.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alt|string|false|none|Alternative text for an `image` block.|
|code|[LLMObsFrontendContentBlockCode](#schemallmobsfrontendcontentblockcode)|false|none|HTML code rendered by a `frontend` block. Required for `frontend` blocks.|
|content|object|false|none|Block payload. A string for `markdown`, `header`, and `text`; an<br>arbitrary JSON value (object, array, or scalar) for `json`. Omitted<br>for `image`, `univiz`, `llmobs_trace`, and `frontend`.|
|height|integer(int64)|false|none|Optional rendered height. Must be positive when set.|
|interactionType|[LLMObsContentBlockLLMObsTraceInteractionType](#schemallmobscontentblockllmobstraceinteractiontype)|false|none|Upstream interaction type referenced by an `llmobs_trace` block.<br>Restricted to `trace` or `experiment_trace`.|
|label|string|false|none|Optional label rendered alongside a `frontend` block.|
|level|[LLMObsContentBlockHeaderLevel](#schemallmobscontentblockheaderlevel)|false|none|Visual size for a `header` block.|
|tileDef|object|false|none|Tile definition for a `univiz` block. Required for `univiz`. The<br>schema is owned by the frontend renderer.|
|timeFrame|[LLMObsContentBlockTimeFrame](#schemallmobscontentblocktimeframe)|false|none|Unix-millis time range used by chart blocks.|
|traceId|string|false|none|Trace identifier. Required for `llmobs_trace` blocks.|
|type|[LLMObsContentBlockType](#schemallmobscontentblocktype)|false|none|Discriminator for a single `display_block` content block. Adding a<br>variant requires coordinated changes in the frontend renderer.|
|url|string|false|none|URL of the image. Required for `image` blocks.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|interactionType|trace|
|interactionType|experiment_trace|
|level|sm|
|level|md|
|level|lg|
|level|xl|
|type|markdown|
|type|header|
|type|text|
|type|json|
|type|image|
|type|univiz|
|type|llmobs_trace|
|type|frontend|

Attributes for creating an Agent Observability prompt and its first version. `prompt_id` and `template` are required; all other attributes are optional. If `config` is omitted, the first version stores an empty object. Configuration authoring must be enabled for your organization to supply `config`. Otherwise, supplying it, including an empty object, returns HTTP 403.

To request access, contact [Datadog Support](https://www.datadoghq.com/support/) or your Customer Success Manager. Customer-owned configuration delivered with a prompt version. Datadog stores and returns the object without interpolating it, validating provider-specific keys, or applying it to model calls. Do not include secrets.|
|description|string|false|none|Optional description of the prompt.|
|env_ids|[string]|false|none|Optional feature-flag environment UUIDs the service attempts to enable and configure to use the first version as their default after creation.|
|labels|[[LLMObsPromptVersionLabel](#schemallmobspromptversionlabel)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Optional labels to attach to the first version. Do not use this attribute for new integrations.|
|prompt_id|string|true|none|Customer-provided identifier for the new prompt.|
|template|[LLMObsPromptTemplate](#schemallmobsprompttemplate)|true|none|A text template, a list of chat messages and named message placeholders, or an authored chat object. Text can include an exact prompt version with `{{>prompt-id version=N}}`; other text, including `{{>...}}` sequences without a version, remains literal. Use an authored chat object when including prompts as chat messages.<br>**Preview**: Prompt composition is available in Preview. To request access, contact [Datadog Support](https://docs.datadoghq.com/help/) or your Customer Success Manager.<br>Without access, inline references remain literal text and structured includes are unsupported. Previously compiled prompt versions remain available for execution.<br>**Preview:** Message placeholders are available in Preview. To request access, contact [Datadog Support](https://www.datadoghq.com/support/) or your Customer Success Manager.|
|title|string|false|none|Optional title of the prompt.|
|user_version|string|false|none|Optional user-supplied version identifier for the first version.|

|labels|production|
|labels|development|

<h2 id="tocS_LLMObsLabelSchema">LLMObsLabelSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemallmobslabelschema"></a>
<a id="schema_LLMObsLabelSchema"></a>
<a id="tocSllmobslabelschema"></a>
<a id="tocsllmobslabelschema"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "Rating of the response quality.",
  "has_assessment": false,
  "has_reasoning": false,
  "id": "abc-123",
  "is_assessment": false,
  "is_integer": false,
  "is_required": true,
  "max": 5,
  "min": 0,
  "name": "quality",
  "type": "score",
  "values": [
    "good",
    "bad",
    "neutral"
  ]
}
```

Schema definition for a single label in an annotation queue.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the label.|
|has_assessment|boolean|false|none|Whether this label includes an assessment field.|
|has_reasoning|boolean|false|none|Whether this label includes a reasoning field.|
|id|string|false|none|Unique identifier of the label schema. Assigned by the server if not provided.|
|is_assessment|boolean|false|none|Whether the boolean label represents an assessment. Requires `has_assessment` to be true.|
|is_integer|boolean|false|none|Whether score values must be integers. Applicable to score-type labels.|
|is_required|boolean|false|none|Whether this label is required for an annotation.|
|max|number(double)|false|none|Maximum value for score-type labels.|
|min|number(double)|false|none|Minimum value for score-type labels.|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the label. Must match the pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` and be unique within the queue.|
|type|[LLMObsLabelSchemaType](#schemallmobslabelschematype)|true|none|Type of a label in an annotation queue label schema.|
|values|[string]|false|none|Allowed values for categorical-type labels. Must contain at least one non-empty, unique value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|score|
|type|categorical|
|type|boolean|
|type|text|

```json
  "evaluation": {
    "property1": null,

  },

  "total_tokens": 192
}
```

A clustered point attached inline to a topic. The metric fields are populated
only when the request includes `include_metrics=true`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|evaluation|object|false|none|Evaluation results for the source span keyed by evaluation name. Included<br>only when metrics are requested.|
|input_tokens|number(double)|false|none|Number of input tokens of the source span. Included only when metrics are requested.|
|output_tokens|number(double)|false|none|Number of output tokens of the source span. Included only when metrics are requested.|
|span_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the source span.|
|status|string|false|none|Status of the source span. Included only when metrics are requested.|
|total_tokens|number(double)|false|none|Total number of tokens of the source span. Included only when metrics are requested.|

```json
{
  "items": [
    0
  ],
  "prompt_id": "response-policy",
  "version": 3
}
```

Includes messages from a specific version of another prompt. Omitting `items` includes every message from that version in its original order. When `items` is present, messages are included in the specified order, including repetitions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|items|[integer(int64)]|false|none|Zero-based indexes of messages from the included prompt. For example, `[2, 0, 0]` includes the third message, followed by the first message twice. Omit this field to include all messages in their original order.|
|prompt_id|string|true|none|Customer-provided identifier of the included prompt.|
|version|integer(int64)|true|none|Positive sequential version number of the included prompt.|

<h2 id="tocS_LLMObsPromptTemplate">LLMObsPromptTemplate</h2>
