A dependency found in the repository, including its identity, location, and `reachability metadata`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exclusions|[string]|false|none|A list of patterns or identifiers that should be excluded from analysis for this dependency.|
|group|string \| null|false|none|The group or organization namespace of the dependency (e.g., Maven group ID).|
|is_dev|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this is a development-only dependency not used in production.|
|is_direct|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates whether this is a direct dependency (as opposed to a transitive one).|
|language|string|false|none|The programming language ecosystem of this dependency (e.g., java, python, javascript).|
|locations|[ScaRequestDataAttributesDependenciesItemsLocations](#schemascarequestdataattributesdependenciesitemslocations)|false|none|The list of source file locations where this dependency is declared.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the dependency package.|
|opaque|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether dependency details are intentionally opaque.|
|package_manager|string|false|none|The package manager responsible for this dependency (e.g., maven, pip, npm).|
|purl|string|false|none|The Package URL (PURL) uniquely identifying this dependency.|
|reachable_symbol_properties|[[ScaRequestDataAttributesDependenciesItemsReachableSymbolPropertiesItems](#schemascarequestdataattributesdependenciesitemsreachablesymbolpropertiesitems)]|false|none|Properties describing symbols from this dependency that are reachable in the application code.|
|requires_transitive_enrichment|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this dependency requires transitive dependency enrichment.|
|target_frameworks|[string]|false|none|The target framework identifiers associated with this dependency.|
|version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the dependency.|
|version_constraint|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the version value represents a version constraint.|
|version_range|string|false|none|The version range associated with this dependency when a manifest declares a range.|

|rotation_start|string(date-time)|true|none|The date/time when the rotation for this layer starts (in ISO 8601).|
|time_zone|string|false|none|The time zone for this layer.|

|name|string|false|none|The security filter name.|
|query|string|false|none|The security filter query. Logs accepted by this query will be accepted by this filter.|

|orgId|integer(int64)|true|none|The ID of the organization that owns the batch migration.|
|resourceStatusCounts|[SecurityMonitoringBatchMigrationResourceStatusCounts](#schemasecuritymonitoringbatchmigrationresourcestatuscounts)|true|none|The number of resources of a batch migration in each status.|
|status|[SecurityMonitoringBatchMigrationStatus](#schemasecuritymonitoringbatchmigrationstatus)|true|none|The status of a batch migration. A batch migration is created as `draft` and moves to<br>`in_progress` when started. It moves to `completed` once no resource is `pending` or<br>`in_progress`, or to `canceled` when canceled.|

<h2 id="tocS_SecurityMonitoringRuleDecreaseCriticalityBasedOnEnv">SecurityMonitoringRuleDecreaseCriticalityBasedOnEnv</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasecuritymonitoringruledecreasecriticalitybasedonenv"></a>
<a id="schema_SecurityMonitoringRuleDecreaseCriticalityBasedOnEnv"></a>
<a id="tocSsecuritymonitoringruledecreasecriticalitybasedonenv"></a>
<a id="tocssecuritymonitoringruledecreasecriticalitybasedonenv"></a>

```json
false
```

If true, signals in non-production environments have a lower severity than what is defined by the rule case, which can reduce signal noise.
The severity is decreased by one level: `CRITICAL` in production becomes `HIGH` in non-production, `HIGH` becomes `MEDIUM` and so on. `INFO` remains `INFO`.
The decrement is applied when the environment tag of the signal starts with `staging`, `test` or `dev`.

and evaluates in real time. For third party detection method, this field is not used.

|hasExtendedTitle|boolean|false|none|Whether the notifications include the triggering group-by values in their title.|
|isEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the rule is enabled.|
|message|string|false|none|Message for generated signals.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the rule.|
|options|[SecurityMonitoringRuleOptions](#schemasecuritymonitoringruleoptions)|false|none|Options.|
|queries|[[SecurityMonitoringRuleQuery](#schemasecuritymonitoringrulequery)]|false|none|Queries for selecting logs which are part of the rule.|
|referenceTables|[[SecurityMonitoringReferenceTable](#schemasecuritymonitoringreferencetable)]|false|none|Reference tables for the rule.|
|schedulingOptions|[SecurityMonitoringSchedulingOptions](#schemasecuritymonitoringschedulingoptions)|false|none|Options for scheduled rules. When this field is present, the rule runs based on the schedule. When absent, it runs real-time on ingested logs.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for generated signals.|
|thirdPartyCases|[[SecurityMonitoringThirdPartyRuleCase](#schemasecuritymonitoringthirdpartyrulecase)]|false|none|Cases for generating signals from third-party rules. Only available for third-party rules.|

```json
{
  "data_exclusion_query": "source:cloudtrail account_id:12345",
  "description": "This rule suppresses low-severity signals in staging environments.",
  "enabled": true,
  "expiration_date": 1703187336000,
  "name": "Custom suppression",
  "rule_query": "type:log_detection source:cloudtrail",
  "start_date": 1703187336000,
  "suppression_query": "env:staging status:low",
  "tags": [
    "technique:T1110-brute-force",
    "source:cloudtrail"
  ],
  "version": 0
}
```

The suppression rule properties to be updated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_exclusion_query|string|false|none|An exclusion query on the input data of the security rules, which could be logs, Agent events, or other types of data based on the security rule. Events matching this query are ignored by any detection rules referenced in the suppression rule.|
|description|string|false|none|A description for the suppression rule.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the suppression rule is enabled.|
|expiration_date|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|A Unix millisecond timestamp giving an expiration date for the suppression rule. After this date, it won't suppress signals anymore. If unset, the expiration date of the suppression rule is left untouched. If set to `null`, the expiration date is removed.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the suppression rule.|
|rule_query|string|false|none|The rule query of the suppression rule, with the same syntax as the search bar for detection rules.|
|start_date|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|A Unix millisecond timestamp giving the start date for the suppression rule. After this date, it starts suppressing signals. If unset, the start date of the suppression rule is left untouched. If set to `null`, the start date is removed.|
|suppression_query|string|false|none|The suppression query of the suppression rule. If a signal matches this query, it is suppressed and not triggered. Same syntax as the queries to search signals in the signal explorer.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|List of tags associated with the suppression rule.|
|version|integer(int32)|false|none|The current version of the suppression. This is optional, but it can help prevent concurrent modifications.|

<h2 id="tocS_Selectors">Selectors</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaselectors"></a>
<a id="schema_Selectors"></a>
<a id="tocSselectors"></a>
<a id="tocsselectors"></a>

```json
{
  "query": "(source:production_service OR env:prod)",
  "rule_types": [
    "misconfiguration",
    "attack_path"
  ],
  "severities": [
    "critical"
  ],
  "trigger_source": "security_findings"
}
```

Selectors are used to filter security issues for which notifications should be generated.
Users can specify rule severities, rule types, a query to filter security issues on tags and attributes, and the trigger source.
Only the trigger_source field is required.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|[NotificationRuleQuery](#schemanotificationrulequery)|false|none|The query is composed of one or several key:value pairs, which can be used to filter security issues on tags and attributes.|
|rule_types|[RuleTypes](#schemaruletypes)|false|none|Security rule types used as filters in security rules.|
|severities|[[RuleSeverity](#schemaruleseverity)]|false|none|The security rules severities to consider.|
|trigger_source|[TriggerSource](#schematriggersource)|true|none|The type of security issues on which the rule applies. Notification rules based on security signals need to use the trigger source "security_signals",<br>while notification rules based on security vulnerabilities need to use the trigger source "security_findings".|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rule_types|application_security|
|rule_types|log_detection|
|rule_types|workload_security|
|rule_types|signal_correlation|
|rule_types|cloud_configuration|
|rule_types|infrastructure_configuration|
|rule_types|application_code_vulnerability|
|rule_types|application_library_vulnerability|
|rule_types|attack_path|
|rule_types|container_image_vulnerability|
|rule_types|identity_risk|
|rule_types|misconfiguration|
|rule_types|api_security|
|rule_types|host_vulnerability|
|rule_types|iac_misconfiguration|
|rule_types|sast_vulnerability|
|rule_types|secret_vulnerability|
|rule_types|workload_activity|
|rule_types|sensitive_data|
|rule_types|serverless_function_code_vulnerability|
|severities|critical|
|severities|high|
|severities|medium|
|severities|low|
|severities|unknown|
|severities|info|
|trigger_source|security_findings|
|trigger_source|security_signals|

<h2 id="tocS_SensitiveDataScannerIncludedKeywordConfiguration">SensitiveDataScannerIncludedKeywordConfiguration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasensitivedatascannerincludedkeywordconfiguration"></a>
<a id="schema_SensitiveDataScannerIncludedKeywordConfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocSsensitivedatascannerincludedkeywordconfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocssensitivedatascannerincludedkeywordconfiguration"></a>

```json
{
  "character_count": 30,
  "keywords": [
    "email",
    "address",
    "login"
  ],
  "use_recommended_keywords": true
}
```

Object defining a set of keywords and a number of characters that help reduce noise.
You can provide a list of keywords you would like to check within a defined proximity of the matching pattern.
If any of the keywords are found within the proximity check, the match is kept.
If none are found, the match is discarded.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|character_count|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of characters behind a match detected by Sensitive Data Scanner to look for the keywords defined.<br>`character_count` should be greater than the maximum length of a keyword defined for a rule.|
|keywords|[string]|true|none|Keyword list that will be checked during scanning in order to validate a match.<br>The number of keywords in the list must be less than or equal to 30.|
|use_recommended_keywords|boolean|false|none|Should the rule use the underlying standard pattern keyword configuration. If set to `true`, the rule must be tied<br>to a standard pattern. If set to `false`, the specified keywords and `character_count` are applied.|

<a id="tocssensitivedatascannerruleattributes"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "excluded_namespaces": [
    "admin.name"
  ],
  "included_keyword_configuration": {
    "character_count": 30,
    "keywords": [
      "email",
      "address",
      "login"
    ],
    "use_recommended_keywords": true
  },
  "is_enabled": true,
  "name": "string",
  "namespaces": [
    "admin"
  ],
  "pattern": "string",
  "priority": 1,
  "suppressions": {
    "ends_with": [
      "@example.com",
      "another.example.com"
    ],
    "exact_match": [
      "admin@example.com",
      "user@example.com"
    ],
    "starts_with": [
      "admin",
      "user"
    ],
    "use_recommended_suppressions": true
  },
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "text_replacement": {
    "number_of_chars": 0,
    "replacement_string": "string",
    "should_save_match": true,
    "type": "none"
  }
}
```

Attributes of the Sensitive Data Scanner rule.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the rule.|
|excluded_namespaces|[string]|false|none|Attributes excluded from the scan. If namespaces is provided, it has to be a sub-path of the namespaces array.|
|included_keyword_configuration|[SensitiveDataScannerIncludedKeywordConfiguration](#schemasensitivedatascannerincludedkeywordconfiguration)|false|none|Object defining a set of keywords and a number of characters that help reduce noise.<br>You can provide a list of keywords you would like to check within a defined proximity of the matching pattern.<br>If any of the keywords are found within the proximity check, the match is kept.<br>If none are found, the match is discarded.|
|is_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the rule is enabled.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the rule.|
|namespaces|[string]|false|none|Attributes included in the scan. If namespaces is empty or missing, all attributes except excluded_namespaces are scanned.<br>If both are missing the whole event is scanned.|
|pattern|string|false|none|Not included if there is a relationship to a standard pattern.|
|priority|integer(int64)|false|none|Integer from 1 (high) to 5 (low) indicating rule issue severity.|
|suppressions|[SensitiveDataScannerSuppressions](#schemasensitivedatascannersuppressions)|false|none|Object describing suppressions for a rule, or the recommended suppression lists published by a standard pattern.<br>There are three types of suppressions, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, and `exact_match`.<br>Rules based on the Datadog library can use recommended or custom suppressions. Custom rules can only use custom suppressions.<br>Suppressed matches are not obfuscated, counted in metrics, or displayed in the Findings page.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|List of tags.|
|text_replacement|[SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacement](#schemasensitivedatascannertextreplacement)|false|none|Object describing how the scanned event will be replaced.|

<h2 id="tocS_SensitiveDataScannerSuppressions">SensitiveDataScannerSuppressions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasensitivedatascannersuppressions"></a>
<a id="schema_SensitiveDataScannerSuppressions"></a>
<a id="tocSsensitivedatascannersuppressions"></a>
<a id="tocssensitivedatascannersuppressions"></a>

```json
{
  "ends_with": [
    "@example.com",
    "another.example.com"
  ],
  "exact_match": [
    "admin@example.com",
    "user@example.com"
  ],
  "starts_with": [
    "admin",
    "user"
  ],
  "use_recommended_suppressions": true
}
```

Object describing suppressions for a rule, or the recommended suppression lists published by a standard pattern.
There are three types of suppressions, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, and `exact_match`.
Rules based on the Datadog library can use recommended or custom suppressions. Custom rules can only use custom suppressions.
Suppressed matches are not obfuscated, counted in metrics, or displayed in the Findings page.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ends_with|[string]|false|none|List of strings to use for suppression of matches ending with these strings.|
|exact_match|[string]|false|none|List of strings to use for suppression of matches exactly matching these strings.|
|starts_with|[string]|false|none|List of strings to use for suppression of matches starting with these strings.|
|use_recommended_suppressions|boolean|false|none|Should the rule use the underlying standard pattern suppression configuration. If set to `true`, the rule must be tied<br>to a standard pattern. If set to `false`, the specified suppressions are applied.|

<h2 id="tocS_SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacement">SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacement</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasensitivedatascannertextreplacement"></a>
<a id="schema_SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacement"></a>
<a id="tocSsensitivedatascannertextreplacement"></a>
<a id="tocssensitivedatascannertextreplacement"></a>

```json
{
  "number_of_chars": 0,
  "replacement_string": "string",
  "should_save_match": true,
  "type": "none"
}
```

Object describing how the scanned event will be replaced.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|number_of_chars|integer(int64)|false|none|Required if type == 'partial_replacement_from_beginning'<br>or 'partial_replacement_from_end'. It must be > 0.|
|replacement_string|string|false|none|Required if type == 'replacement_string'.|
|should_save_match|boolean|false|none|Only valid when type == `replacement_string`. When enabled, matches can be unmasked in logs by users with ‘Data Scanner Unmask’ permission. As a security best practice, avoid masking for highly-sensitive, long-lived data.|
|type|[SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacementType](#schemasensitivedatascannertextreplacementtype)|false|none|Type of the replacement text. None means no replacement.<br>hash means the data will be stubbed. replacement_string means that<br>one can chose a text to replace the data. partial_replacement_from_beginning<br>allows a user to partially replace the data from the beginning, and<br>partial_replacement_from_end on the other hand, allows to replace data from<br>the end.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|none|
|type|hash|
|type|replacement_string|
|type|partial_replacement_from_beginning|
|type|partial_replacement_from_end|

<h2 id="tocS_SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacementType">SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacementType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasensitivedatascannertextreplacementtype"></a>
<a id="schema_SensitiveDataScannerTextReplacementType"></a>
<a id="tocSsensitivedatascannertextreplacementtype"></a>
<a id="tocssensitivedatascannertextreplacementtype"></a>

```json
"none"
```

Type of the replacement text. None means no replacement.
hash means the data will be stubbed. replacement_string means that
one can chose a text to replace the data. partial_replacement_from_beginning
allows a user to partially replace the data from the beginning, and
partial_replacement_from_end on the other hand, allows to replace data from
the end.

<h2 id="tocS_SeverityModifierRuleAction">SeverityModifierRuleAction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaseveritymodifierruleaction"></a>
<a id="schema_SeverityModifierRuleAction"></a>
<a id="tocSseveritymodifierruleaction"></a>
<a id="tocsseveritymodifierruleaction"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "Lower severity for dev environment noise",
  "severity": "low",
  "type": "set"
}
```

The action to take when a severity modifier rule matches a finding. This is a discriminated union on `type`: `set` assigns a fixed severity, while `shift` moves the severity up or down by one rank.

A severity modifier rule's `rule.query` must not filter on `@severity` or on the `@severity_details.user_adjusted.*` namespace.

Use `@severity_details.adjusted.value` instead, which reflects the severity before user-defined adjustments.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[SeverityModifierRuleSetAction](#schemaseveritymodifierrulesetaction)|false|none|Sets matched findings to a fixed severity.|
|*oneOf*|[SeverityModifierRuleShiftAction](#schemaseveritymodifierruleshiftaction)|false|none|Shifts matched findings up or down by one severity rank.|

<h2 id="tocS_SingleAggregatedConnectionResponseDataAttributes">SingleAggregatedConnectionResponseDataAttributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasingleaggregatedconnectionresponsedataattributes"></a>
<a id="schema_SingleAggregatedConnectionResponseDataAttributes"></a>
<a id="tocSsingleaggregatedconnectionresponsedataattributes"></a>
<a id="tocssingleaggregatedconnectionresponsedataattributes"></a>

```json
{
  "bytes_sent_by_client": 0,
  "bytes_sent_by_server": 0,
  "group_bys": {
    "property1": [
      "string"
    ],
    "property2": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "packets_sent_by_client": 0,
  "packets_sent_by_server": 0,
  "rtt_micro_seconds": 0,
  "tcp_closed_connections": 0,
  "tcp_delivered_ce": 0,
  "tcp_established_connections": 0,
  "tcp_probe0_count": 0,
  "tcp_rcv_ooo_pack": 0,
  "tcp_recovery_count": 0,
  "tcp_refusals": 0,
  "tcp_reord_seen": 0,
  "tcp_resets": 0,
  "tcp_retransmits": 0,
  "tcp_rto_count": 0,
  "tcp_timeouts": 0
}
```

Attributes for an aggregated connection.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bytes_sent_by_client|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of bytes sent by the client over the given period.|
|bytes_sent_by_server|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of bytes sent by the server over the given period.|
|group_bys|object|false|none|The key, value pairs for each group by.|
|packets_sent_by_client|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of packets sent by the client over the given period.|
|packets_sent_by_server|integer(int64)|false|none|The total number of packets sent by the server over the given period.|
|rtt_micro_seconds|integer(int64)|false|none|Measured as TCP smoothed round trip time in microseconds (the time between a TCP frame being sent and acknowledged).|
|tcp_closed_connections|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP connections in a closed state. Measured in connections per second from the client.|
|tcp_delivered_ce|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP segments acknowledged with the ECN Congestion Experienced (CE) mark, indicating that an upstream router marked packets as experiencing congestion.|
|tcp_established_connections|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP connections in an established state. Measured in connections per second from the client.|
|tcp_probe0_count|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP zero-window probes sent. These probes are sent when the receiver advertises a zero receive window, indicating it cannot accept more data.|
|tcp_rcv_ooo_pack|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP packets received out of order. This indicates network-level packet reordering, which can degrade TCP performance by triggering spurious retransmissions and reducing throughput.|
|tcp_recovery_count|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP fast recovery events. Fast recovery retransmits lost segments detected through duplicate ACKs or selective acknowledgment (SACK) without waiting for a retransmission timeout.|
|tcp_refusals|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP connections that were refused by the server. Typically this indicates an attempt to connect to an IP/port that is not receiving connections, or a firewall/security misconfiguration.|
|tcp_reord_seen|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of times reordering of sent packets was detected. Reordering detection adjusts the duplicate ACK threshold, preventing spurious retransmissions caused by out-of-order delivery.|
|tcp_resets|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP connections that were reset by the server.|
|tcp_retransmits|integer(int64)|false|none|TCP Retransmits represent detected failures that are retransmitted to ensure delivery. Measured in count of retransmits from the client.|
|tcp_rto_count|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP retransmission timeouts (RTOs). An RTO occurs when an ACK is not received within the estimated round-trip time, forcing the sender to retransmit and halve its congestion window.|
|tcp_timeouts|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of TCP connections that timed out from the perspective of the operating system. This can indicate general connectivity and latency issues.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|do_table_crawler_cron|string|false|none|Cron expression setting how often Datadog crawls your Snowflake table metadata. It takes the five standard fields, with the restriction that the month must be `*` and that the day of the month and the day of the week cannot both be constrained. |sync_snowflake_system_database|boolean|false|none|Whether metadata from the Snowflake `SNOWFLAKE` system database is included in Data Observability alongside your own databases. Defaults to `true`.|

<h2 id="tocS_SnowflakeEventTableLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest">SnowflakeEventTableLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasnowflakeeventtablelogsintegrationdataflowrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "settings": {
    "event_table_events_enabled": true,
    "event_table_logs_enabled": true,
    "event_table_logs_interval_min": 15,
    "event_table_span_events_enabled": false,
    "event_table_spans_enabled": false
  }
}
```

Records from your Snowflake event tables, used to monitor application behavior and identify issues. `enabled` turns the dataflow on and off as a whole, and the per-record-type toggles in `settings` select which kinds of record it collects while it is on. The Snowflake role needs usage granted on the database, the schema, and the event table itself; without those grants this dataflow collects no data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Datadog collects this data. Defaults to `false`; set to `true` to start collection.|
|settings|[SnowflakeEventTableLogsIntegrationDataflowSettingsRequest](#schemasnowflakeeventtablelogsintegrationdataflowsettingsrequest)|false|none|Settings of the event table dataflow. Each record type is collected independently so that you can control ingestion costs, and every record type is ingested into Datadog as logs tagged with its `record_type`. Only the fields provided are changed.|

|event_table_span_events_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether records with a `record_type` of `span_event` are collected. Defaults to `false`.|

Writable attributes used to create a Snowflake integration account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authentication|[SnowflakeIntegrationAccountAuthenticationRequest](#schemasnowflakeintegrationaccountauthenticationrequest)|true|none|Authentication for creating the Snowflake integration account. Exactly one method is set.|
|dataflows|[SnowflakeIntegrationDataflowsRequest](#schemasnowflakeintegrationdataflowsrequest)|false|none|Data Datadog collects from Snowflake, keyed by dataflow id. Each dataflow turns on a distinct kind of collection: set `enabled` to start or stop it, and use `settings` to configure what it collects. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Every dataflow reads from Snowflake as the user in `settings.username`, so that user's role must be granted access to the underlying views; a dataflow enabled without those grants is stored but collects no data.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the Snowflake integration account. Must be<br>unique within your Datadog organization.|
|settings|[SnowflakeIntegrationAccountSettingsRequest](#schemasnowflakeintegrationaccountsettingsrequest)|true|none|Settings for creating the Snowflake integration account.|

```json
      }
```

Writable attributes used to update a Snowflake integration account. Every field is optional; only the fields provided are changed. When `dataflows` is provided, only the dataflow ids included in the request are modified; dataflows omitted from the map keep their current configuration, as do the settings of an included dataflow that provides only `enabled`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authentication|[SnowflakeIntegrationAccountAuthenticationUpdate](#schemasnowflakeintegrationaccountauthenticationupdate)|false|none|Authentication for updating the Snowflake integration account. Exactly one method is set.|
|dataflows|[SnowflakeIntegrationDataflowsRequest](#schemasnowflakeintegrationdataflowsrequest)|false|none|Data Datadog collects from Snowflake, keyed by dataflow id. Each dataflow turns on a distinct kind of collection: set `enabled` to start or stop it, and use `settings` to configure what it collects. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Every dataflow reads from Snowflake as the user in `settings.username`, so that user's role must be granted access to the underlying views; a dataflow enabled without those grants is stored but collects no data.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable name of the Snowflake integration account. Must be<br>unique within your Datadog organization.|
|settings|[SnowflakeIntegrationAccountSettingsUpdate](#schemasnowflakeintegrationaccountsettingsupdate)|false|none|Settings for updating the Snowflake integration account. Only the fields provided are changed.|

Data Datadog collects from Snowflake, keyed by dataflow id. Each dataflow turns on a distinct kind of collection: set `enabled` to start or stop it, and use `settings` to configure what it collects. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Every dataflow reads from Snowflake as the user in `settings.username`, so that user's role must be granted access to the underlying views; a dataflow enabled without those grants is stored but collects no data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|snowflake-account-usage-metrics|[SnowflakeAccountUsageMetricsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakeaccountusagemetricsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Account-level usage metrics read from the Snowflake `ACCOUNT_USAGE` schema, covering storage usage, credit consumption, and query activity.|
|snowflake-cloud-cost-metrics|[SnowflakeCloudCostMetricsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakecloudcostmetricsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Cost data aggregated from the Snowflake `ORGANIZATION_USAGE` schema. [Cloud Cost Management](https://docs.datadoghq.com/cloud_cost_management/) must be enabled for your organization while this dataflow is enabled. Any request that enables this dataflow without Cloud Cost Management is rejected with a `422` response. The Snowflake role also needs the ORGANIZATION_BILLING_VIEWER database role to read the underlying cost views; without that role this dataflow collects no data.|
|snowflake-data-observability-quality-monitoring|[SnowflakeDataObservabilityQualityMonitoringIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakedataobservabilityqualitymonitoringintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Data Observability, which collects lineage and data quality information from your Snowflake databases so you can explore how data flows and detect and resolve quality issues.|
|snowflake-event-table-logs|[SnowflakeEventTableLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakeeventtablelogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Records from your Snowflake event tables, used to monitor application behavior and identify issues. `enabled` turns the dataflow on and off as a whole, and the per-record-type toggles in `settings` select which kinds of record it collects while it is on. The Snowflake role needs usage granted on the database, the schema, and the event table itself; without those grants this dataflow collects no data.|
|snowflake-organization-usage-metrics|[SnowflakeOrganizationUsageMetricsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakeorganizationusagemetricsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Organization-level usage metrics read from the Snowflake `ORGANIZATION_USAGE` schema, covering the credit consumption of every account in the organization and the history of data transferred out of Snowflake. Reading that schema requires the ORGADMIN role; without it this dataflow collects no data.|
|snowflake-query-history-logs|[SnowflakeQueryHistoryLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakequeryhistorylogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Per-query logs that let you identify long-running, poorly performing, and expensive queries.|
|snowflake-security-logs|[SnowflakeSecurityLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflakesecuritylogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Security logs from the Snowflake `ACCOUNT_USAGE` schema, for analyzing the security of your Snowflake account and running threat detection with [Cloud SIEM](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_siem/).|
|snowflake-task-history-logs|[SnowflakeTaskHistoryLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schemasnowflaketaskhistorylogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Execution logs for your scheduled Snowflake tasks, covering start time, end time, status, and any error message.|

```json
{
  "file": "bundle.js",
  "mappings": "AAAA,OAAO,CAAC,GAAG",
  "minifiedLineLengths": [
    50,
    30
  ],
  "names": [
    "console",
    "log"
  ],

    "src/index.js",
    "src/utils.js"
  ],

  ],
  "version": 3
}
```

Attributes of a JavaScript source map file.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file|string|true|none|The name of the minified JavaScript file.|
|mappings|string|true|none|The Base64 VLQ encoded string that maps positions in the minified<br>file to positions in the original source files.|
|minifiedLineLengths|[integer(int64)]|true|none|List of character counts for each line in the minified file.|
|names|[object]|true|none|List of symbol names referenced in the mappings.|
|sourceRoot|string|true|none|The root path prepended to source file paths.|
|sources|[string]|true|none|List of original source file paths.|
|sourcesContent|[string]|true|none|List of original source file contents corresponding to the paths in `sources`.|
|version|integer(int64)|true|none|The version of the source map format (typically 3).|

A sort rule. With `type: alphabetical` (the default), buckets are sorted by facet value
and only `order` is allowed. With `type: measure`, buckets are sorted by a computed value:
set `aggregation`, and set `metric` unless the aggregation is `count`.

|aggregation|[SpansAggregationFunction](#schemaspansaggregationfunction)|false|none|An aggregation function.|
|metric|string|false|none|The metric to sort by (only used for `type=measure`).|
|order|[SpansSortOrder](#schemaspanssortorder)|false|none|The order to use, ascending or descending.|
|type|[SpansAggregateSortType](#schemaspansaggregatesorttype)|false|none|The type of sorting algorithm.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregation|count|
|aggregation|cardinality|
|aggregation|pc75|
|aggregation|pc90|
|aggregation|pc95|
|aggregation|pc98|
|aggregation|pc99|
|aggregation|sum|
|aggregation|min|
|aggregation|max|
|aggregation|avg|
|aggregation|median|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|
|type|alphabetical|
|type|measure|

```json
  "interval": "5m",
  "metric": "@duration",
  "type": "total"
}
```

A compute rule to compute metrics or timeseries.
All computes in a request must have the same `type`, and `timeseries` computes must use the same `interval`.
To get both totals and timeseries, send separate requests.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregation|[SpansAggregationFunction](#schemaspansaggregationfunction)|true|none|An aggregation function.|
|interval|string|false|none|The time buckets' size (only used for type=timeseries)<br>Defaults to a resolution of 150 points.|
|metric|string|false|none|The metric to use.|
|type|[SpansComputeType](#schemaspanscomputetype)|false|none|The type of compute.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregation|count|
|aggregation|cardinality|
|aggregation|pc75|
|aggregation|pc90|
|aggregation|pc95|
|aggregation|pc98|
|aggregation|pc99|
|aggregation|sum|
|aggregation|min|
|aggregation|max|
|aggregation|avg|
|aggregation|median|
|type|timeseries|
|type|total|

<h2 id="tocS_SpansGroupBy">SpansGroupBy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaspansgroupby"></a>
<a id="schema_SpansGroupBy"></a>
<a id="tocSspansgroupby"></a>
<a id="tocsspansgroupby"></a>

```json
{
  "facet": "host",
  "histogram": {
    "interval": 10,
    "max": 100,
    "min": 50
  },
  "limit": 10,
  "missing": "string",
  "sort": {
    "aggregation": "pc90",
    "metric": "@duration",
    "order": "desc",
    "type": "measure"
  },
  "total": false
}
```

A group by rule.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|facet|string|true|none|The name of the facet to use (required).|
|histogram|[SpansGroupByHistogram](#schemaspansgroupbyhistogram)|false|none|Used to perform a histogram computation (only for measure facets).<br>Note: At most 100 buckets are allowed, the number of buckets is (max - min)/interval.|
|limit|integer(int64)|false|none|The maximum buckets to return for this group by.<br>A request can generate at most 10,000 groups. Nested `group_by` entries multiply, so the<br>product of their limits must stay within that bound. For example, two entries with a limit of 100 each<br>produce up to 10,000 groups. With a `timeseries` compute, the number of groups multiplied by<br>the number of time buckets must not exceed 400,000.|
|missing|[SpansGroupByMissing](#schemaspansgroupbymissing)|false|none|The value to use for spans that don't have the facet used to group by.|
|sort|[SpansAggregateSort](#schemaspansaggregatesort)|false|none|A sort rule. With `type: alphabetical` (the default), buckets are sorted by facet value<br>and only `order` is allowed. With `type: measure`, buckets are sorted by a computed value:<br>set `aggregation`, and set `metric` unless the aggregation is `count`.|
|total|[SpansGroupByTotal](#schemaspansgroupbytotal)|false|none|A resulting object to put the given computes in over all the matching records.|

```json
{

      }
```
```json
    }
```
```json
  },
```

```json
  "display": {
    "bounds": {
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0
    }
  },
  "errorHandlers": [
    {
      "fallbackStepName": "",
      "retryStrategy": {
        "kind": "RETRY_STRATEGY_LINEAR",
        "linear": {
          "interval": "",
          "maxRetries": 0
        }
      }
    }
  ],

      "nextStepName": "Step2"
    }

    }
  ],

    "thresholdType": "ANY"
  }
```


A Step is a sub-component of a workflow. Each Step performs an action.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actionId|string|true|none|The unique identifier of an action.|
|completionGate|[CompletionGate](#schemacompletiongate)|false|none|Used to create conditions before running subsequent actions.|
|connectionLabel|string|false|none|The unique identifier of a connection defined in the spec.|
|display|[StepDisplay](#schemastepdisplay)|false|none|The position of a step on the workflow canvas. Omit `display` from every step to use<br>automatic layout, or provide it for every step to preserve a manual layout.|
|errorHandlers|[[ErrorHandler](#schemaerrorhandler)]|false|none|The `Step` `errorHandlers`.|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the step.|
|outboundEdges|[[OutboundEdge](#schemaoutboundedge)]|false|none|A list of subsequent actions to run. This list is empty for a terminal step.|
|parameters|[[Parameter](#schemaparameter)]|false|none|A list of inputs for an action.|
|readinessGate|[ReadinessGate](#schemareadinessgate)|false|none|Used to merge multiple branches into a single branch.|

```json
{
  "children": [],
  "durationSeconds": 0.5,
  "endTime": "2026-05-27T12:00:00.5Z",
  "error": 0,
  "hidden_child_spans_count": 0,
  "meta": {
    "env": "production"
  },
  "metrics": {
    "http.status_code": 200
  },
  "name": "web.request",
  "parentID": 0,
  "resource": "GET /products",
  "service": "web-store",
  "spanID": 9876543210987655000,
  "span_kind": "SERVER",
  "startTime": "2026-05-27T12:00:00Z"
}
```

A node in the pruned trace tree.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|children|[[SummarizedSpan](#schemasummarizedspan)]|true|none|The child spans of this node in the pruned tree.|
|durationSeconds|number(double)|true|none|The duration of the span, in seconds.|
|endTime|string(date-time)|true|none|The end time of the span, in RFC3339 format.|
|error|[APMSpanErrorFlag](#schemaapmspanerrorflag)|true|none|Error flag for a span. `1` when the span is in error, `0` otherwise.|
|hidden_child_spans_count|integer(int32)|true|none|The number of child spans that were pruned from this node when summarizing the trace.|
|meta|object|true|none|String-valued tags attached to the span.|
|metrics|object|true|none|Numeric metrics attached to the span.|
|name|string|true|none|The operation name of the span.|
|parentID|integer(int64)|true|none|The ID of the parent span, or `0` when the span is the trace root.|
|resource|string|true|none|The resource that the span describes.|
|service|string|true|none|The name of the service that emitted the span.|
|spanID|integer(int64)|true|none|The span ID, as an unsigned 64-bit integer.|
|span_kind|string|true|none|The OpenTelemetry span kind, for example `INTERNAL`, `SERVER`, `CLIENT`,<br>`PRODUCER`, or `CONSUMER`.|
|startTime|string(date-time)|true|none|The start time of the span, in RFC3339 format.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|error|0|
|error|1|

<h2 id="tocS_SyntheticsDowntimeWeekdayPosition">SyntheticsDowntimeWeekdayPosition</h2>

<a id="tocssyntheticsdowntimeweekdayposition"></a>

```json
1
```

The position of a weekday within a month for a monthly Synthetics downtime recurrence. `1` through `4` select the first through fourth occurrence of the weekday in the month, and `-1` selects the last occurrence.

```json
[
  1
]
```

Positions of the weekdays within a month for a monthly Synthetics downtime recurrence. Used in combination with `weekdays` to schedule occurrences such as "the first Monday of the month".

Detailed result data for the fast test run. The exact shape of nested fields
(`request`, `response`, `assertions`, etc.) depends on the test subtype.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assertions|[[SyntheticsTestResultAssertionResult](#schemasyntheticstestresultassertionresult)]|false|none|Results of each assertion evaluated during the test.|
|call_type|string|false|none|gRPC call type (for example, `unary`, `healthCheck`, or `reflection`).|
|cert|[SyntheticsTestResultCertificate](#schemasyntheticstestresultcertificate)|false|none|SSL/TLS certificate information returned from an SSL test.|
|duration|number(double)|false|none|Total duration of the test in milliseconds.|
|failure|[SyntheticsTestResultFailure](#schemasyntheticstestresultfailure)|false|none|Details about the failure of a Synthetic test.|
|finished_at|integer(int64)|false|none|Unix timestamp (ms) of when the test finished.|
|id|string|false|none|The result ID. Set to the fast test UUID because no persistent result ID exists for fast tests.|
|is_fast_retry|boolean|false|none|Whether this result is from an automatic fast retry.|
|request|[SyntheticsTestResultRequestInfo](#schemasyntheticstestresultrequestinfo)|false|none|Details of the outgoing request made during the test execution.|
|resolved_ip|string|false|none|IP address resolved for the target host.|
|response|[SyntheticsTestResultResponseInfo](#schemasyntheticstestresultresponseinfo)|false|none|Details of the response received during the test execution.|
|run_type|[SyntheticsTestResultRunType](#schemasyntheticstestresultruntype)|false|none|The type of run for a Synthetic test result.|
|started_at|integer(int64)|false|none|Unix timestamp (ms) of when the test started.|
|status|string|false|none|Status of the test result (`passed` or `failed`).|
|steps|[[SyntheticsTestResultStep](#schemasyntheticstestresultstep)]|false|none|Step results for multistep API tests.|
|timings|object|false|none|Timing breakdown of the test request phases (for example, DNS, TCP, TLS, first byte).|
|traceroute|[[SyntheticsTestResultTracerouteHop](#schemasyntheticstestresulttraceroutehop)]|false|none|Traceroute hop results, present for ICMP and TCP tests.|
|triggered_at|integer(int64)|false|none|Unix timestamp (ms) of when the test was triggered.|
|tunnel|boolean|false|none|Whether the test was run through a Synthetics tunnel.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|run_type|scheduled|
|run_type|fast|
|run_type|ci|
|run_type|triggered|

Object describing the request for a Network Path test.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|destination_service|string|false|none|An optional label displayed for the destination host in the Network Path visualization.|
|e2e_queries|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of packets sent to probe the destination to measure packet loss, latency and jitter.|
|host|string|true|none|Host name to query.|
|max_ttl|integer(int64)|true|none|The maximum time-to-live (max number of hops) used in outgoing probe packets.|
|port|integer(int64)|false|none|For TCP or UDP tests, the port to use when performing the test.<br>If not set on a UDP test, a random port is assigned, which may affect the results.|
|source_service|string|false|none|An optional label displayed for the source host in the Network Path visualization.|
|tcp_method|[SyntheticsNetworkTestRequestTCPMethod](#schemasyntheticsnetworktestrequesttcpmethod)|false|none|For TCP tests, the TCP traceroute strategy.|
|timeout|integer(int64)|false|none|Timeout in seconds.|
|traceroute_queries|integer(int64)|true|none|The number of traceroute path tracings.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|tcp_method|prefer_sack|
|tcp_method|syn|
|tcp_method|sack|

(for example, renotification).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|escalation_message|string|false|none|Message to include in the escalation notification.|
|notification_preset_name|[SyntheticsTestOptionsMonitorOptionsNotificationPresetName](#schemasyntheticstestoptionsmonitoroptionsnotificationpresetname)|false|none|The name of the preset for the notification for the monitor.|
|renotify_interval|integer(int64)|false|none|Time interval before renotifying if the test is still failing<br>(in minutes).|
|renotify_occurrences|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of times to renotify if the test is still failing.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|notification_preset_name|hide_all|

|notification_preset_name|hide_query_and_handles|
|notification_preset_name|show_only_snapshot|

An individual assertion result from a Synthetic test.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actual|object|false|none|Actual value observed during the test. Its type depends on the assertion type.|

|expected|object|false|none|Expected value for the assertion. Its type depends on the assertion type.|
|operator|string|false|none|Operator used for the assertion (for example, `is`, `contains`).|
|property|string|false|none|Property targeted by the assertion, when applicable.|
|target|object|false|none|Target value for the assertion. Its type depends on the assertion type.|
|target_path|string|false|none|JSON path or XPath evaluated for the assertion.|
|target_path_operator|string|false|none|Operator used for the target path assertion.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the assertion (for example, `responseTime`, `statusCode`, `body`).|
|valid|boolean|false|none|Whether the assertion passed.|


A step result from a browser, mobile, or multistep API test.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_failure|boolean|false|none|Whether the test continues when this step fails.|
|api_test|object|false|none|Inner API test definition for browser `runApiTest` steps.|
|assertion_result|[SyntheticsTestResultStepAssertionResult](#schemasyntheticstestresultstepassertionresult)|false|none|Assertion result for a browser or mobile step.|
|assertions|[[SyntheticsTestResultAssertionResult](#schemasyntheticstestresultassertionresult)]|false|none|Assertion results produced by the step.|
|blocked_requests_urls|[string]|false|none|URLs of requests blocked during the step.|
|bounds|[SyntheticsTestResultBounds](#schemasyntheticstestresultbounds)|false|none|Bounding box of an element on the page.|
|browser_errors|[[SyntheticsTestResultBrowserError](#schemasyntheticstestresultbrowsererror)]|false|none|Browser errors captured during the step.|
|bucket_keys|[SyntheticsTestResultBucketKeys](#schemasyntheticstestresultbucketkeys)|false|none|Storage bucket keys for artifacts produced during a step or test.|
|cdn_resources|[[SyntheticsTestResultCdnResource](#schemasyntheticstestresultcdnresource)]|false|none|CDN resources encountered during the step.|
|click_type|string|false|none|Click type performed in a browser step.|
|compressed_json_descriptor|string|false|none|Compressed JSON descriptor for the step (internal format).|
|config|object|false|none|Request configuration executed by this step (API test steps).|
|description|string|false|none|Human-readable description of the step.|
|duration|number(double)|false|none|Duration of the step in milliseconds.|
|element_description|string|false|none|Description of the element interacted with by the step.|
|element_updates|[SyntheticsTestResultStepElementUpdates](#schemasyntheticstestresultstepelementupdates)|false|none|Element locator updates produced during a step.|
|extracted_value|[SyntheticsTestResultVariable](#schemasyntheticstestresultvariable)|false|none|A variable used or extracted during a test.|
|failure|[SyntheticsTestResultFailure](#schemasyntheticstestresultfailure)|false|none|Details about the failure of a Synthetic test.|
|http_results|[[SyntheticsTestResultAssertionResult](#schemasyntheticstestresultassertionresult)]|false|none|HTTP results produced by an MCP step.|
|id|string|false|none|Identifier of the step.|
|is_critical|boolean|false|none|Whether this step is critical for the test outcome.|
|javascript_custom_assertion_code|boolean|false|none|Whether the step uses a custom JavaScript assertion.|
|locate_element_duration|number(double)|false|none|Time taken to locate the element in milliseconds.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the step.|


Metadata specifying where and how to access the reference table's data file.

For cloud storage tables (S3/GCS/Azure):
  - sync_enabled and access_details will always be present
  - error fields (error_message, error_row_count, error_type) are present only when errors occur

For local file tables:
  - error fields (error_message, error_row_count) are present only when errors occur
  - sync_enabled, access_details are never present

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_details|[TableResultV2DataAttributesFileMetadataOneOfAccessDetails](#schematableresultv2dataattributesfilemetadataoneofaccessdetails)|false|none|Cloud storage access configuration. Only present for cloud storage sources (S3, GCS, Azure).|
|error_message|string|false|none|The error message returned from the last operation (sync for cloud storage, upload for local file).|
|error_row_count|integer(int64)|false|none|The number of rows that failed to process.|
|error_type|[TableResultV2DataAttributesFileMetadataCloudStorageErrorType](#schematableresultv2dataattributesfilemetadatacloudstorageerrortype)|false|none|The type of error that occurred during file processing. Only applicable for cloud storage sources.|
|sync_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether this table is synced automatically from cloud storage. Only applicable for cloud storage sources.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|error_type|TABLE_SCHEMA_ERROR|
|error_type|FILE_FORMAT_ERROR|
|error_type|CONFIGURATION_ERROR|
|error_type|QUOTA_EXCEEDED|
|error_type|CONFLICT_ERROR|
|error_type|VALIDATION_ERROR|
|error_type|STATE_ERROR|
|error_type|OPERATION_ERROR|
|error_type|SYSTEM_ERROR|

<h2 id="tocS_TagIndexingRuleDynamicTags">TagIndexingRuleDynamicTags</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematagindexingruledynamictags"></a>
<a id="schema_TagIndexingRuleDynamicTags"></a>
<a id="tocStagindexingruledynamictags"></a>
<a id="tocstagindexingruledynamictags"></a>

```json
{
  "exclude_not_queried_window_seconds": 3600,
  "exclude_not_used_in_assets": false
}
```

Options for dynamic tag indexing applied per metric, such as tags filtered by query usage.

Before a tag key is dropped by this rule, two grace period conditions must be met:

1. The metric must be submitted for at least as long as the selected window.
2. A tag key must have been submitted for at least 15 days.

Any metric or tag key that does not meet these conditions are excluded from this
indexing rule. The `exclude_not_*` fields require `exclude_tags_mode` to be set to `true`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exclude_not_queried_window_seconds|integer(int64)|false|none|Tags that have not been queried within this window are excluded from indexing. Maximum of `7776000` (90 days).|
|exclude_not_used_in_assets|boolean|false|none|Tags not used in any dashboards,  monitors, notebooks, or SLOs are excluded from indexing.|

Attributes of a tag indexing rule exemption.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Timestamp when the exemption was created.|
|created_by_handle|string|false|read-only|Handle of the user who created the exemption.|
|estimated_change_in_volume|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|Estimated change in indexed cardinality or points if the exemption is removed and the matching tag indexing<br>rule applies to the metric. A negative value indicates a reduction in indexed volume, a positive value<br>indicates an increase, and zero indicates no change. A `null` value indicates that the estimate is unavailable.|
|kind|string|false|none|Discriminates between an explicit exemption (`exemption`) and a pre-existing legacy tag configuration acting as an implicit exclusion (`legacy_tag_configuration`).|
|missing_indexed_tags|[string]|false|read-only|Tag keys used to query this metric in monitors, dashboards, notebooks, and SLOs that the matching rule would<br>remove or not include if the exemption is removed.|
|reason|string|false|none|The reason the metric is exempt from tag indexing rules.|
|volume_status|[TagIndexingRuleExemptionVolumeStatus](#schematagindexingruleexemptionvolumestatus)|false|read-only|Indicates whether `estimated_change_in_volume` is available and, if not, why. `ok` indicates a fresh estimate.<br>`unindexed_tags` indicates that the matching rule uses tags that are not indexed for the metric.<br>`unavailable` indicates that the estimate is stale, was not computed, or could not be retrieved.|

|override_previous_rules|boolean|false|none|When true, this rule's tag list overrides tags configured by earlier rules for the same metric. When false (default), tags from all matching rules are combined.|

<h2 id="tocS_TagRuleUpdateAttributes">TagRuleUpdateAttributes</h2>

```json
  "required": true,

  "tag_value_patterns": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Mutable attributes of a tag rule. Each field is optional; omitting a field leaves its
current value unchanged. The `source` of a rule cannot be changed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the rule is currently enforced.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable name for the tag rule.|
|negated|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the rule matches tag values that do NOT match any of the supplied patterns.|
|required|boolean|false|none|When `true`, telemetry without this tag is treated as a violation.|
|rule_type|[TagRuleType](#schematagruletype)|false|none|How the rule is enforced. `blocking` rejects telemetry that violates the rule.<br>`surfacing` only highlights non-compliant telemetry without blocking it.|
|scope|string|false|none|The scope the rule applies within.|
|tag_key|string|false|none|The tag key that the rule governs.|
|tag_value_patterns|[string]|false|none|One or more patterns that valid values for the tag key must match.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rule_type|blocking|
|rule_type|surfacing|

```json
{
  "atomic:results": [
    {
      "data": {
        "attributes": {
          "application_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
          "created_at": "2026-01-15T09:30:00.000Z",
          "created_by": "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee",

          "org_id": 123456,

        },

      }
    }

    {
      "detail": "prefix match_type is not enabled for this org",
      "status": "400",
      "title": "Bad Request"
    }
  ]

```

The response body for the bulk create and remove operation. On success, `atomic:results`
contains one entry per operation. Add results appear before remove results and may not match
request order. Correlate add results by their `type` and `id` rather than by array position.
On failure, no operations were applied and `errors` describes what went wrong.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|atomic:results|[[TeamsOwnershipMappingBatchResult](#schemateamsownershipmappingbatchresult)]|false|none|The result of each operation.<br>Add operations are processed first, then remove operations, so results may not appear<br>in the same order as the request. Present only on success.|
|errors|[[TeamsOwnershipMappingBatchError](#schemateamsownershipmappingbatcherror)]|false|none|The validation or processing errors encountered. Present only when the request could not be completed.|

Attributes for updating Test Optimization service settings.
All non-required fields are optional; only provided fields will be updated.
Setting a field to `null` is a no-op. To reset a setting to inherit from the repository level, use the corresponding `<setting>_inherit` field.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_test_retries_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Auto Test Retries are enabled for this service. Setting to `null` is a no-op; use `auto_test_retries_enabled_inherit` to reset to repository-level inheritance.|
|auto_test_retries_enabled_inherit|boolean|false|none|When `true`, resets the Auto Test Retries setting to inherit from the repository level.|
|code_coverage_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Code Coverage is enabled for this service. Setting to `null` is a no-op; use `code_coverage_enabled_inherit` to reset to repository-level inheritance.|
|code_coverage_enabled_inherit|boolean|false|none|When `true`, resets the Code Coverage setting to inherit from the repository level.|
|early_flake_detection_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Early Flake Detection is enabled for this service. Setting to `null` is a no-op; use `early_flake_detection_enabled_inherit` to reset to repository-level inheritance.|
|early_flake_detection_enabled_inherit|boolean|false|none|When `true`, resets the Early Flake Detection setting to inherit from the repository level.|
|env|string|false|none|The environment name. If omitted, defaults to `none`.|
|failed_test_replay_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Failed Test Replay is enabled for this service. Setting to `null` is a no-op; use `failed_test_replay_enabled_inherit` to reset to repository-level inheritance.|
|failed_test_replay_enabled_inherit|boolean|false|none|When `true`, resets the Failed Test Replay setting to inherit from the repository level.|
|pr_comments_enabled|boolean|false|none|This field is ignored. PR Comments cannot be overridden at the service level.|
|repository_id|string|true|none|The repository identifier.|
|service_name|string|true|none|The service name.|
|test_impact_analysis_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Test Impact Analysis is enabled for this service. Setting to `null` is a no-op; use `test_impact_analysis_enabled_inherit` to reset to repository-level inheritance.|
|test_impact_analysis_enabled_inherit|boolean|false|none|When `true`, resets the Test Impact Analysis setting to inherit from the repository level.|

<h2 id="tocS_TimeAggregation">TimeAggregation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematimeaggregation"></a>
<a id="schema_TimeAggregation"></a>
<a id="tocStimeaggregation"></a>
<a id="tocstimeaggregation"></a>

```json
86400
```

Time aggregation period (in seconds) is used to aggregate the results of the notification rule evaluation.
Results are aggregated over a selected time frame using a rolling window, which updates with each new evaluation.
Notifications are only sent for new issues discovered during the window.
Time aggregation is only available for vulnerability-based notification rules. When omitted or set to 0, no aggregation
is done.

Twilio Event resource logs, which record virtually every action taken in your Twilio account, such as provisioning a phone number, changing account security settings, or deleting a recording. Actions are recorded whether they came from the REST API, a user in the Twilio Console, or Twilio itself. [Cloud SIEM](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_siem/) analyzes and correlates these logs to detect threats in real time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

```json
    },

    },

    },

      "enabled": true
    }

  }
```

Writable attributes used to create a Twilio integration account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authentication|[TwilioIntegrationAccountAuthenticationRequest](#schematwiliointegrationaccountauthenticationrequest)|true|none|Authentication for creating the Twilio integration account. Exactly one method is set.|
|dataflows|[TwilioIntegrationDataflowsRequest](#schematwiliointegrationdataflowsrequest)|false|none|Data Datadog collects from Twilio, keyed by dataflow id. Each dataflow turns on a distinct kind of collection: set `enabled` to start or stop it. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Where a dataflow depends on a Twilio feature being enabled, that prerequisite is noted on the dataflow; a dataflow enabled without it is stored but collects no data.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the Twilio integration account.|
|settings|[TwilioIntegrationAccountSettingsRequest](#schematwiliointegrationaccountsettingsrequest)|true|none|Settings for creating the Twilio integration account.|

Writable attributes used to update a Twilio integration account. Every field is optional; only the fields provided are changed. When `dataflows` is provided, only the dataflow ids included in the request are modified; dataflows omitted from the map keep their current configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authentication|[TwilioIntegrationAccountAuthenticationUpdate](#schematwiliointegrationaccountauthenticationupdate)|false|none|Authentication for updating the Twilio integration account. Exactly one method is set.|
|dataflows|[TwilioIntegrationDataflowsRequest](#schematwiliointegrationdataflowsrequest)|false|none|Data Datadog collects from Twilio, keyed by dataflow id. Each dataflow turns on a distinct kind of collection: set `enabled` to start or stop it. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Where a dataflow depends on a Twilio feature being enabled, that prerequisite is noted on the dataflow; a dataflow enabled without it is stored but collects no data.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable name of the Twilio integration account.|
|settings|[TwilioIntegrationAccountSettingsUpdate](#schematwiliointegrationaccountsettingsupdate)|false|none|Settings for updating the Twilio integration account. Only the fields provided are changed.|

<h2 id="tocS_TwilioIntegrationDataflowsRequest">TwilioIntegrationDataflowsRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematwiliointegrationdataflowsrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TwilioIntegrationDataflowsRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStwiliointegrationdataflowsrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstwiliointegrationdataflowsrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "twilio-alerts-logs": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "twilio-call-summaries-logs": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "twilio-cloud-cost-metrics": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "twilio-events-logs": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "twilio-messages-logs": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

Data Datadog collects from Twilio, keyed by dataflow id. Each dataflow turns on a distinct kind of collection: set `enabled` to start or stop it. Defaults listed on each dataflow apply when the account is created; on update, omitted fields keep their current values. Where a dataflow depends on a Twilio feature being enabled, that prerequisite is noted on the dataflow; a dataflow enabled without it is stored but collects no data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|twilio-alerts-logs|[TwilioAlertsLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schematwilioalertslogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Twilio Alert resource logs, which detail the errors and warnings raised when Twilio makes a webhook request to your server or when your application calls the Twilio REST API. This is the one kind of data the integration collects by default.|
|twilio-call-summaries-logs|[TwilioCallSummariesLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schematwiliocallsummarieslogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Twilio Call Summary resource logs, covering the metadata and performance of the calls made from your Twilio account. Requires Voice Insights Advanced Features to be enabled on the Twilio account; without it this dataflow collects no data.|
|twilio-cloud-cost-metrics|[TwilioCloudCostMetricsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schematwiliocloudcostmetricsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Your Twilio cost data, so that Twilio spend can be broken down and attributed in [Cloud Cost Management](https://docs.datadoghq.com/cloud_cost_management/). Cost data appears in Cloud Cost Management within 24 hours of enabling this dataflow.|
|twilio-events-logs|[TwilioEventsLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schematwilioeventslogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Twilio Event resource logs, which record virtually every action taken in your Twilio account, such as provisioning a phone number, changing account security settings, or deleting a recording. Actions are recorded whether they came from the REST API, a user in the Twilio Console, or Twilio itself. [Cloud SIEM](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_siem/) analyzes and correlates these logs to detect threats in real time.|
|twilio-messages-logs|[TwilioMessagesLogsIntegrationDataflowRequest](#schematwiliomessageslogsintegrationdataflowrequest)|false|none|Twilio Message resource logs for inbound and outbound messages, used to track delivery and troubleshoot message errors. A log is produced when you send a message through the REST API, when Twilio executes a TwiML instruction, and when someone messages one of your Twilio numbers or channel addresses. Message bodies are never collected.|

<h2 id="tocS_UsageQuotaBulkResultAttributes">UsageQuotaBulkResultAttributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemausagequotabulkresultattributes"></a>
<a id="schema_UsageQuotaBulkResultAttributes"></a>
<a id="tocSusagequotabulkresultattributes"></a>
<a id="tocsusagequotabulkresultattributes"></a>

```json
{
  "enforced": true,
  "error": "usage_limit is out of range",
  "org_public_id": "abcdef12345",
  "pending_effective_from": "2026-11",
  "pending_usage_limit": 50000,
  "scope": {
    "user_handle": "jane@example.com"
  },
  "usage_limit": 100000
}
```

Attributes of a usage quota bulk write result. On success, quota fields are present as applicable, and pending fields are present only when a change is scheduled. On failure, only `error` is present and the other fields are omitted.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enforced|boolean|false|none|Whether usage above the limit is actively blocked instead of only tracked or alerted on. Omitted if this item failed to write.|
|error|string|false|none|An error message describing why this item failed to write. Omitted if this item was written successfully.|
|org_public_id|string|false|none|The public ID of the organization that owns the quota. Omitted if this item failed to write.|
|pending_effective_from|string|false|none|The future UTC month when the scheduled limit takes effect, formatted as `YYYY-MM`, starting at 00:00 UTC on its first day. Present only together with `pending_usage_limit` and omitted when no change is scheduled or this item failed to write.|
|pending_usage_limit|number(double)|false|none|The usage limit scheduled for the organization-wide quota in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. A value of `0` is valid. At the start of the effective month, this value becomes `usage_limit` and both pending fields are omitted. Omitted when no change is scheduled or this item failed to write.|
|scope|[UsageQuotaResponseScope](#schemausagequotaresponsescope)|false|none|A namespace-specific key and value identifying what the quota applies to within an organization. The object contains exactly one entry. A value of `"*"` identifies the default quota applied to entities without a specific quota. This field is omitted for an organization-wide quota.|
|usage_limit|number(double)|false|none|The quota limit in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. May be fractional for quotas configured before public writes required whole units. Omitted if this item failed to write.|

<h2 id="tocS_UsageQuotaCreateAttributes">UsageQuotaCreateAttributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemausagequotacreateattributes"></a>
<a id="schema_UsageQuotaCreateAttributes"></a>
<a id="tocSusagequotacreateattributes"></a>
<a id="tocsusagequotacreateattributes"></a>

```json
{
  "enforced": true,
  "pending_usage_limit": 100000,
  "usage_limit": 600000
}
```

Attributes for creating or updating a usage quota by scope. Each item must provide `usage_limit`, `pending_usage_limit`, or both. Providing only `pending_usage_limit` updates an existing organization-wide quota, never creates one, requires `enforced` to be omitted, and fails if the quota does not exist.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enforced|boolean|false|none|Whether to actively block usage above `usage_limit` instead of only tracking or alerting on it. Required when `usage_limit` is provided and must be omitted when only `pending_usage_limit` is provided.|
|pending_usage_limit|integer(int64)|false|none|The non-negative, whole-number limit to schedule for the organization-wide quota in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. It is not checked against current usage. Each write schedules the value for 00:00 UTC on the first day of the next calendar month and replaces any previously scheduled change; the server computes `pending_effective_from`. Omit this field to leave any scheduled change unchanged, including when raising `usage_limit`. Cancel a scheduled change only by deleting the quota's `/pending` sub-resource.|
|scope|[UsageQuotaRequestScope](#schemausagequotarequestscope)|false|none|A namespace-specific key and value identifying what the quota applies to within an organization. The object must contain exactly one entry. Use `"*"` as the value for the default quota applied to entities without a specific quota, or omit the scope for an organization-wide quota. A specific value must identify an existing user handle in the caller's organization when `include_descendants` is false. When `include_descendants` is true, the handle must exist in the caller's organization or in at least one targeted descendant organization; the quota is then applied only to the organizations where that handle exists, and the request fails only if the handle exists in none of them.|
|usage_limit|integer(int64)|false|none|The non-negative, whole-number quota limit to set in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. For an organization-wide quota (scope omitted), the limit must be greater than usage already recorded in the current period. When this field is provided, `enforced` is required.|

At the start of the effective month, this value becomes `usage_limit` and both pending<br>fields are omitted. Omitted when no change is scheduled.|
|scope|[UsageQuotaResponseScope](#schemausagequotaresponsescope)|false|none|A namespace-specific key and value identifying what the quota applies to within an organization. The object contains exactly one entry. A value of `"*"` identifies the default quota applied to entities without a specific quota. This field is omitted for an organization-wide quota.|
|usage_limit|number(double)|true|none|The quota limit in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. May be fractional for quotas configured before public writes required whole units.|

```json
  "usage_limit": 120000
}
```

Attributes to update on a usage quota. At least one of `usage_limit`, `enforced`, or `pending_usage_limit` must be provided. Omitting a property leaves its current value unchanged.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enforced|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to actively block usage above the limit. Omit this field to leave the current enforcement setting unchanged.|
|pending_usage_limit|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The non-negative, whole-number limit to schedule for the organization-wide quota in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. It is not checked against current usage. Each write schedules the value for 00:00 UTC on the first day of the next calendar month and replaces any previously scheduled change; the server computes `pending_effective_from`. Omit this field to leave any scheduled change unchanged, including when raising `usage_limit`; use `DELETE /api/v2/usage/quotas/{quota_namespace}/{id}/pending` to cancel one.|
|usage_limit|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|The new quota limit in the usage units defined by the quota namespace. For an organization-wide quota (empty scope), the limit must be greater than the usage already recorded in the current period. Omit this field to leave the current limit unchanged.|
